articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India needs to be at its best in Tests against New Zealand

New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Elusive peace: On Kashmir terror attack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Restoration of Statehood is essential for peace in Jammu and Kashmir

Three months of lull established by security forces in Jammu and Kashmir was rattled by the back-to-back incidents of violence in the past six days. On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

That said, the decline in terrorist incidents and the silence of the streets should not be mistaken for peace. The current situation demands a political reach-out by the Centre to all the stakeholders of J&K. It has to begin with the much-promised restoration of Statehood , which will give the voters a sense that their mass participation in the 2024 Assembly elections allowed their elected leaders to hold institutions accountable, and they were able to work freely to protect the interests of the region. Though the security agencies need to be focused on Pakistan-backed terrorism, it should not come at the cost of re-inflicting psychological scars within Kashmir, which could turn into a powder keg if left unattended. Healing through both political and security processes has to be complementary rather than conflicting. Allowing the political class of J&K to establish its writ and providing room to security agencies to combat challenges are not contradictory.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: All-too fallible: On India’s vote against moratorium on death penalty
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Death penalty requires a near-infallible criminal justice system

India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.

Only a small group of countries worldwide are executing more people. In India, per Project 39A, the Supreme Court released 38 persons from death row in 2016-2025 after they had spent eight years there on average. Some have endured more than two decades. The punishment requires a measure of infallibility that the criminal justice system cannot supply. The safeguards neither deter convictions in cases with flawed evidence, false testimony, and so on nor remedy unequal access to competent legal representation among those facing the penalty. India should formally suspend executions and commission a review of penalty statutes and the treatment of prisoners on death row. Second, it should spare offences that do not involve intentional killing from the penalty. Research suggests meting out excessively harsh punishments for non-fatal crimes could incentivise offenders to escalate their violence, including to kill potential witnesses. The greater goal should be to abolish the practice in law while improving investigative and prosecutorial practices and access to legal aid.

articles.title: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

Editorial Context: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Clear the path: On SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India should use multilateral fora to advance bilateral cooperation

While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: India, Japan discuss economic security, deeper business, people-to-people ties
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jaishankar flagged the growing “weaponisation” of connectivity, resources, services, supply chains and market shares, saying many of these developments had direct implications for national security

India and Japan on Thursday (November 19, 2026) discussed strengthening economic security and deepening government-to-government, business-to-business and people-to-people linkages as External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held talks with his Japanese counterpart Toshimitsu Motegi.
The meeting, held in Tokyo, was the 19th India-Japan Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue.

In a post on X after the talks, Mr. Jaishankar said, "Glad to hold the 19th Foreign Ministers’ Strategic Dialogue with FM @moteging of Japan. Reviewed the entire gamut of our bilateral cooperation, focusing on strengthening economic security and deepening G2G, B2B and P2P linkages.”
“Our discussions also covered challenges and opportunities in the Indo-Pacific, regional hotspots, global issues, and multilateral cooperation," the Minister added.
Earlier, Mr. Jaishankar joined Mr. Motegi for the unveiling of a logo to mark the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between India and Japan in 2027.

On Thursday (November 19, 2026), Mr. Jaishankar and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh also participated in the fourth India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers' Dialogue, known as the 2+2 meeting, in Tokyo.

Addressing the media after the meeting, Mr. Jaishankar flagged the growing “weaponisation” of connectivity, resources, services, supply chains and market shares, saying many of these developments had direct implications for national security.
He said India and Japan were committed to keeping the Indo-Pacific free and open and were joined in that endeavour by other Quad partners.
Mr. Jaishankar, on Thursday (November 19, 2026), also met Taro Aso, vice-president of Japan's Liberal Democratic Party.

In a post on X, Mr. Jaishankar said the two agreed on the need to strengthen their strategic, economic and energy security cooperation. He also said he valued Aso's commitment towards deepening the partnership between the two countries across governments, businesses and people.

articles.title: Bihar Chief Minister likely to begin statewide journey from November 26
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: During his journey, Mr. Choudhary is likely to spend a day in each district; reviewing development projects and the implementation of various government schemes. Bihar has total 38 districts.

Following the footsteps of his predecessor and former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary is likely to launch his statewide journey on November 26, 2026, from the West Champaran district.
During his journey, he is expected to review government schemes and development projects on the ground by meeting district officials, ministers in charge, and local residents.
Replacing Mr. Kumar, Mr. Choudhary of the Bharatiya Janata Party, for the first time in the party, became Bihar Chief Minister in April this year.
The Chief Minister is also likely to meet local residents and inaugurate and lay foundation stones for new development projects.

“The tentative date for the Chief Minister’s statewide journey is November 26. However, everything is still being finalised. While his participation in the journey is confirmed, final details are being given the finishing touches,” a senior official of the Chief Minister’s office, who wanted to be anonymous, told The Hindu.

The Bihar CM’s proposed journey is to begin after Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Bihar on November 21, 2026. During the visit, Mr. Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the six-lane ‘Nitish Setu’ from Kacchi Dargah-Bidupur in Vaishali district, and lay the foundation stone for other projects at Jaffarpatti industrial area under Rajapakar block of the Vaishali district.

Mr. Choudhary, along with other ministers in his cabinet, has been regularly reviewing the venues and holding meetings with senior officials ahead of the Prime Minister’s visit. Other BJP leaders of the State are also camping and holding meetings with local residents to make the PM’s visit, on the completion of one year of the NDA government in the State, a grand success.
Mr. Choudhary is likely to begin his journey from West Champaran district in the northern Bihar. Mr. Kumar, too began most of his statewide journeys from Valmikinagar of West Champaran district.
Since coming to power in November 2005, Mr. Kumar has undertaken over a dozen statewide journeys to gather feedback directly from local residents and leaders on government’s development initiatives.
“Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary may also emulate Nitish Kumar during his statewide journeys,” an official confirmed.
During his journey, Mr. Choudhary is likely to spend a day in each district, reviewing development projects and the implementation of various government schemes. Bihar has total 38 districts.
“He (chief minister) would also be meeting the respective top district officials and ministers in charge of those districts to get the actual feedback,” said the Bihar CMO official.

articles.title: Malaysia to end visa-free entry to Indians from January 1, 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Earlier, Indian nationals travelling to the South East Asian nation were granted a 30-day visa exemption and just had to register for Malaysia Digital Arrival Card within three days before arrival
Malaysia is ending its visa-free access for Indian nationals from January 1, 2027, the Immigration Department of Malaysia has announced.
Earlier, Indian nationals travelling to the South East Asian nation were granted a 30-day visa exemption and just had to register for Malaysia Digital Arrival Card within three days before arrival.
The visa exemption was introduced on December 1, 2023, and later extended to the end of 2026.
The Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM), in a notice on November 17, said the visa exemption facility for Indian nationals will no longer be available with effect from 1 January 2027.

Accordingly, Indian nationals entering Malaysia from this date onwards will be required to obtain a valid visa prior to their arrival, it said. Visa applications may be submitted through the MyVISA portal starting 1 December 2026, it added.
The JIM further said that visa processing fees would be non-refundable, regardless of the application outcome, change of policy or any subsequent changes to travel plans.
The Immigration Department of Malaysia reserves the right to amend these entry requirements at any time in accordance with directives from the Government of Malaysia, the notice said.

It also advised visitors to obtain travel medical coverage for the full duration of their intended stay in Malaysia. Medical treatment and related healthcare services are chargeable to non-residents, who are responsible for all expenses incurred, it said.
In September, India had advised its nationals in Malaysia not to use the country's 30-day visa-free entry facility to seek employment.

In an advisory posted on X , the High Commission of India in Kuala Lumpur said it has noticed a “noticeable increase” in Indian nationals arriving in Malaysia who are "misled by unscrupulous agents with false job promises." The High Commission said the 30-day visa-free facility is meant for tourism and social visits and does not permit employment.

articles.title: T.N. BJP chief Nainar Nagenthran slams TVK govt. over alleged halting of ₹1,000 assistance to women
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The TVK-led government had denied the claim that the assistance has been halted

BJP State unit president Nainar Nagenthran on Thursday (November 19, 2026) accused the TVK government of betraying the women of Tamil Nadu by allegedly stopping the monthly ₹1,000 assistance to lakhs of beneficiaries under the Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai scheme.

Citing media reports in this regard, he said more than 50% of the 16.94 lakh beneficiaries added during the second phase in December 2025 had reportedly not received the assistance for the past three months. The scheme had earlier benefited 1.31 crore women every month, he said.
Demanding that the government immediately credit the three months’ arrears to the affected beneficiaries, Mr. Nagenthran urged it to implement the promised ₹2,500 assistance without further delay.
It may be mentioned that the TVK-led government had denied the claim that the assistance has been halted.

articles.title: Telangana BIE releases Intermediate exam 2027 time table
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Theory examinations for Intermediate first-year students will commence on February 24, 2027, while second-year examinations will begin on February 25

The Telangana Board of Intermediate Education (TGBIE) on Thursday (November 19, 2026) announced the tentative schedule for the Intermediate Public Examinations (IPE) February/March 2027 for first and second-year students.

Theory examinations for Intermediate first-year students will commence on February 24, 2027, while second-year examinations will begin on February 25. All theory examinations will be conducted from 9 a.m. to 12 noon

Practical examinations for second-year science students will be held from February 1 to February 10, including Sundays. The examinations will be conducted in two sessions from 9 a.m. to 12 noon and 2 p.m. to 5 p.m.

For first-year science students, practical examinations will take place from February 11 to February 18, in three sessions from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m., 12 noon to 2 p.m., and 3.30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. English practical examinations for first-year students are scheduled for January 29, and second-year students will appear for the examination on January 30.

Compulsory examinations such as Environmental Education is on January 27, and Ethics and Human Values is on January 29. As per the schedule, first-year internal assessment will be held from January 20 to 25.

The first-year theory examinations will begin with the second language Paper-I on February 24, followed by English Paper-I on February 26. The second-year examinations will commence with second language Paper-II on February 25, followed by English Paper-II on February 27.
The examinations conclude on March 20. The dates will also apply to Intermediate vocational course examinations, and a separate timetable will be issued, the Board said..

Telangana BIE releases Intermediate exam 2027 time table

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Theory examinations for Intermediate first-year students will commence on February 24, 2027, while second-year examinations will begin on February 25

The Telangana Board of Intermediate Education (TGBIE) on Thursday (November 19, 2026) announced the tentative schedule for the Intermediate Public Examinations (IPE) February/March 2027 for first and second-year students.

Theory examinations for Intermediate first-year students will commence on February 24, 2027, while second-year examinations will begin on February 25. All theory examinations will be conducted from 9 a.m. to 12 noon

Practical examinations for second-year science students will be held from February 1 to February 10, including Sundays. The examinations will be conducted in two sessions from 9 a.m. to 12 noon and 2 p.m. to 5 p.m.

For first-year science students, practical examinations will take place from February 11 to February 18, in three sessions from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m., 12 noon to 2 p.m., and 3.30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. English practical examinations for first-year students are scheduled for January 29, and second-year students will appear for the examination on January 30.

Compulsory examinations such as Environmental Education is on January 27, and Ethics and Human Values is on January 29. As per the schedule, first-year internal assessment will be held from January 20 to 25.

The first-year theory examinations will begin with the second language Paper-I on February 24, followed by English Paper-I on February 26. The second-year examinations will commence with second language Paper-II on February 25, followed by English Paper-II on February 27.

articles.title: Keralam mulling community-based system for early identification of at-risk children, providing support
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: FOLKS – Friends of Little Kids is envisaged as a structured child protection early warning and intervention initiative that aims at connecting vulnerable children with the formal child protection system without delays.

In the wake of the death of a toddler at Nedumangad following physical trauma, allegedly inflicted by his mother’s partner, Keralam is considering putting in place a community-based mechanism for early identification of children at risk and connecting them with the formal child protection system without delays.

FOLKS – Friends of Little Kids is envisaged as a structured child protection early warning and intervention initiative that focusses on children who may be facing abuse, neglect, abandonment, or other forms of harm but go unnoticed until very late, besides children who show violent behaviour.

The Statewide mechanism aims at strengthening connections between communities and existing institutional framework such as child welfare committees, district child protection units, Childline, and educational and health institutions to enable timely reporting of situations where children are at risk and support interventions such as rescue and rehabilitation.
FOLKS will tap into the network of Social Work students and faculty members and professionally qualified social work practitioners who work in the child protection and welfare sectors.

These FOLKS members will observe and report physical or emotional abuse, repeated injuries, severe neglect, malnutrition or starvation, child labour, child marriage risks, unsafe living conditions, dropping out of schools, and similar other situations.
The reporting will be done through Childline 1098, district child protection units (DCPUs), designated district-level WhatsApp groups, and child protection nodal officers.
The WhatsApp groups will include DCPU officials, Childline representatives, police nodal officers, social work college coordinators, and FOLKS representatives.

As serious incidents usually occur in households already experiencing social distress, DCPUs may maintain a confidential vulnerable family support register. Families with severe vulnerability, domestic violence, substance abuse, repeated police intervention, family breakdown, child neglect complaints, and previous child protection interventions will be identified through referrals from stakeholders in the existing child protection institutional framework.

A monitoring network including anganwadi workers, school teachers, DCPUs, and FOLKS members will all have roles such as observation of children; monitoring attendance and behavioural changes; reporting neglect, malnutrition, and safety concerns; conducting welfare visits; case management, and follow-up interventions.

Mentorship is an important aspect of the FOLKS initiative, particularly in the case of children in child care institutions. Regular communication with the children will allow the social work students to build a rapport with them and identify behavioural changes if any and bring about a modification in their behaviour. This will be particularly helpful once the department conducts vulnerability mapping to identify children in high-risk environments. The social work students in turn will be awarded certificates or some other token of appreciation for their work.
Inter-department coordination will be a significant aspect of FOLKS, which will be piloted in some districts before being extended across the State.

articles.title: How AI could reshape global growth and productivity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole.

A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

articles.title: India’s Oct. crude import bill soars 87.5% to $19.5-bn amid West Asia tensions, volumes up 11%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: While higher petroleum product exports offer a partial natural hedge, sustained increases in crude and gas prices could intensify pressure on the country’s import bill.

India’s crude oil import bill surged 87.5% year-on-year (YoY) to $19.5 billion in October, as elevated international benchmark prices, fuelled by renewed tensions in West Asia, sharply increased procurement costs. The increase came alongside an 11% rise in import volumes.

The net import bill, calculated as imports of crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas less exports of petroleum products, rose 60% to $16 billion during the month, compared with $10 billion in October last year.
Higher export realisations from petroleum products, however, provided some cushion against the escalating import burden.

According to provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), India imported 23.3 million metric tonnes (MMT) of crude oil in October, against 21 MMT in the corresponding month last year.
The expenditure on crude imports, meanwhile, climbed to $19.5 billion from $10.4 billion, reflecting the disproportionate impact of higher international prices on the country’s energy import bill.

The Indian crude oil basket averaged $119.91 per barrel in October, compared with $124.77 per barrel for Brent crude. In September, the Indian basket had averaged $116.09 per barrel, while Brent stood at $116.77 per barrel.

The sustained increase in benchmark prices, amid continuing geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia, has left India exposed to higher energy procurement costs, given its dependence on imported crude oil.
The impact of the rising crude import bill was partly offset by stronger earnings from petroleum product exports.
India’s petroleum product exports increased 5.9% in volume terms to 5.4 MMT in October. However, export revenues surged approximately 91% to $6.3 billion.
The increase in export earnings provided an important buffer against the higher cost of crude procurement.

Meanwhile, India’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports declined approximately 7% to 3,014 million standard cubic metres (MMSCM) during October. Despite the decline in volumes, the import bill increased 8.33%, pointing to the persistence of price pressures in the international gas market.

articles.title: India-U.S. trade deal signing will still ‘take some time’, says Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: He added that the deal can be signed only after the U.S. finalises its new tariff framework. Recently, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the two nations had agreed that India would receive an advantage over its competitors

The actual signing of the India-U.S. trade will still “take some time”, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), adding that the negotiation part and the legal text will be completed soon.

The delay in signing, he said, was because it can be done only after the U.S. concludes its Section 301 investigations into its trade partners and finalises its tariff structure. A few days ago, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal asserted that the U.S. has acknowledged that India will receive lower tariffs as compared to its competitors.

“This is a deal that has been announced in February, the contours have already been announced as part of the joint statement,” Mr. Agrawal said while speaking at the curtain raiser of the FICCI Annual General Meeting. “The legal agreement has also been negotiated and it is now in final stages and it will be concluded soon.”
He was referring to the joint statement between India and the U.S. in February that announced the framework of an interim deal on trade.

However, Mr. Agrawal explained that the “challenge” is that this framework was announced against the background of the executive tariffs system that the U.S. President Donald Trump had put in place. At the time, the tariff on India was 50%. Later in February, the U.S. Supreme Court struck down the legal foundation of these tariffs.

“Now a new tariff architecture is being created by the U.S.,” Mr. Agrawal explained. “So until that tariff architecture comes back in place, the signing of a deal is something that I think will take some time. But concluding the negotiations and having everything ready will be something that we will strive to achieve as soon as possible.”
In particular, Mr. Agrawal spoke about the investigations undertaken by the American administration under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

One of these investigations, regarding forced labour, has been completed and a tariff of 10% has been levied on imports from India. The second investigation, looking into excess capacity, is yet to be completed and could come with further tariffs.

“There are certain 301 investigations which are already under review,” Mr. Agrawal said. “Those will also be coming to the fore in the next few weeks or months. You can’t have a deal until you have got uncertainty around multiple investigations which are already there.”

Separately, without mentioning the U.S. or any other country, Mr. Agrawal also asserted that trade deals can take a long time to conclude when parties try to maximise the benefits accruing to them rather than engaging in a spirit of compromise.

“Negotiations are always, to my mind, the art of what is possible,” the Commerce Secretary said. “You try to bring it together and keep it in a mutual win-win position because each party wants to go from the table as a victor and wants to showcase to its people that they have got something good for their business.”
As such, he explained that most agreements are not perfect, but instead involve an even trade-off where parties have simultaneously minimized their risk and also taken advantage of what they can.

articles.title: Balancing AI-driven estimates and ground-level evidence in official statistics
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: While AI and Machine Learning promise to make India’s official statistics faster and comprehensive, they cannot automatically replace ground-level evidence; synthetic data with inherited limitations may lead to misallocation of public resources and distortion of economic indicators

A statement reading: “Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war,” was signed by 350 technology and industry leaders including Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio, Demis Hassabis (Google DeepMind), Sam Altman (OpenAI), Dario Amodei (Anthropic), and Bill Gates. It warns of scenarios including loss of human control over machine optimisation goals, illustrating the risks of man-made invention.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are positioned as core pillars in the newly approved Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR), which is set to overhaul India’s official data architecture.

articles.title: Rising prices reflect government’s economic mismanagement: Congress
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Monthly costs up by over 20% for 61% of families, according to a survey cited by Congress leader Jairam Ramesh; claims PM is more pre-occupied with politics than tackling the inflation crisis

The Congress on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) accused the Union government of fuelling inflation through its “economic mismanagement and anti-people policies” and alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi remained preoccupied with politics rather than addressing the economic distress faced by households and businesses.

Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh cited a survey which found that, for 61% of families across the country, monthly household expenditure had risen by more than 20% over the past year. While 74% of respondents were cutting back on non-essential spending, 50% had reduced purchases of essential goods, he said.
Citing the survey, Mr. Ramesh said prices of ghee and edible oils had risen by 75%, vegetables by 73%, cereals by 71%, milk and dairy products by 65%, and pulses by 62%.

He also claimed that 200 garment factories had shut down in Noida over the past year, citing the impact of U.S. tariffs, high input costs, and government apathy. He said the closures reflected the wider distress in the textile industry.

“People’s plates are shrinking, and factories are being locked down. Yet, the Prime Minister’s only concern remains politics,” he said on X, accusing the government of failing to acknowledge people’s hardships or offer relief.

articles.title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting highlights: Xi-Trump-Putin summit in China ends; major powers must not touch each other's bottom lines on sensitive issues, says Xi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: China-U.S. relations 'stable and improved', Xi says; Ukraine strikes Crimean bridge again as Trump says U.S., China want to help end war

Some in the West are comparing the three-way meeting to the 1945 Yalta conference, where the wartime leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union divided Germany and Berlin, carved out zones of influence in Europe, and agreed to establish the United Nations.
The Kremlin, which long has courted the concept of a “multipolar world” offering an equal say to all nations, plays down the Yalta comparisons, which are also unwelcome to China for similar reasons.

Fyodor Lukyanov, a pro-Kremlin foreign policy expert, noted that even as Moscow publicly rejects the Yalta analogy, it seems to believe the leaders could “reach agreements and make decisions that will determine global developments”.
Of the three nations, “it seems that only Russia really believes in the possibility of global control”, he told a recent roundtable.

Chatham House director Bronwen Maddox said in a commentary that “standing with Xi and Trump, Putin will look like one of the three main leaders of the world”, even though “Russia is no superpower” and its economy, overloaded with military spending, is dwindling.
She warned that “the danger for Ukraine is that Trump uses this summit to try to advance his notion of peace, including giving Russia territory it has not managed to seize by force”.

The meeting follows US-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine held in Abu Dhabi last week for the first time in nine months. The negotiations produced few visible results as the parties stuck to their sharply divergent demands. -- AP
Trilateral Xi-Putin-Trump summit draws Yalta 1945 comparisons, highlighting postwar order shifts amid Ukraine tensions and multipolar world debates.

articles.title: China-Russia-U.S. trilateral summit: Xi, Putin, Trump call for cooperation to confront global security challenges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The three heads of state — Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump — had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security

Chinese President Xi Jinping met Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday (November 19, 2026). Following the meeting, the three leaders reviewed the main areas of consensus reached during their discussions.
Shenzhen trilateral summit: Follow LIVE updates on November 19, 2026

“I’m delighted that this trip has given us the opportunity for this first ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia, and China, and today, in that sense, we are really making history,” said Mr. Trump.
Mr. Xi said today’s meeting among the leaders had been positive, constructive and productive, and that the three countries shared common views on safeguarding world peace.

“We all remember the history of fighting side by side during the Second World War and emphasise the importance of cherishing the hard-won peace that emerged from it. We all agree that major powers should take seriously the legitimate security concerns of all countries. We all believe that dialogue and negotiation are the correct ways to resolve differences. As long as dialogue does not cease and doors remain open, there is hope for peace,” said Mr. Xi.
The three heads of State had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security.

“We have a special responsibility to maintain open, respectful, and productive dialogue on issues impacting not just our people but the entire planet. Too often, past leaders avoided talking to nations with whom they had disagreements, and we feel the opposite. No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement and speech,” said Mr. Trump.

The three heads of state recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for the immunities of state officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.
The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.

“As the world’s three largest nuclear powers by far, the United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on earth and also to lessen the risk that those weapons will ever be used, the power is unbelievable, unthinkable. In addition to exploring the potential for arms reduction in our own countries, and I must say it’s quite frankly a very hard thing to do, because once you have the nuclear weapons it’s very hard to not have them, it’s very hard to give them up as the leader of a country,” said Mr. Trump.
The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

“We all believe that cooperation is the only viable path for addressing challenges. Based on our shared interests, we should strengthen cooperation, promote peace through cooperation, and pursue win-win outcomes. The seeds planted by today’s meeting among our three countries will surely take root, blossom and bear fruit. China, Russia and the United States should faithfully implement the consensus reached at this meeting, continue to strengthen communication, build consensus through dialogue, confront challenges with a sense of responsibility, and work together to build a better world,” said Mr. Xi.

fullParagraphs: The ICJ had for seven years weighed the accusations made by Gambia against Myanmar’s treatment of its minority Rohingya community.

Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, the International Court of Justice said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) in an historic verdict, the first time it has ruled a state committed the crime.

“The Republic of the Union of Myanmar has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine State, in violation of its obligations under the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide,” said ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa.

Judges at the top UN court (also called the World Court) had for seven years been weighing accusations made by Gambia about whether Myanmar’s treatment of the Rohingya people breached the 1948 UN Genocide Convention.
The international community closely watched the verdict as an archetype for the case filed by South Africa against Israel over its campaign in Gaza.
The Rohingya are a minority ethnic group, largely comprising Muslims, in the predominantly Buddhist Myanmar, formerly referred to as Burma.

Most of the Rohingya come from the Rakhine State, also known as Arakan State, in northwest Myanmar. The State borders Bangladesh. They speak a dialect of Bengali, as opposed to the commonly spoken Burmese language. While the Rohingya people have been living in Myanmar for generations, they are not recognised by the country, rendering them effectively stateless. Their movement are also restricted within the Rakhine State.
When Burma won Independence from the UK in 1948, the Bengali-speaking Muslim population near the border exceeded that of the Buddhists, leading to secessionist tensions, according to Reuters .

In 1962, a coup led to nearly five decades of military rule by the ethnic Burman majority. In 1978, thousands of people fled to Bangladesh to escape a military census of the Rohingya called “Operation Dragon.”
In 1991, another wave of refugees fled to Bangladesh where the UN says 300,000 Rohingya now live a stateless existence.

Due to years of harassment beginning in 2012 and exacerbated in 2017, thousands of Rohingya have fled Myanmar, with many attempting to travel in rickety wooden boats to Malaysia, where 14,300 official Rohingya refugees and maybe half as many unregistered ones live.

Sectarian violence between Rohingyas and Rakhine’s Buddhist natives began flaring up in June 2012, following the rape and murder of a Rakhine woman in a Rohingya-dominated locality, according to a report published in The Hindu. The riots, which were triggered as a result, went on for almost a month with causalities on both the sides.

articles.title: Trump says U.S. opposes 'globalist regulation' of AI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The United States opposes "globalist regulation" of artificial intelligence in any form, President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) ahead of talks with China's Xi Jinping, expected to broach the topic.
Mr. Trump has repeatedly rejected calls for wide-reaching international governance of AI, warning it could hold his country back in its race with China.
"It's super intelligence, but we have to watch it," he told leaders at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in Shenzhen, using his administration's preferred term for AI.
"We have to be careful. We have to cherish it. It's almost completely good, but it's got some bad elements, and we have to be very careful in managing those bad elements," Mr. Trump said.
"So we oppose any form of globalist regulation or anything to control and stifle SI, and we won't allow that to happen, frankly."
Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi are due to hold talks later on Thursday, with the issues they are set to discuss including how to address the rapid changes brought by AI.
Despite the countries' fierce tech rivalry, AI safety risks of shared concern range from infrastructure hacking to people using the technology to help build bioweapons.

Another problem in the spotlight is out-of-control AI agents, tools that complete real-life tasks online, after ChatGPT maker OpenAI's bots hacked into websites including an Australian government portal, incidents followed by similar reports by other labs.
Military use and mass surveillance are also potential flashpoints for the world's two leading AI powers.
Looming over the talks, however, is Jensen Huang's resignation as boss of US chip titan Nvidia after revelations of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi agreed in September to create a channel for urgent communication on AI incidents, with details to be hammered out on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
Mr. Xi this summer said the technology should be "always under human control" -- calling for more "laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning and emergency response systems".

articles.title: Replace Russian junk with American weapons system: U.S. lawmaker to India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Michael Baumgartner made the remarks on Capitol Hill in the presence of Namgya Khampa, the Deputy Chief of Mission at the Indian Embassy in Washington

India should replace its "legacy ineffective Russian junk” with American weapons systems and also opt for Boeing aircraft over those manufactured by European Airbus Industries, a U.S. Congressman has suggested.

Michael Baumgartner, a Republican from Washington state, made the remarks at Deepavali celebrations on Capitol Hill on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) in the presence of Namgya Khampa, the Deputy Chief of Mission at the Indian Embassy in Washington.

The Deepavali celebrations were hosted by BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Asian American Hotel Owners Association, Hindu American Foundations, Srimad Rajchandra Mission Dharampur, Sikhs of America, Art of Living, Foundations of Jain Associations in North America and the U.S. Indian Community Foundation.

As a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Mr. Baumgartner said he regularly engages with diplomats from the Indian Embassy as the two countries seek to strengthen relations across economic and security issues.

“I was pleased to again express my thoughts that the more U.S. exports to India — from weapons systems to replace their legacy ineffective Russian junk to Boeing airplanes that are superior to Airbus to the world’s best lentils from the Palouse — the better it is for our two great countries,” Mr. Baumgartner said in a post on X.
Mr. Baumgartner also raised the issue of disruptions during Deepavali celebrations in his home state of Washington.

“A couple weeks back some attention-seeking racist morons disrupted a Diwali celebration in my home state of Washington. This evening, I was pleased to attend the Diwali celebration at the US Capitol,” he said.

The Deepavali celebrations were also attended by the U.S. Congresswoman-elect Pia Dandiya, Congresspersons Grace Meng, Suhas Subramanyam, Shri Thanedar, Nick LaLota, Jonathan Jackson, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Norma Torres, Pete Sessions, Deborah Ross, Buddy Carter, Michael Guest, among others.
Scott Colom, who scripted history by becoming the first black Senator from Mississippi in 146 years, also lit the traditional lamp at the Deepavali celebrations.

fullParagraphs: With record pre-orders and broad market reach, GTA VI is positioned to dominate digital engagement through the end of the year

As Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI officially launches today , November 19, 2026, a market intelligence report from Sensor Tower highlights an unprecedented shift in consumer engagement and industry revenue.

According to Sensor Tower’s report, the title generated $1.1 billion in pre-order revenue globally across PlayStation and Xbox consoles prior to release, with 11.3 million copies sold. This accomplishment marks the largest pre-launch revenue total on record.

The analytics firms project that total sales could reach $3.2 billion by the end of 2026. Beyond financial performance, the report forecasts a noticeable reallocation of consumer attention across the broader digital landscape.
Daily active user metrics across competing games and entertainment platforms are expected to see a measurable decline as players engage with the new release.
Sensor Tower estimates the average GTA VI player age at approximately 34 years old. This audience displays high companion engagement on second-screen platforms, including Discord, TikTok, and Twitch.
With record pre-orders and broad market reach, GTA VI is positioned to dominate digital engagement through the end of the year.

articles.title: GTA VI: Gamers enter Vice City as most-awaited game is rolled out globally
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Game unlocked at midnight on November 19 in each market; Rockstar says story follows criminal couple Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval in Vice City
The wait is over. ‌After 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, the most anticipated video game release in history is finally ​here.

“Grand Theft Auto VI” became available as midnight struck in New Zealand on Thursday (November 19, 2026), with the launch then following the clock around ⁠the world. Millions of players have already downloaded the game to their consoles in anticipation.

The release, with events worldwide and many users taking days off work to play, marks the latest instalment in one of entertainment’s most successful franchises. Since its 1997 debut, “Grand Theft Auto” has become one of the best-selling video game series of all time.

“I’ve been waiting 13 years to ‌play,” said 20-year-old Jonah Bowen-Brown from Australia’s southern island of Tasmania, who persuaded his mother to give him and his brother a week off work at the family-run fragrance shop, Whiff-it!.
“She was really against it at first,” said Bowen-Brown. “I had to say, mum, please, please, I need ‌it.”
A gamer plays Grand Theft Auto VI in Miami, Florida | Photo Credit: Reuters
The game is made by Take-Two Interactive’s Rockstar Games and available on Sony’s PlayStation 5 and Microsoft’s Xbox Series X and S consoles.

The original “Grand Theft ‌Auto” ⁠looks basic by today’s standards, and its missions — stealing cars and carrying out jobs for crime syndicates — angered politicians and parents. But it delighted ⁠gamers.

Each successive release delivered more sophisticated graphics and storytelling. “Grand Theft Auto V”, released in 2013 and set in the fictional Los Santos, a stand-in for Los Angeles, became one of the best-selling video games ever.
While retaining the series’ trademark mix of crime, driving and morally dubious missions, it added activities ranging from parachute jumps to cinema visits and radio stations satirising US culture.
The action now moves to Vice City, a ‌fictional version of Miami, in the state of Leonida, the game’s take on Florida.

From previews, fans know a little. Play will switch between two leading characters, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval. They are partners in crime and romantically involved — just how romantically will be up to the player. There will be nightclubs, gun stores, scuba diving and a zoo. But much remains to be revealed.

articles.title: GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru

This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open.

The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015.

GTA 6 is now live on Blinkit! 🎮 It took 13 years for GTA 6 to be released. In the meantime, we built Blinkit so that you can get the game delivered in minutes. We've launched it in select areas of Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata & Ahmedabad (launching in more cities between today and tomorrow). We'll deliver a physical box with a download code inside (the box is a nice collectible for your shelf). Get yours now and start downloading so you're ready to play from 19th November. Expecting a suspicious number of sick leaves over the next few days 😮‍💨

In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”.

For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia.

Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.
Your KRA is updated to completing missions and side quests 🎮 https://t.co/x1xSmUIPqU

Grand Theft Auto V arrived in India in September 2013, priced at around ₹3,000 for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. But its second life here began after PUBG Mobile was banned in September 2020. Several of India’s biggest streamers, including Dynamo and MortaL, turned to other games, GTA V among them, and roleplay helped make it a mainstay of Indian livestreaming.

A roleplay server is a fan-run version of GTA V’s online world where players invent characters with names, jobs and backstories, from cab drivers and paramedics to cops and small-time crooks, and inhabit them for hours. Soulcity, launched by S8UL and Velocity Gaming in early 2023, became one of India’s biggest GTA V roleplay servers and helped create a new breed of gaming star. S8UL co-founder Lokesh Jain, better known as 8Bit Goldy, played a character called Rocket Singh on the server. The scene grew big enough for S8UL to sign creators such as Sunny Jha, aka Pitaji Playz, specifically for its GTA roleplay roster.
Gamers watch a screen showing the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) at a gaming centre in Buenos Aires on the day of the highly anticipated video game's release. | Photo Credit: AFP

One of the biggest differences between GTA VI and its predecessors for Indian players is how much of it was made here. Rockstar India’s Bengaluru studio reportedly has the largest team of any Rockstar office working on the game, with around 1,615 developers, and media reports credit it with building Vice Beach, a location on the map. Its roots go back to Dhruva Interactive, founded by Rajesh Rao in Bengaluru in 1997 and considered India’s oldest game developer when Rockstar folded it into Rockstar India in 2019. Rockstar India was established in 2016 and contributed to Red Dead Redemption 2 before turning to Leonida.

The game follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, two small-time criminals drawn into a conspiracy across Leonida, Rockstar’s fictional Florida, after a job goes wrong. Lucia is the series’ first female lead since it moved into three dimensions. The Vice City she drives through is a contemporary one, a far cry from the pastel-hued 1980s city many Indian players grew up with.

articles.title: India missed its 2025 TB elimination target. What does the WHO report show?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The WHO’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 has withheld India’s 2025 incidence estimate pending an assessment of new surveillance data. What does the report reveal about India’s TB burden, and why has the country missed its target?

The story so far: India continues to account for nearly a quarter of the world’s tuberculosis (TB) burden despite expanded diagnosis and treatment services, falling short of the national target of eliminating TB by 2025. According to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report, released on November 12, 2026, an estimated 10.6 million people developed TB worldwide in 2025.

While India’s estimated TB mortality rate fell by 38%, from 28 deaths per lakh population in 2015 to 18 per lakh in 2025, the country diagnosed and notified 25.3 lakh cases during the year. However, the WHO has not published India’s estimated incidence for that year, as the figures are under review.

Science, Space & Environment Report: India missed its 2025 TB elimination target. What does the WHO report show?. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

India missed its 2025 TB elimination target. What does the WHO report show?

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

The WHO’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 has withheld India’s 2025 incidence estimate pending an assessment of new surveillance data. What does the report reveal about India’s TB burden, and why has the country missed its target?

The story so far: India continues to account for nearly a quarter of the world’s tuberculosis (TB) burden despite expanded diagnosis and treatment services, falling short of the national target of eliminating TB by 2025. According to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report, released on November 12, 2026, an estimated 10.6 million people developed TB worldwide in 2025.

While India’s estimated TB mortality rate fell by 38%, from 28 deaths per lakh population in 2015 to 18 per lakh in 2025, the country diagnosed and notified 25.3 lakh cases during the year. However, the WHO has not published India’s estimated incidence for that year, as the figures are under review.

articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.
Editorial Context: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India needs to be at its best in Tests against New Zealand

New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.
