The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP

As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

articles.title: Ruckus erupts between SFI activists and police over setting up bookstalls near Calcutta University
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The SFI leaders said they sought permission from the Kolkata Police to set up a bookstall on the College Street footpath, but police refused on November 16 evening, saying it could disrupt traffic

A ruckus erupted between supporters of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), and police near the University of Kolkata for setting up a book stall. After the clash, police detained several SFI supporters, including the SFI State secretary, Debanjan Dey.

The SFI leadership said that they sought permission from the Kolkata Police to set up a book stall at a makeshift stall on the footpath of College Street. However, the police refused to grant permission on Monday evening, stating that it might disrupt traffic. The book stall was part of a three-day campaign, “Sangrami Boipotro”, by the party. It was supposed to be inaugurated by the Left Front chairman, Biman Bose, on Tuesday evening.

“We have permission from the Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Jorasanko Police Station for a period of five years to set up bookstalls at College Street. Necessary tax was also paid to the concerned authorities. We have been setting up such stalls for the last four years. Our plan was to do the same this year too. But the Kolkata Police have now refused to allow us anymore,” said Mr. Dey to the media persons

The protesters said that a few police vans had already been stationed on College Street since Monday night. When they began preparing to set up the stalls on Tuesday morning, the police stopped them and said that no book stalls could be organised in the area.

The situation escalated when they blocked College Street and staged a sit-in. They laid out a sheet on the tram line in the middle of the road and began selling their books. They also invited the police to buy books for their children. It immediately resulted in a clash with the police. The police were seen using mild force to disrupt the protesters and clear the road. Several activists, including Mr. Dey, Subhadeep Bandyopadhyay, Didhiti Roy, and Haseeb Hossain, have been detained.

“A heavy police force was deployed across College Street on Tuesday only to stop us selling some books. They have assaulted the students who have been fighting for the books. It is now clear that the government has declared war against the books. They want to destroy the culture and tradition of Bengal. We will have to fight the battle with books only against them,” said Mr. Dey after the detention.
Following the development, the left student union also organised a rally in the evening at the Mahabodhi Society and demanded the immediate release of the detained students.

The dispute over the book stalls set up by the Left parties began during Durga Puja. Police and civic bodies demolished several stalls set up by the parties across Kolkata. In Jadavpur, a bulldozer was also brought in to dismantle a stall, sparking a huge political controversy. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had described Left party supporters as “atheist” and declared that they would not be allowed to set up their book stalls near puja pandals, where such stalls have been a fixture for decades.

articles.title: Convocation ceremony row: Maharaja’s College council asks suspended students to accept their mistake
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The incident caused disrepute to the image of the institution in the public domain, finds inquiry report

A meeting of the council of Maharaja’s College, Kochi, held on Tuesday accepted an inquiry committee report that indicted activists of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) for disrupting a convocation ceremony attended by Minister for Higher Education Roji M. John on October 30.

The meeting recommended that V. Praneel Raj, chairperson, and Nafeesathul Misriya, vice-chairperson of the college union, who were suspended in connection with the incident on November 2, submit an apology admitting their mistake. The inquiry committee report found that the incident had caused disrepute to the image of the institution in the public domain, according to sources.

The council observed that it did not wish to initiate further disciplinary action against the students, but they need to accept their mistake. The meeting took note of the case registered by the police against 10 SFI activists booked in connection with the protest.

SFI activists staged the protest soon after the Minister completed his inaugural address at the convocation ceremony, seeking answers from him on the suspension of 16 students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady. The activists demanded that the Minister withdraw his alleged statements against those who were suspended for protesting against Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas. Following the protest, Mr. John had to leave the function midway.

articles.title: Kochi woman loses ₹90,000 in credit card activation scam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The complainant, a resident of Mulavukad, was allegedly cheated by an unidentified person who contacted her over the phone, promising to activate a credit card issued by a private sector bank
The Kochi City cyber police have registered a case after a 36-year-old woman was allegedly cheated of nearly ₹90,000 on the pretext of activating a credit card.

The complainant, a resident of Mulavukad, was allegedly cheated by an unidentified person who contacted her over the phone, promising to activate a credit card issued by a private sector bank. On November 2, the accused convinced her to share a one-time password (OTP) to activate the card using another credit card she owns. She lost ₹49,440 after sharing the OTP. Two days later, the accused contacted the woman again and asked her to share another OTP to credit the amount debited earlier back to her card. This time, she was duped of ₹40,464.
The police have registered a case of cheating under Section 318 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

articles.title: Kerala High Court allows Cusat employees to seek review of suspension
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court directed the Syndicate to examine whether the continued suspension was justified
The Kerala High Court has held that the suspended employees of the Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat) can approach the university Syndicate seeking a review of their suspension.

Justice P. Gopinath issued the interim direction in view of the Syndicate meeting scheduled for November 21. The court directed the Syndicate to examine whether the continued suspension was justified. It also instructed the petitioners to file an application before the Syndicate seeking a review of the suspension order.
Cusat Employees Association members Anurin Salim, P.M. Sivadas, and Harilal had approached the court challenging the suspension order.

The Syndicate had suspended the petitioners based on an inquiry report by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) into allegations of irregularities in appointments to the sweeper-cum-cleaner posts. They alleged that the officials were not given an opportunity to explain their position and that they were suspended before a charge memo was issued.

articles.title: Opposition, ruling councillors in Keralam’s Kochi Corporation spar over Thuruthy Towers, ro-ro service at stormy council meet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: LDF seeks dates for apartment handover and launch of third ro-ro vessel; UDF cites procedural delays in commissioning vessel; Opposition alleges UDF is using losses incurred by KSINC to justify privatisation of ro-ro ferry operations

The Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) staged a protest towards the fag end of the Kochi Corporation council meeting on Tuesday, disrupting proceedings over the alleged delay in handing over apartments to beneficiaries of Thuruthy Towers in the Kalvathy division and the induction of the third roll-on roll-off (ro-ro) vessel into service. The Opposition demanded that dates for both be announced in the council.

LDF councillors sought to know why the new vessel was yet to commence operations despite being inaugurated by Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on July 12. They also accused the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) council of attempting to pave the way for the privatisation of ro-ro operations by highlighting losses incurred by the existing public sector operator, Kerala Shipping and Inland Navigation Corporation Limited (KSINC).

LDF councillor P.J. Yesudas drew attention to the hardships faced by commuters on the Fort Kochi-Vypeen route, as one of the two existing ro-ro vessels has remained out of service for the past five days due to a snag. “Though the Mayor announced the formation of a sub-committee to discuss issues affecting the ro-ro service, it has not met even once. The new vessel should be introduced without further delay ahead of the festive season in December, when lakhs visit Fort Kochi for the Carnival and New Year celebrations. Any further delay runs the risk of a tragedy similar to the Fort Kochi boat accident 11 years ago,” he said.

UDF councillor Henry Austin attributed the delay to the formation of the special purpose vehicle (SPV) to manage ro-ro services and the time taken to secure nearly 10 different certificates and licences before commissioning the vessel. “We cannot afford inadequacies in the formation of the SPV as it would ultimately cost the Corporation. There is no need to create a narrative that the service is being run at a loss to justify privatisation, since it has been operating at a loss from the very outset,” he said.

Welfare standing committee chairperson Antony Painuthara said the SPV had been formed and would be placed before the council for approval on Wednesday, following which it would be submitted to the government for clearance. He said the UDF council had managed to constitute the SPV within a year, whereas the LDF had failed to do so despite being in power in the Corporation for five years. He also questioned how the new vessel, ordered during the previous council’s tenure, had cost ₹15 crore, while the two vessels introduced during the LDF administration had collectively cost ₹10 crore.

LDF parliamentary party leader V.A. Sreejith alleged that the council was being repeatedly misled, citing multiple missed deadlines for handing over the Thuruthy apartments, the latest being November 1. “The lack of clarity in the beneficiary list is being cited as the reason for the delay, though the welfare standing committee met thrice to resolve the issue. The list has also not been placed before the council. The apartments should be handed over immediately to eligible beneficiaries who have completed all formalities, followed by the rest at the earliest,” he said.

Works standing committee chairperson T.K. Asharaf initially said the apartments would be handed over in December, but later claimed that letters had been sent to more than 250 beneficiaries informing them that the apartments were ready for occupancy. The LDF then sought clarification from the Corporation secretary, who said the council would be updated on Wednesday. The Opposition also rejected the UDF’s allegation that the towers had been inaugurated by the former Chief Minister before the completion of the works, pointing out that 24 storeys had been constructed during the previous council’s tenure.

articles.title: Earthshot Prize: Climate action needs innovation, global cooperation, say leaders on green carpet in Mumbai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Maharashtra Environment and Climate Change Minister Pankaja Munde called for global cooperation to protect the planet for future generations

Global leaders, business executives, and celebrities called for greater investment in environmental innovations and collective action against climate change as they gathered on the green carpet ahead of the Earthshot Prize Awards in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
Among those attending were former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern, Serum Institute of India CEO Adar Poonawalla, filmmaker Karan Johar, and Maharashtra Environment Minister Pankaja Mund.
Speaking to reporters, Mr. Poonawalla emphasised the importance of supporting environmental innovations and helping them attract investment.

“Prevention is better than cure—that’s what we believe at Serum Institute,” he said, explaining the company’s partnership with the Earthshot Prize. He added that the initiative would help innovators connect with investors and scale up technologies capable of addressing environmental challenges.
Ms. Ardern welcomed the awards to Mumbai, highlighting India’s record of producing the highest number of Earthshot finalists and winners.

“The Earthshot Prize is showcasing responses to that crisis to demonstrate that things are happening and innovation is available, we just need to scale it up with speed,” she said, referring to the climate crisis.

Coral Pasisi, president of Tofia, Niue, highlighted Indigenous-led ocean conservation efforts. “We’re protecting one of the largest areas of ocean on the planet. And we developed a sustainable financing mechanism that’s driven by Indigenous people,” she said, stressing the need for international support.

Maharashtra Environment and Climate Change Minister Pankaja Munde called for global cooperation to protect the planet for future generations. She expressed concern that rapid urbanisation and industrialisation had drowned out natural sounds, including birdsong and flowing water, and urged people to protect forests and biodiversity.
Filmmaker Karan Johar praised Prince William’s environmental commitment, describing him as a “climate warrior” who empowered innovators through the Earthshot Prize.

Actor Sonam Kapoor emphasised that environmental responsibility extended beyond public statements. Speaking about her children, she said individuals and governments needed to take concrete steps to protect the environment for future generations.

Former Indian football captain Sunil Chhetri, attending with Football for Peace for its “Rehydrate the Earth” campaign, stressed the importance of awareness and collective efforts to minimise environmental risks.

Founded by Prince William, the Earthshot Prize recognises innovative solutions to environmental challenges, including climate change, pollution, biodiversity loss and ocean conservation. Five winners are selected annually, each receiving £1 million to help scale their solutions.

articles.title: Fearmongering around fake drugs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: As per the last National Drug Survey published in 2017, the volume of counterfeit drugs in the Indian market detected in the survey was at a negligible 0.0245%

Recent news from Karnataka regarding the seizure of fake cancer drugs from a licensed distributor during a raid has understandably sparked concerns. Counterfeit drugs for serious conditions like cancer are a sensational and emotive issue, often provoking a demand for severe action, including death sentences for those involved in the distribution.

However, in this case, there is a serious reason to doubt the authenticity of the news reports about the recent seizure since the Government of Karnataka has not confirmed that indeed counterfeit cancer drugs were seized in the raid. While a purported list of the drugs seized was circulated on social media, it only contained antibiotics, not cancer drugs. The silence of the State Health Department on the news reports about the counterfeit drugs is insensitive to the dread and uncertainty being faced by patients receiving cancer treatment, not to mention the doubts of those wondering whether they lost their loved ones to cancer because of counterfeit drugs. The Department should clear the air on the matter by issuing a press release or holding a press conference. If counterfeit cancer drugs were indeed seized, the government should release the names of the drugs and the hospitals possibly affected. If not, it should at least communicate the same to the public. Letting the uncertainty hang without authoritative answers is not in public interest.

articles.title: India needs a comprehensive doctrine on space security
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: India’s objective should not be to turn outer space into another arena of conflict, but to ensure that disruption in space does not translate into vulnerability on Earth

Space has transformed from a specialised domain of scientific exploration into an area which hosts essential infrastructure underpinning everyday life, economic activity and national security. Communications, navigation, weather forecasting, disaster management, agriculture, banking, logistics and critical infrastructure are increasingly dependent on satellites and space-enabled services. In India, space capabilities support the armed forces through communications, positioning, surveillance, timing and situational awareness. Space is therefore no longer a separate technological sector but an essential component of national resilience and strategic autonomy. As dependence expands, disruption can have consequences for markets, governance, security and society at large.

The character of threats in space is changing. Competition extends beyond the destruction of satellites to the disruption of the services they provide. Space systems can now be affected by jamming and spoofing that interfere with communications and navigation. Cyber interference can target satellite networks, ground stations and supporting infrastructure, while electronic warfare can degrade signals and reduce the reliability of space-enabled systems. Such methods can produce effects without physically damaging a spacecraft, making attribution and response more complex. The vulnerability lies not only in the satellite itself, but in the wider architecture connecting space assets to users on Earth. This shift from destruction to disruption has made space security a more complex challenge for states.

India’s objective should not be to turn outer space into another arena of conflict, but to ensure that disruption in space does not translate into vulnerability on Earth

Space has transformed from a specialised domain of scientific exploration into an area which hosts essential infrastructure underpinning everyday life, economic activity and national security. Communications, navigation, weather forecasting, disaster management, agriculture, banking, logistics and critical infrastructure are increasingly dependent on satellites and space-enabled services. In India, space capabilities support the armed forces through communications, positioning, surveillance, timing and situational awareness. Space is therefore no longer a separate technological sector but an essential component of national resilience and strategic autonomy. As dependence expands, disruption can have consequences for markets, governance, security and society at large.

The character of threats in space is changing. Competition extends beyond the destruction of satellites to the disruption of the services they provide. Space systems can now be affected by jamming and spoofing that interfere with communications and navigation. Cyber interference can target satellite networks, ground stations and supporting infrastructure, while electronic warfare can degrade signals and reduce the reliability of space-enabled systems. Such methods can produce effects without physically damaging a spacecraft, making attribution and response more complex. The vulnerability lies not only in the satellite itself, but in the wider architecture connecting space assets to users on Earth. This shift from destruction to disruption has made space security a more complex challenge for states.

articles.title: Transgender rights, healthcare should not be compromised
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Clinical understanding of the care needs of a transgender person remains rudimentary in India. Doctors, nurses, receptionists, security staff and hospital administrators need to be trained in basic transgender health.

Parliament passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026 earlier this year. The new Act represents a significant shift from the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019. The 2026 amendment removes the principle of self-identification and demands a medical board’s recommendation; a selection from prescribed categories; and certification by a District Magistrate. It fundamentally changes legal recognition for transgender persons from self-identification to medical assessment. While the 2026 Act does increase protection, it changes the philosophical foundation of transgender rights — from recognition based substantially on autonomy and self-identification towards recognition mediated by medical and administrative authorities.

The definition of “transgender” as introduced in the Amendment Act is in contradiction to established international evidence and guidelines laid down in the World Health Organization ICD-11 and the World Professional Association for Transgender Health Standards of Care Version 8.

articles.title: Prince William says Gen Z is the torchbearer of the global movement for change
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Himalayan Kingdom of Bhutan, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility among the five winners of Earthshot Prize

Young people from around the world are not waiting for someone else to find the solution, they are the torchbearers of the global movement for change, Britain’s Prince William said in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
He was speaking at the 2026 Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony, which was held in India for the first time.

“India is a nation of extraordinary innovation, ambition, facing immense environmental pressures, yet moving ahead with determination. Not because the challenge is simple, not because the path is easy. But because millions of people have decided that progress simply cannot wait,” said Prince William.
Winners of the Earthshot Prize award were declared under five categories in a glittering ceremony. The awardees include the Himalayan Kingdom of Bhutan and Mahindra Last Mile Mobility.
“They [Gen Z] are bringing fresh ideas and showing what is possible when optimism is matched with action. Their ideas, their energy, and their determination are helping to shape the future,” he said.
During his address, Prince William reflected on the achievements of this year’s finalists and the growing global movement behind environmental innovation.
The ceremony was attended by environmental innovators, philanthropists, business leaders, government representatives and global figures from sport, entertainment and culture.
Mahindra Last Mile Mobility won the Earthshot Prize in the ‘Clean Our Air’ category. Accepting the award, the company’s CEO, Suman Mishra, said it showed how urgent optimism worked.
The company has won 1 million pounds for its efforts, due to which 33 per cent of India’s three-wheelers are now electric.
Prince Williams and Princess Catherine meet the winners of Earthshot Prize post the award ceremony in Mumbai on November 17, 2026. | Photo Credit: Emmanual Yogini
In the ‘Revive Our Oceans’ category, Niue Ocean Wide Trust was chosen for protecting the oceans, especially the vast Pacific region.
Coral Pasisi, vice chair and co-architect of Ocean Conservation Commitments, expressed gratitude for indigenous, people-led sustainability efforts being honoured.

articles.title: Kedarnath generates 73 tonnes of waste during 2026 Char Dham Yatra
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around 65.65 lakh pilgrims visit four Char Dham shrines and Hemkund Sahib in 2026 as Badrinath portals close for winter

Pilgrims visiting the Kedarnath shrine generated 73 tonnes of waste during the 2026 Char Dham Yatra, more than three times the amount recorded last year. The yatra, which ended on Monday (November 16, 2026) with the closure of the Badrinath shrine portals, witnessed a record 65.65 lakh pilgrims this year.
According to data shared by the civic body at Kedarnath, the 73 tonnes of waste comprised plastic bottles, food packets, Tetra Pak, and cardboard.
Neeraj Kukreti, an official of the Kedarnath Nagar Panchayat, told The Hindu that waste generation this year was more than three times the 21.40 tonnes recorded in 2025.
The waste generated in Kedarnath stood at 26.10 tonnes in 2024 and 32.58 tonnes in 2023, he added.

To help manage the waste buildup near the temple, the district administration launched the ‘Carry Me Back’ initiative in June. The drive mobilised over 6,000 pilgrims to carry 14 tonnes of waste down to a collection point, from where it was sent for segregation and disposal.”

The increase in waste generation comes amid a broader rise in pilgrim numbers across Uttarakhand’s Char Dham circuit, according to a comparative analysis released by the Dehradun-based SDC Foundation.

Prepared by Anoop Nautiyal and Praveen Upreti, the study found that 65.65 lakh pilgrims visited the four Char Dham shrines — Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri and Yamunotri — and Hemkund Sahib in 2026, registering a 29% increase over 51.07 lakh in 2025. The pilgrimage season extended from mid-April to mid-November.

Kedarnath recorded 19,33,138 pilgrims, a 9% rise over the previous year. However, its average daily footfall declined by around 6%, from 10,113 pilgrims in 2025 to 9,476 in 2026. The foundation attributed the higher cumulative numbers partly to a longer pilgrimage season and fewer weather-related disruptions. Kedarnath remained operational for 204 days, compared with 175 days last year.

The SDC Foundation report also flagged concerns over pilgrim safety, recording 297 fatalities across the five shrines in 2026, compared with 182 in 2025. Health-related natural deaths alone increased by 81%, from 159 to 288, with Kedarnath accounting for 142 such deaths.

Vehicle movement during the Char Dham Yatra also witnessed a significant rise, increasing from 5,14,016 in 2025 to 6,68,877 in 2026 (till November 14). This represents an increase of 1,54,861 vehicles, or more than 30% over the previous year.

“The sharp rise in vehicle numbers reflects the growing pressure on pilgrimage infrastructure, road networks, traffic management, road safety and healthcare services. These trends underline the urgent need for strengthened safety measures, improved traffic management and a more coordinated, data-driven approach to ensuring a safe and sustainable Char Dham Yatra,” said Mr. Nautiyal.

He stressed that Uttarakhand must move beyond the pursuit of record-breaking pilgrim numbers and focus on carrying capacity, pilgrim health, sustainability and the long-term future of the Char Dham Yatra.

articles.title: Won’t allow hiring of outsiders, hire locals: J&K CM Omar Abdullah to outside companies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He made the statement during the inauguration of development projects worth ₹30 crores in Jammu, Samba and Kathua districts
Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) said that companies from the outside must hire locals and that hiring outsiders will not be allowed.

“The excuse that trained youths are not available will not work. We will provide you (companies) six months or one year and prepare our youths. We also have ITIs (Industrial Training Institutes), polytechnics, colleges, and universities,” said Mr. Abdullah.
The J&K Chief Minister said youths from J&K have no shortage of talent. “They (youths) only need opportunities. We will not tolerate excuses at the cost of our children’s future,” said Mr. Abdullah.
He made the statement during the inauguration of development projects worth ₹30 crores in Jammu, Samba and Kathua districts.

Stating that youngsters from J&K were demonstrating their capabilities in different fields, Mr. Abdullah said, “Wherever you look, you will find young people from J&K serving the country. The moment they get a chance, they leave their mark.”
He said his government was putting in efforts “to ensure development works across the entire region”.

On the current status of Union Territory (UT), Mr. Abdullah said, “We did not become a UT by choice. This situation would never have arisen if it were up to us. The Central Government has put us in this difficult situation. Working under these circumstances is not easy. However, I am not someone who makes excuses based on the prevailing circumstances.”

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jharkhand CEO K Ravi Kumar appeals to all eligible Indian citizens in the state to ensure their names are included in the electoral roll by taking part in Ek Aur Avsar (One More Opportunity) camps

Jharkhand Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) K. Ravi Kumar on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) appealed to all eligible Indian citizens in the State to ensure their names are included in the electoral roll being published under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

Speaking to the media in Ranchi, Mr. Ravi asserted that an “Ek Aur Avsar” (One More Opportunity) camp will be held on November 18 at all polling stations in the State, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., where meetings of BLOs (Booth Level Officers) and BLAs-2 (Booth Level Agents-2) will take place in the form of a “Chunav Pathshala” (Electoral Awareness Session).

He pointed out that the objective of this special initiative is to provide one additional opportunity for any eligible Indian citizen who, for various reasons, has not yet had their name added to the electoral roll.

Mr. Ravi explained that the camps will focus primarily on three key areas. First, the Election Commission of India (ECI) is republishing the ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead, or Duplicate) list at all polling stations. If any eligible Indian citizen has been included in this list, they may follow the prescribed procedure to submit Form-6 or an enumeration form.

Second, lists of voters in categories such as “No Mapping” or those with “Logical Discrepancies”—who have failed to provide the necessary documentation despite receiving two notices from the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) and undergoing a door-to-door verification process—will be made available at the respective polling stations.

Third, efforts are being made to identify eligible Indian citizens who will have turned 18 by October 1, 2026, but who have not yet registered their names in the electoral roll for their respective polling stations. Eligible Indian citizens will be able to have their names included in the electoral roll by submitting Form 6.

The CEO said that this is the sixth and final BLO-BLA-2 meeting being held under the ongoing SIR process in Jharkhand. He urged all eligible citizens in the state to take advantage of this opportunity and get their names added to the electoral roll, ensuring that no eligible Indian citizen remains excluded.

The ECI has already extended the deadline for final publication of electoral rolls in Jharkhand under the SIR to November 30. The final publication was initially scheduled for October 7 and was later extended to October 19 before being revised.

articles.title: Construction activities on Kaziranga wildlife corridors flagged
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: An Eastern Assam-based environment activist writes to the Supreme Court-constituted Central Empowered Committee, highlighting the concerns

An eastern Assam-based environmental activist has reminded the Supreme Court–constituted Central Empowered Committee (CEC) to continue construction activities on the wildlife corridors of Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve.

Kaziranga has nine notified wildlife corridors and several dandis or animal pathways. Animals use these corridors and dandis mostly to escape to the hills of Karbi Anglong district when the park is flooded during the monsoon months.

In a letter to the CEC’s Member-Secretary on November 16, Rohit Choudhury said he had brought such construction activities to the notice of the Committee on May 11. He lamented the lack of action against these activities, violating the Supreme Court’s April 2019 order.

“We order that all kinds of mining and related activities along the aforesaid Kaziranga National Park area and in the entire catchment area of rivers, streams and rivulets originating in the Karbi Anglong Hill ranges and flowing into Kaziranga National Park, including the Tiger Reserve, are restrained. No new construction shall be permitted on private lands which form part of the nine identified animal corridors,” the apex court’s order read.

“Despite this clear and categorical prohibition, the Government of Assam has displayed a disturbing disregard for the mandate of the Supreme Court by permitting and facilitating unlawful construction activities within these ecologically sensitive wildlife corridors,” Mr. Choudhury wrote.

He reminded the CEC of photographic evidence of a building under construction on the Haldhibari Wildlife Corridor attached to his May 11 letter. “The construction activity was allowed to proceed unabated and has now reached an advanced stage of completion,” he wrote, attaching recent photographs of the construction site.

Mr. Choudhury said the CEC’s inability to take up the matter six months ago “effectively afforded the concerned authorities sufficient time to continue and substantially complete the illegal construction”.
He said such delays in addressing matters of grave environmental significance seriously undermine the purpose and efficacy of the CEC’s mandate.
The activist further said the Assam Government did not inform the Supreme Court of any instance of violation of its April 12, 2019, order for necessary action.

“This persistent failure of enforcement has emboldened continued violations and weakened the protection envisaged by the Supreme Court,” he said, urging the CEC to recommend contempt proceedings against the officials responsible for permitting, facilitating or failing to prevent these blatant violations of the court’s binding directions.

“The matter concerns not merely a breach of judicial orders but the continued degradation of one of India’s most treasured ecological landscapes and a globally recognised natural heritage site. Immediate intervention is therefore both necessary and imperative,” Mr. Choudhury wrote.

articles.title: Russian military transport plane crashes in Siberia, killing 19: Defence Ministry
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The An-12 aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000 kilometres (about 1,860 miles) east of Moscow

A Russian military transport plane crashed in western Siberia on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), killing all 19 people on board, the Defence Ministry said. Preliminary findings pointed to equipment failure.

The An-12 aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000 kilometres (about 1,860 miles) east of Moscow. Air force experts were investigating the cause of the crash. The An-12 typically has a crew of six.
Kemerovo Gov. Ilya Serdyuk said the plane crashed near the village of Yagunovo, which is close to Kemerovo airport. “Emergency responders put out a fire on the site of the crash,” he said.
The Investigative Committee, the country’s top criminal investigation agency, launched an inquiry into possible violations of flight safety rules, a standard practice following crashes.
The An-12 is a Soviet-built four-engine turboprop transport plane that has been in service since the late 1950s. Over 1,000 were built and some still remain in operation in Russia and other nations.

articles.title: U.K. hands NATO-assigned American soldier accused of Russia spying to U.S.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner

A senior American soldier assigned to NATO who was arrested in Britain last week on suspicion of spying for Russia has been transferred to U.S. military custody, U.K. police said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The espionage case, the latest involving suspected Kremlin agents in Britain and elsewhere in Europe, comes amid heightened tensions between Moscow and various European capitals after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
It also follows recent security scares at two British air force bases hosting the U.S. military, with officials accusing Iran of involvement in plots to target them.
A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner.

Held in British police custody since his November 10 arrest near Gloucester, southwest England, he was handed to the US military “over suspected national security and espionage allegations”, U.K. Counter Terrorism Policing said.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor said the decision to “pass the investigation to them to progress” followed an extensive probe by his counter-terror unit and subsequent discussions between British prosecutors and “American partners”.
FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that the unnamed Army officer was in U.S. custody after “an espionage investigation”.
He noted it had involved “close cooperation” between the FBI’s Philadelphia field office and various other US and UK law enforcement and intelligence agencies.
“Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action,” Mr. Patel added.

A senior NATO military official last week confirmed that the arrested soldier had been assigned to its Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC), the alliance’s 20-nation, high-readiness force led by the British Army.
Based at Imjin Barracks near Gloucester, it can deploy at short notice anywhere in Europe or globally under the direct operational command of NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe.
Imjin is also just a few miles from the U.K.’s highly sensitive GCHQ intelligence, security and cyber agency headquarters.

articles.title: All-too fallible: On India’s vote against moratorium on death penalty
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Death penalty requires a near-infallible criminal justice system

India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . articles.title: Cancel wetland excavation project in eastern Assam grazing grounds, CM urged
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: People from villages in Jorhat district’s Teok region staged a protest in Guwahati, demanding a halt to the ongoing project across 7,598 bighas

Farmers and fishing community members in eastern Assam’s Teok region have urged Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to scrap an ongoing “anti-people” project in “historic” grazing grounds and natural wetlands. They submitted a memorandum to the Chief Minister after staging a sit-in protest in Guwahati on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) against the project being implemented “in the guise of” a Flood Mitigation by Capacity Augmentation of Wetlands scheme.

The Teok Ban Niskashan Nala Khanan Dabi Samiti, a collective of villagers around the 7,598 bighas (almost 2,512 acres) under excavation, organised the protest. They said the authorities began implementing the project in January without any open public hearings, independent Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), Social Impact Assessment (SIA) or public consent.
Located in Jorhat district, Teok is about 330 km east of Guwahati.

The Hindu had reported on the first resistance in February-March after police served a notice to Debanga Sourav Gogoi, the Samiti’s advisor, for allegedly instigating villagers against the project involving the grazing grounds and the Jelengitup-Ghorachowa, Kenduguri, Garchiga and Kawaimari wetlands.
These wetlands are located within 5 km of the Brahmaputra River’s southern bank.
The Teok Ban Niskashan Nala Khanan Dabi Samiti, a collective of villagers around the 7,598 bighas under excavation, organised the protest on November 18, 2026 | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Mr. Gogoi said representatives from various progressive organisations, farmer organisations, political parties, students’ unions and civil society participated in Tuesday’s protest to express solidarity with the Samiti.

The other organisations and parties included Rabha Hasong, Asom Nagarik Samaj, Bhumi Adhimar Joutha Sangram Samiti, Silsako Uchchhed Protirudhi Raij, Darabil Go-Soroniya Pothar Suraksha Samiti Raijor Dal, Asom Jatiya Parishad, Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist), and Students’ Federation of India.
Samiti president Ramesh Duara said the organisation listed three demands in the memorandum to the Chief Minister.

The organisation wants the government to stop the excavation work; conduct a transparent and open public hearing in each project area involving independent environmental experts, public representatives, agriculturists, livestock farmers, fishermen and other affected citizens; and ensure legal protection of ancestral rights over the grazing grounds and traditional fishing rights in the targeted wetlands.

articles.title: CCMB study points to new way of tackling fungal infections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fungi can gradually develop resistance to current antifungal drugs, making infections increasingly difficult to treat

Scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB), Hyderabad, have identified a promising new strategy to combat fungal infections by preventing disease-causing fungi from becoming invasive, rather than killing them outright.

Most current antifungal drugs work by destroying fungal cells. However, fungi can gradually develop resistance to these medicines, making infections increasingly difficult to treat. A team led by Sriram Varahan at CCMB studied ‘Candida albicans’, a fungus commonly found on human skin and in the body. While generally harmless, it can cause serious infections when it enters the bloodstream or internal organs.

The researchers focused on ‘morphogenesis’, in which the fungus changes from a round-cell form into long, filament-like structures, a transformation allowing the pathogen to evade the body’s immune defences and spread more effectively within tissues.

Earlier studies had shown that glycolysis, the process through which cells metabolise sugar, plays a key role in controlling this shape change. Building on these findings, the team screened a library of small molecules that target glycolysis and identified two compounds capable of blocking the transformation.

Although the fungus continued to grow, it remained in its harmless rounded form suggesting that the compounds could serve as “anti-infective” agents that reduce the fungus’ ability to cause disease without necessarily eliminating it.

The study also identified pyruvate kinase, an enzyme involved in sugar metabolism, as a crucial regulator of fungal morphogenesis. Researchers further found that one of the compounds reduced biofilm formation, a protective layer that helps fungi resist treatment. The compound also increased the effectiveness of widely used antifungal drugs such as fluconazole and amphotericin B.

In a mouse model of systemic Candida infection, treatment with the lead compound significantly improved survival rates, highlighting its potential for future therapeutic development. “Our findings suggest that fungal disease-associated behaviour can be targeted without necessarily stopping fungal growth,” said Dhrumi Shah, first author of the study. “We need further studies to evaluate the compounds effectiveness and safety but by blocking the fungus from becoming invasive, they could complement existing treatments,” said Sriram Varahan.

The findings, published in ACS Infectious Diseases , emerged from a collaboration between CSIR-CCMB and the BRIC-Translational Health Science and Technology Institute, said a press release on Tuesday.

articles.title: Indian national missing after attacks on commercial vessel in Strait of Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: MEA said that of the 24 Indian nationals on board MT Tara Gas, 21 have been safely evacuated

An Indian national went missing and two others sustained injuries after their Panama-flagged vessel came under attack in the Strait of Hormuz this week that triggered a strong condemnation from New Delhi.
The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said that of the 24 Indian nationals on board MT Tara Gas, 21 have been safely evacuated.
"We condemn the attack on the Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT Tara Gas in the Strait of Hormuz on 16 November 16," it said in a statement.
India said the targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end.

"Of the 24 Indian nationals on board, 21 have been safely evacuated ashore at Khasab, two injured Indian crew members have been admitted to hospital, while one Indian national remains missing," it added.
The MEA said the Embassy in Oman is closely monitoring the ongoing search and rescue operations in coordination with the Omani authorities.
"We appreciate the timely assistance and support extended by the Government of Oman in the rescue efforts," it said.
New Delhi said the "continuing incidents of attacks on shipping in the region are deeply worrisome and pose a serious threat to the safety of civilian seafarers."

"The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest," it said in a statement.

articles.title: No mandate only women personnel can ‘handle’ women in crowd-control operations, Delhi Police to SC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police said it was yet to be determined if “reel-makers can be elevated to the status of journalists or reporters”.
The Delhi Police has told the Supreme Court there is no strict rule that only women police officers must “handle” women in crowd-control operations.

The police was responding to allegations of manhandling women protestors and journalists by male police officers during widespread protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar . The allegations were made in petitions by Network of Women in Media, India, represented by advocate Aarthi Rajan, and others like the Delhi Union of Journalists, Free Speech Collective and the Kerala Union of Working Journalists.
The legal requirement that only women police officers could arrest or carry out searches on women was not a mandate in crowd-control situations, the police submitted in an affidavit.

“With regards to the allegations of manhandling of women journalists, it is respectfully submitted that the requirement of women personnel handling women is not a statutory mandate in the context of crowd-control operations, in the same manner as it is expressly prescribed under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 in relation to searches and arrests,” the police said.

The police said the deployment of women personnel in a crowd-control situation was an “operational consideration” depending on various factors, including the need to maintain propriety, avoid unnecessary confrontation and defuse tensions at a protest site, particularly if there were women participants.
The mere presence or involvement of male police personnel in crowd-control operations during the CJP protest cannot, itself, be construed as misconduct.
There is no legal bar on a male police officer from acting as a first responder. Nor is he stopped from assisting a woman police officer in the discharge of her duties.
“Such decisions have to be taken at the fraction of a second,” the police affidavit said.

articles.title: At Deepavali celebration, Mamdani flags targeting of Hindu temples
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The New York mayor said this year's Deepavali also served as a reminder of the work still needed to build a politics rooted in tolerance and compassion

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani flagged the targeting of Hindu temples in the U.S. in recent months and the growing presence of hate in political campaigns, calling on communities to reject divisive politics and stand together against discrimination.

Speaking at a Deepavali celebration he hosted in New York on Tuesday (November 17), Mr. Mamdani said Hindu temples had been targeted over the past year and alleged that leaders at the highest levels of the U.S. federal government had also targeted Sikhs.
He said hatred that was once confined to the margins of society has increasingly found a place at the centre of political campaigns.
"Whether it is fear-mongering in Washington or Delhi, we hold a shared obligation, as we mark this holiday, to reject any politics that brings darkness into this world," the mayor said.

Addressing those whose identity and belonging had been questioned, Mr. Mamdani said, “To anyone who has been told to go back home, whose belonging has been questioned, let me say unequivocally, you are home.”

The mayor, whose mother is Punjabi-Hindu and father a Gujarati Ugandan Muslim, spoke about growing up with a diverse cultural and religious heritage, saying his family had taught him to appreciate the beauty and wisdom of Hinduism.
"Our shared heritage was never a single language, faith, or affiliation. From an early age, my mother's family taught me how much beauty and wisdom lives in Hinduism,” he said.

Describing Hinduism as a faith with many gods and diverse narratives, Mr. Mamdani referred to its scriptures and the idea that there are multiple paths to truth and that the same light resides in everyone, irrespective of whether they worship at a temple, mosque, gurdwara or do not follow a religion.

"It is a faith of many gods... it's a faith whose oldest scripture teaches us that there are many roads to Satya (truth), and that the same light lives in every one of us, whether we pray in a mandir, a masjid, a gurudwara, or nowhere at all,” he said.
Mr. Mamdani also drew upon the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, saying the epics offered lessons on relationships, family, duty and moral responsibility.

“Ramayana shows us the brother, the wife, the husband, and the friend that we aspire to be. The Mahabharata shows us what families are really like, where even the bravest heroes and wisest gods stumble, and where one's Dharma must come before one's loyalty,” he noted.

Mr. Mamdani said the wisdom of these traditions had resonated beyond religious practices and influenced movements for justice across the world, citing Mahatma Gandhi's Salt March and Martin Luther King Jr's March on Washington.

fullParagraphs: What triggered the resurgence of measles in the U.S.? Is vaccine hesitancy putting decades of progress against measles at risk? How is the global measles surge affecting India?

The story so far: After 26 years of holding on to its measles elimination status, the United States lost this distinction. On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organisation (PAHO) revoked the United States’ measles elimination status. This was after over 5400 cases of measles were reported in the U.S. in 2026.

This is the highest annual total since 1989-91, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention(CDC). As per data put out by the Unicef, 96% of cases are in unvaccinated people or those with unknown vaccination status. Children under five account for 18% of cases and those aged 5-19 for 40%.

articles.title: Why Ukraine keeps targeting the Kerch Bridge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Ukraine has targeted the structure several times, latest on November 17, 2026

In 2022, Ukraine bombed the Kerch bridge linking mainland Russia to the Crimean Peninsula, using explosives hidden in a truck. In 2023, naval drones struck the bridge. In 2025, covert Ukrainian operatives planted bombs on its undersea support pillars. But none of these attacks caused major damage to the structure, which Russian President Vladimir Putin described in 2018 as a “miracle”. But earlier this week, two back-to-back Ukrainian attacks, involving drones and missiles, brought down a crucial span of the road bridge and damaged the parallel rail bridge. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed it as an “unprecedented operation”. Russian authorities acknowledged the damage, announcing a suspension of road traffic and restrictions on train services.

The 19-km Kerch bridge , across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, is the longest bridge in Europe, built at a cost of $3.6 billion. It was opened in 2018 by Russian President Vladimir Putin, four years after Russia annexed Crimea from Ukraine through a contested referendum. Mr. Putin drove an orange truck across its length and said “a miracle has come true”.

The bridge is important for Russia for symbolic, administrative and operational reasons. When Russia swiftly moved to annex Crimea in 2014 , after a pro-Russian elected government in Kyiv fell amid West-backed anti-regime protests, there was no direct connectivity between the Russian mainland and the peninsula, which hosts Russia’s Black Sea fleet. Mr. Putin immediately ordered the construction of the bridge. But the bridge remained a weak link as Ukraine grew in military strength, backed by the West, in subsequent years.

This 2017 photo shows the newly installed railroad arch of a road-and-rail bridge under construction to connect the Russian mainland with Crimea, at dawn in the Kerch Strait, Crimea. | Photo Credit: Reuters

When Mr. Putin ordered the invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022 (what Russia calls a ‘special military operation’), one of the military objectives, according to experts, was to secure a “land bridge” from southwest Russia to Crimea, where 77% of the local population identified Russian as their native language. Today, Russia has the land bridge extending from northeastern Ukraine through the Donbas and Kherson to Crimea. But the bridge remains a critical logistical supply link for the Russian troops in the south. And for Crimea, which depends on mainland Russia for much of its food, fuel and consumer goods, the bridge is also an economic lifeline.

If Russia sees the bridge as a symbol of pride, Ukraine sees it as a symbol of occupation. Russia also used Crimea as a launchpad to start its 2022 invasion. That’s why Ukrainians have repeatedly targeted the bridge. The context of the latest attack is also significant. articles.title: Bahrain, Kuwait attacked after U.S. strikes Iranian island
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Bahrain and Kuwait said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) that they had repelled air attacks launched against them following U.S. strikes on an Iranian island, as Gulf nations face retaliatory bombardment in the Middle East war.
The conflict — which began with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February — has spilled over to Gulf states that host U.S. military facilities.

The Iranian army said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) its drones "targeted Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms belonging to the terrorist US military at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait," in a statement carried by state television IRIB.
Kuwait's military said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) its air defences were "responding to hostile drone threats", urging its public to follow security and safety advice.
While Bahrain said its air defences intercepted attacks from Iran early on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), a day after Tehran's Revolutionary Guards said they attacked a base used by Washington.

The United States and Iran are in a standoff over the vital Strait of Hormuz, with the U.S. military working to escort ships transiting the waterway in defiance of Tehran's attempts to close the waterway.
Iran's official IRNA news agency cited a regional official as saying the United States had hit Qeshm Island in the Hormuz strait without causing serious damage.

U.S. fighter jets "used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island", an American official told AFP on condition of anonymity, adding that the strike was in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets".
Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) it had intercepted a cruise missile launched by the Iran-backed group toward the Riyadh area.
Explosions boomed across Bahrain's capital on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) as a mobile phone alert warned residents to seek safety.

Bahrain's armed forces said they "confronted, intercepted and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today... before they could achieve their objectives", while Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a U.S.-operated radar system.

"Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain," the Guards' Sepah news website said.

articles.title: Gilead signs generic licensing deals for experimental Ebola drug
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A late-stage trial is testing the drug in people at high risk after exposure. The deals are intended to line up manufacturing and supply before trial results and regulatory filings

Gilead Sciences said on Monday it had signed royalty-free deals with three generic drugmakers to make its experimental Ebola prevention drug available in 127 mainly low- and lower-middle-income countries if it succeeds in trials and wins regulatory approvals.

The deals with Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories, Eva Pharma and Ferozsons Laboratories cover obeldesivir, and include all African countries reporting cases in the current Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak. Obeldesivir has shown activity against several Ebola-related viruses in preclinical studies but is not approved for any use in any country.
A late-stage trial is testing the drug in people at high risk after exposure. The deals are intended to line up manufacturing and supply before trial results and regulatory filings.

Gilead is also expanding remdesivir licences to cover Ebola-related diseases if trial results are positive and regulators approve the drug. The company has donated more than 38,000 remdesivir vials to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda and Kenya, including more than 2,000 recently sent to Kenya for investigational treatment and post-exposure prevention.
Remdesivir is not approved to treat or prevent Ebola Bundibugyo disease, and its clinical effectiveness has not been established.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Measurements lying in the shadows of their successors can find new lives in the light of new theories. The Voyager 1 mission’s longevity made that more apparent, allowing successive generations of researchers to find more uses for its data even as it continues to collect new information

Today, the Voyager 1 spacecraft will be one light-day away from the earth. This means a signal travelling at the speed of light will take one full day to go from the earth to Voyager 1, and signals from the spacecraft will similarly take one day to reach receivers on the earth.

This is a tremendous distance — almost 26 billion kilometres. Since February 17, 1998, Voyager 1 has been the farthest any space mission has been from us. And it keeps going at 61,000 km/hr. But even at such breathtaking speed, Voyager 1 is still barely out of the solar system. Each star’s gravitational and magnetic fields extend out for billions of kilometres around them, bending the destinies of multiple worlds to their stellar will.

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on November 18: What does it mean?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: NASA’s Voyager 1, humanity’s farthest spacecraft, is about to reach one light-day from Earth, more than 16 billion miles away; Know what it means

NASA’s Voyager 1 is set to cross a historic threshold in space exploration as it is about to become humanity’s first object to reach one light-day from Earth. The iconic probe, which has travelled farther from Earth than any other human-made object since its launch in 1977, is expected to cross the landmark on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (3:46:07 p.m. IST), according to NASA.
Infographics: Voyager I’s 49-year journey into the void
Having spent 49 years, two months and 11 days hurtling through the cosmos, Voyager 1 continues to push the boundaries of human space exploration.

One light-day is a staggering measure of distance, rather than a measure of time. It represents the exact space that light, which travels at roughly 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometres) per second, covers in a full 24-hour period.
For Voyager 1, this is equivalent to more than 16 billion miles away from Earth.
When Voyager 1 reaches that incredible milestone on November 18, its radio signals will take precisely 24 hours travelling at the speed of light to reach Earth — in other words, one light-day.

Sunlight takes just over eight minutes to reach Earth, and over four hours and 10 minutes to reach Neptune. From November 18, any radio command sent from NASA’s Deep Space Network to Voyager 1 will take a full 24 hours to arrive, requiring another 24 hours for the spacecraft’s response to return.

Launched on September 2, 1977, Voyager 1 was originally designed for a four-year mission to study Jupiter and Saturn. Its trajectory eventually allowed it to overtake its twin, Voyager 2, which was launched 16 days earlier. According to NASA, Voyager 2 is expected to reach the one-light-day distance from Earth in November 2035.

The two spacecrafts were launched to explore the outer planets, with Voyager 1 taking a trajectory that eventually carried it towards interstellar space. It became the first spacecraft that entered the interstellar space in August 2012 and has continued transmitting information from beyond the solar system. Today, it speeds onward at roughly 38,000 miles per hour.
In 1990, Voyager 1 captured the most distant image of Earth, known as the iconic “Pale Blue Dot,” while venturing farther than any other human-made object beyond Neptune.
NASA said Voyager 1 is currently travelling in the direction of a star known as AC +79 3888, or Gliese 445, located more than 17 light-years from Earth in the constellation Ursa Minor.

Powered by decaying plutonium generators, Voyager 1 loses a small amount of electrical power every year. With this plutonium supply continually depleting, both probes lose about 4 watts of power each year.

articles.title: This 2D rhythm platformer video game is an ode to India’s multiplicities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Suri: The Seventh Note by Tathvamasi Studios is set in a universe controlled by evil music. The game was launched in October

The story of Suri: The Seventh Note, a 2D video game by Bengaluru-based Tathvamasi Studios, is set in a world corrupted by an evil version of music. Everything in this universe moves in tune with that nefarious sonic presence. The protagonist, Ajira, must find a fruit located at the centre of the island to save her mother from certain death. Soon, she realises her actions shall determine the fate of the island itself.

Suri: The Seventh Note is the brainchild of Glen Martin from Kochi, founder of Tathvamasi Studios, who is also the game director of the video. He is joined by Chitrak Srivastava, co-founder and the game’s art director. The game was launched on Playstation Store and Steam, in October for PlayStations and PCs.

Glen, formerly a data scientist, found himself immersed in game-making during the pandemic. He began by making smaller games, with friends from different places joining him on a Discord server to help. “When we started to build the game, it was not meant to be a project. But once we realised its potential, we began to think about what could be unique about this game,” says Glen.
Glen Martin and Chitrak Srivastava | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

“At that point, I was playing a parry-focused combat game called Sekiro. It’s a very hard game, and I am not good at it. But then I saw a lot of streamers play the game skilfully, without even taking a single hit, and I realised that when the game is played at that level, it has a certain rhythmic quality to it,” he adds. “The sounds of the sword clinking, the jumps and movements, everything felt choreographed.”
This ultimately led him to turn Suri… into a rhythm platformer game.

Suri... is a mix of two different games: rhythm and platformer. Rhythm games are music-themed action games that assess a player’s sense of timing and metre, while platformers are a sub-genre where a main character moves through uneven terrain and suspended platforms.

“There are very few games that I’ve done this before, so our well of references was limited. In Suri..., the world moves to the rhythm. All the things that you would normally interact with in a regular platformer, like traps, obstacles, etc., are all tied to the rhythm in our game. You have to listen to the music to understand when a thing would move up and down or when a leaf would open or close and so on,” explains Glen. “When done well, it feels like dancing through levels.”

In 2024, Suri was one of five games at the inaugural edition of PlayStation’s India Hero Project, an incubator programme from Sony Interactive Entertainment. This ultimately allowed Glen to quit his job and hire more people.
A still from Suri: The Seventh Note | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

One of the most intriguing aspects about Suri is the world it is set in. “Suri is set in our own version of mythical India. While we are inspired by Indian ethos and culture, we have not tried to mimic it or take things from it directly. We’ve tried to create our own world,” says Glen.

Chitrak says, “We wanted to create something that belongs to those places we grew up in. Usually when you play these games, they mostly have European or Japanese settings. We wanted to find something that we could relate to and have the world explore that side of our culture. That was the north star for us, while we began developing this world.”

articles.title: One in five women in parts of Northeast deficient in vitamin B1: ICMR-NIN study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Vitamin B1 or Thiamine is an essential micronutrient that supports energy metabolism and healthy nervous system function

Around one in five pregnant and lactating women in Assam’s Barak Valley and adjoining districts of Tripura suffer from suboptimal levels of ‘Thiamine’ (vitamin B1), according to a study by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN), Hyderabad, highlighting a continuing public health concern in the region.

The study, ‘Re-Emergence of Thiamine Deficiency Among Pregnant and Lactating Women in Northeast India’, published in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, examined the prevalence of thiamine deficiency and its link to dietary practices in areas where beriberi cases have previously been reported, said a press release on Monday.

Researchers conducted the community-based study during 2023-24 among 1,083 women from 120 villages in Assam’s Barak Valley and neighbouring parts of Tripura. Thiamine status was assessed using biochemical and functional indicators to determine the extent of deficiency.

The findings showed that about 20% of participants had inadequate thiamine levels. Based on blood thiamine measurements, 4.9% were deficient, and 15.2% had marginal levels. A separate functional assessment produced similar results, with 8.5% showing severe deficiency and 12.1% marginal deficiency. Pregnant women were found to be more vulnerable than lactating mothers.

Thiamine is an essential micronutrient that supports energy metabolism and healthy nervous system function. Deficiency can lead to serious health complications, making adequate intake particularly important during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

According to Mahesh Kumar Mummadi, NIN scientist and lead author of the study, dietary assessments revealed that most women consumed rice-based diets with limited diversity. Practices such as consuming stored rice, repeatedly washing rice before cooking, chewing betel nut and drinking salted tea were associated with a higher risk of deficiency.

NIN director Bharati Kulkarni said the findings underscore the need to look beyond routinely monitored nutrients in maternal health programmes. She called for greater dietary diversity, regular nutritional surveillance and targeted supplementation in high-risk regions. Researchers also noted that since the study focused on areas with previously reported beriberi clusters, the findings may not be representative of all pregnant and lactating women across India.

articles.title: Season’s first ground frost recorded in the Nilgiris
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Temperatures between 5°C and 6°C were recorded in the higher elevations of the district

The first seasonal ground frost was recorded in the Nilgiris on the intervening night of Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and Wednesday (November 18), as temperatures between 5°C and 6°C were recorded in the higher elevations of the district.

While frost usually sets in in late November or early December, the season was extremely delayed in 2025. However, the delay in the onset of ground frost led to colder weather in the early part of that year, with many places, especially Thalakundha, becoming tourist hotspots as the area was blanketed by ground frost.
While frost usually sets in in late November or early December, the season was extremely delayed in 2025 | Photo Credit: M. Sathyamoorthy

According to officials, ground frost was seen early Wednesday morning in the low-lying parts of Ooty town surrounding Ooty lake, as well as in Thalakundha, Khandal, and a few other areas. Temperature gauges recorded lows of anywhere between 5°C and 6°C.

Over the last few years, pictures of the district’s annual ground frost have led to an increase in tourism footfall in the district, with visitors keen to witness this weather phenomenon, which occurs when ground temperatures fall below freezing, causing ice crystals to form from condensed water vapour and creating the illusion of snow carpeting open expanses, particularly grasslands.

Over the last few years, pictures of the district’s annual ground frost have led to an increase in tourism footfall in the district, with visitors keen to witness this weather phenomenon | Photo Credit: M. Sathyamoorthy

The ground-frost season also has ecological implications, with the phenomenon helping to curtail the spread of invasive species into the upper Nilgiris, as many species of invasive flora are unable to tolerate the extreme cold that native and endemic species have evolved to withstand and thrive in.
