articles.title: Over 50 students of Keralam school hospitalised after suspected pollution from tar-mixing unit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Panchayat authorities had earlier issued a stop memo against the tar-mixing plant located close to the school in Kollam. However, it resumed operations after obtaining court permission, local residents claimed

Around 50 students of Auxilium ISC School at Kottiyam in Kollam district of Keralam were rushed to a nearby private hospital on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) afternoon after experiencing acute health distress, including severe breathing difficulties, nausea, and vomiting. The sudden medical emergency sparked panic among parents and school authorities, prompting an immediate evacuation of the affected classrooms.

Local residents and parents have strongly alleged that toxic fumes emanating from a tar-mixing unit located in close proximity to the school campus triggered the incident. According to them, thick smoke began drifting into the school premises shortly after the facility resumed operations earlier in the day.

This is not the first time the industrial unit has been linked to health hazards in the area. In a similar incident previously, more than 10 students from the same school were hospitalised with identical symptoms. Following public outcry and protests from parents at the time, the panchayat had issued a formal stop memo, forcing the unit to suspend its operations.

However, tensions flared again on Wednesday morning when the tar-mixing plant reopened after securing a favourable court order. Within hours of the machinery starting up, dozens of children began falling ill.
“We warned the authorities that restarting this unit would put our children’s lives at risk. How can a court order override the basic right of these children to breathe clean air?” a parent asked.

Echoing the sentiment, a local resident demanded permanent closure of the facility. “The panchayat issued a stop memo earlier because the pollution was unbearable. After they restarted the plant this morning, ambulances were rushing our children to the hospital. We will not allow this unit to function here anymore,” he said.
Hospital authorities confirmed that the admitted students are currently under close medical observation and their condition is reported to be stable.

articles.title: Annamalai flays TVK-led govt. over delay in appointing Cauvery technical cell vice-chairman
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The delay in filling such a crucial position raises questions about the government’s administrative efficiency and sense of responsibility, he says

We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) termed as unacceptable the delay in appointing the vice-chairman of the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing by the Tamil Nadu government.

In a post on X, Mr. Annamalai said the resignation of M. Selvaraj, who served as vice-chairman of the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing, was accepted on June 28, 2026. However, the Government Order (G.O.) to fill this post was issued only on October 9, 2026. Even more than a month after the issuance of the G.O., there is no information so far on the appointment of a new vice-chairman.

The delay in filling such a crucial position, which plays a significant role in safeguarding Tamil Nadu’s water rights and dealing with inter-State river water disputes, raises questions about the government’s administrative efficiency and sense of responsibility. This is not an ordinary administrative post but one that involves important technical and legal responsibilities in protecting Tamil Nadu’s water rights, he said.

On the one hand, farmers in the Cauvery delta districts are worried over the lack of adequate water for Samba cultivation. On the other, the Cauvery water-sharing dispute continues, while Karnataka’s proposed Mekedatu dam project remains a challenge to Tamil Nadu’s rights. “At a time when the State is confronted with several such critical issues, the vacancy in the key post of vice-chairman of the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing is nothing but a serious administrative failure,” he said.

Reports have emerged that Tamil Nadu Ministers N. Anand and Aadhav Arjuna are set to meet the Union Minister for Jal Shakti and submit a representation on the Mekedatu dam issue. “Does the TVK government believe that meeting a Union Minister and submitting a representation alone will resolve these issues, without strengthening the State’s own administrative machinery and making timely appointments to key positions?” Mr. Annamalai questioned.

Such administrative delays and lack of accountability by the TVK government in matters of such significance, which concern the livelihoods of farmers and Tamil Nadu’s water rights, are wholly unacceptable, he added.

articles.title: DC inspects public parks in Yadgir, orders anti-encroachment drive and formation of ward committees
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Amid widespread complaints that open public spaces were being encroached upon due to the lack of boundary walls, Mr. Pandve stressed the need for immediate protective measures.

​To curb the encroachment of government land, rejuvenate public parks, and expedite the resolution of civic issues, Yadgir Deputy Commissioner Rahul Pandve has directed the City Municipal Council (CMC) Commissioner to constitute citizen committees across every ward in the city.

​Accompanied by Superintendent of Police Pruthvik Shankar and CMC Commissioner Umesh Chavan, the Deputy Commissioner conducted a spot inspection of several public parks in Gandhi Nagar and Wards 25 and 26 on Monday (November 16) morning to assess their present condition.

​Taking serious note of widespread complaints that open public spaces were being encroached upon due to the lack of boundary walls around hundreds of parks in the city, Mr. Pandve stressed the need for immediate protective measures.

As a priority, he instructed the CMC Commissioner to immediately construct a compound wall, undertake sapling plantation, and install a signage board at the park located on the stretch leading to Gandhi Nagar.

​Emphasising participatory governance to enhance the city’s aesthetics and address local civic grievances effectively, the Deputy Commissioner directed officials to form dedicated ward-level committees without delay. He specified that these panels must be inclusive, comprising senior citizens, advocates, youth, women, and intellectuals, and must begin functioning immediately.

​During the inspection, local residents interacted with the Deputy Commissioner, the Superintendent of Police, and the CMC Commissioner to highlight pressing civic issues in their respective neighbourhoods.
​CMC Engineer Rakesh Reddy, Environmental Engineer Prashanth, and staff member Sharanamma were present during the visit.

articles.title: Andhra’s first semiconductor plant to come up near Visakhapatnam with ₹2,387 crore investment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The chip assembly and testing unit at Tarluvada is the State’s first project under the India Semiconductor Mission and will create 1,000 jobs

Andhra Pradesh is set to mark its entry into the high-technology semiconductor manufacturing sector with Advanced System In Package Technologies Private Limited establishing an Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facility at Tarluvada village in Anandapuram mandal of Visakhapatnam district.

Cleared with a total proposed investment of ₹2,387.81 crore across two phases, the facility is projected to generate direct employment for 1,000 people, beginning with an outlay of ₹542.19 crore and 200 jobs in Phase I, followed by ₹1,845.61 crore and 800 jobs in Phase II.

In the global microelectronics value chain, an OSAT unit performs the crucial back-end stages of chip production. It takes fabricated silicon wafers and carries out precision assembly, protective encapsulation and rigorous electrical testing before the finished integrated circuits are deployed in mobile devices, telecommunications gear, consumer electronics and automotive systems.

Approved by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) on August 20, 2025, the Tarluvada plant holds strategic significance as the first ISM-sanctioned project to be grounded in Andhra Pradesh.

By building domestic capacity in chip packaging and testing, the project addresses a critical link in India’s semiconductor supply chain while anchoring a high-value electronics ecosystem on the east coast.

To expedite the project, the State government has rolled out an extensive package of fiscal, land and infrastructure support under the Andhra Pradesh Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy (4.0), 2024–29. Following clearance by the State Council of Ministers on February 24, 2026, the Information Technology, Electronics and Communications (IT, E&C) Department issued formal orders on February 27, 2026, treating the venture as a “special case” in view of its status as the State’s maiden ISM project.

Under the order, the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC) will allot 30 acres of land at Tarluvada at a nominal rate of ₹1 per acre. The State will also extend special incentives of up to 40% of the project cost on a pari passu basis alongside the Government of India’s 50% grant disbursement.

Additionally, APIIC has been entrusted with developing external infrastructure, including approach roads, power and water supply, funded through the IT, E&C Department, while the Revenue, Energy and Municipal Administration and Urban Development departments, along with the Visakhapatnam District Collector, VMRDA and APEPDCL, have been instructed to work in tandem for early execution.
State IT Secretary Katamneni Bhaskar said regulatory hurdles had been cleared at both the State and Central levels to facilitate rapid execution.

“Work has started on the ground. All statutory clearances have been issued proactively by the State government, and the Government of India has also approved all clearances on its end. The company now has to speed up the works on the ground to complete the project on time,” Mr. Bhaskar told The Hindu .

articles.title: U.S. proposes tougher rules for employment-based green cards, longer hiring process
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Proposed changes would extend advertising periods, curb tailoring of jobs to foreign workers, shift to online recruitment, and increase scrutiny of employers’ efforts to hire Americans before sponsoring visas

The U.S. has proposed stricter rules for employment-based green cards for foreign workers to ensure that Americans get priority in recruitment for jobs ranging from physical therapists and nurses to highly skilled professionals.

The Department of Labour on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) proposed a new rule to modernise the labour market test under the Programme Electronic Review Management (PERM) immigrant visa process, the first major revision of the rules in 20 years.
Under the proposed changes, employers would be prohibited from tailoring job opportunities to foreign workers.
The proposed rule would require employers to level the playing field when recruiting workers by using the same channels and methods when advertising jobs.
The proposal seeks to replace traditional print advertisements with online recruitment through employer websites, job portals, social media platforms, job fairs and campus recruitment.

It would also extend the minimum period for advertising vacancies from the existing 30 days to 90 calendar days and require employers to demonstrate that they had made genuine efforts to recruit qualified American workers.
“This proposed rule change will ensure American workers are first in line for high-skilled, high-paying job opportunities over foreign labour,” Secretary of Labour Keith Sonderling said.
The department also proposed to eliminate the administrative exemption that allowed employers to bypass the statutory labour market test for certain occupations.

Under the revised framework, employers recruiting for physical therapists, nurses, and positions requiring exceptional ability in the sciences or arts would have to consider qualified American applicants.

The proposal also seeks to strengthen safeguards for American workers who have been laid off. Employers would be required to continue considering qualified laid-off workers throughout the labour certification and immigrant petition processes.
Comment | The U.S.’s immigration blocks as a self-defeating path
It would bar certain employers who have laid off American workers within the preceding two years from seeking permanent labour certification for the same or similar positions.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank chair backs CEO after reports expose past lapses; Trump calls tax leak ‘illegal’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Reports cite 15 million leaked records reviewed by more than 200 journalists; German Finance Minister calls for authorities to investigate

Deutsche Bank’s chairman backed ​his CEO Christian Sewing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) after a huge cache of leaked internal records renewed scrutiny ⁠of the German lender’s past dealings with clients including Russian oligarchs, U.S. President Donald Trump and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The reports, compiled by a consortium of international journalists and published by outlets including Der Spiegel , the Financial Times , the New York Times and Le ‌Monde , examined Deutsche Bank’s dealings with Mr. Trump, Epstein and Russian oligarchs, including its pursuit of business in Russia before the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
Deutsche Bank, whose shares fell by as much as 6%, ‌said the matters in the various reports “date back many years”, and that the bank had since strengthened its ‌controls.
Christian Sewing, Chief Executive Officer of Deutsche Bank | Photo Credit: Reuters

“During ⁠my tenure, I haven’t seen a single decision from Christian Sewing that I was not comfortable ⁠with,” Deutsche Bank Chairman Alexander Wynaendts said in an emailed statement. Mr. Sewing has led Germany’s biggest lender since 2018.

The Financial Times reported that Deutsche Bank had inadvertently sent a Trump tax document to another client’s accountant in 2017 when the President was a Deutsche Bank client during his first ​term in office.
Asked in Manila about the ‌error, Mr. Trump said the bank should not have disclosed it. “They shouldn’t have done it. It’s illegal for them to do it,” Mr. Trump said.
Deutsche Bank declined to comment on Mr. Trump’s reaction.

The leaks also showed that Deutsche Bank was ambitious in pursuing business in Russia, including with high-profile oligarchs, right up to the invasion ‌of Ukraine in February 2022, even as some of the bank’s managers voiced concerns over the risks, according ​to the publications.

German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil called on authorities to investigate “and take the necessary action”. Deutsche Bank, he said, needs to explain “with complete transparency” how it has fixed failures and will ⁠prevent new ones.

A member of the European Parliament called on Mr. Sewing to appear before the body to answer questions about the bank’s business practices and control mechanisms. The European Central Bank and the Bank of England’s regulatory arm declined to comment.
The ‌6% share drop was the biggest since April 2025. Shares recouped some losses to trade 3.8% lower by early afternoon.

articles.title: Iran army says it targeted U.S. military base in Kuwait
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The army claimed it had targeted air defence systems, as well as drone and missile launch platforms, according to a statement carried by Iran’s state broadcaster

The Iranian army claimed early on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) it targeted U.S. Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait with drones, triggering the air defence alerts in the oil-rich Gulf country for the first time in weeks.
The army claimed it had targeted air defence systems, as well as drone and missile launch platforms, according to a statement carried by Iran’s state broadcaster.
U.S. Central Command, which oversees U.S. forces in the West Asia, did not immediately comment.

Earlier on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Kuwait’s Army said its air defences were intercepting drone attacks but did not immediately report any damage. The country’s Foreign Ministry condemned the repeated Iranian “criminal” attacks and said they threatened Kuwait’s security and stability.

Iran also recently claimed attacks against U.S. military targets in the tiny island kingdom of Bahrain. Iran targeted U.S. facilities and interests in the neighbouring Gulf countries following the U.S. and Israeli strikes against it on Feb 28.

articles.title: Israeli Parliament elects new Knesset Speaker backed by Netanyahu's opponents
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The newly-elected Speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Mr. Netanyahu
The Israeli Parliament elected a new speaker on Tuesday (November 18, 2026), a key step toward rolling back policies passed by the outgoing government led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The newly-elected Speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Mr. Netanyahu. Eisenkot's bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu's most contentious policies following Kahana's election.

He was approved as speaker with 66 votes in the 120-member chamber, backed by the Jewish-led opposition parties and by the Arab-led parties. The candidate backed by Netanyahu's bloc, Ofir Katz, received 52 votes following a stormy debate that stretched over seven hours.
"The appointment of Matan Kahana as Knesset speaker is a worthy democratic move that reflects the absolute majority in favour of change," Mr. Eisenkot said ahead of the vote.

The vote took place weeks after October 27 parliamentary elections in which Netanyahu and his allies lost their parliamentary majority. Mr. Eisenkot was subsequently given the task by Israel's president to try to form a new coalition government.

Mr. Eisenkot has up to five more weeks to secure enough alliances to form a coalition. As negotiations continue on the sidelines, his bloc, along with unaffiliated Arab-led parties, can use their majority in the newly-sworn in Knesset to advance their legislative agenda. They introduced several bills last week, including to set term limits on the role of prime minister, to form a government-led inquiry into the Hamas-led Oct 7, 2023, attacks and to reverse laws to limit the powers of the judiciary.
Mr. Kahana gives the opposition bloc a major legislative advantage, according to Assaf Shapira with the Israel Democracy Institute, a Jerusalem think tank.
"It's important because there is not much time, because the speaker of the Knesset can make the legislative process much, much faster or much slower," Shapira said.
Mr. Kahana replaced Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally, as speaker.

Mr. Eisenkot and his allies are under pressure to swiftly advance their legislative priorities in the weeks ahead. Currently a member of Eisenkot's Yashar party, Roy Folkman, heads the temporary committee that decides much of the Knesset's work until a government is formed.
If Mr. Eisenkot fails to form a government, the Israeli President could give Netanyahu an opportunity to do so. That would likely give Netanyahu's Likud party control of the committee.

Even though Netanyahu's opponents would still hold a majority, they would "feel that their momentum has gone," Shapira said, and there would be a "real danger that some of the legislation will be delayed."

The Israeli Parliament elected a new speaker on Tuesday (November 18, 2026), a key step toward rolling back policies passed by the outgoing government led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The newly-elected Speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Mr. Netanyahu. Eisenkot's bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu's most contentious policies following Kahana's election.

He was approved as speaker with 66 votes in the 120-member chamber, backed by the Jewish-led opposition parties and by the Arab-led parties. The candidate backed by Netanyahu's bloc, Ofir Katz, received 52 votes following a stormy debate that stretched over seven hours.

"The appointment of Matan Kahana as Knesset speaker is a worthy democratic move that reflects the absolute majority in favour of change," Mr. Eisenkot said ahead of the vote.

The vote took place weeks after October 27 parliamentary elections in which Netanyahu and his allies lost their parliamentary majority. Mr. Eisenkot was subsequently given the task by Israel's president to try to form a new coalition government.

Mr. Eisenkot has up to five more weeks to secure enough alliances to form a coalition. As negotiations continue on the sidelines, his bloc, along with unaffiliated Arab-led parties, can use their majority in the newly-sworn in Knesset to advance their legislative agenda. They introduced several bills last week, including to set term limits on the role of prime minister, to form a government-led inquiry into the Hamas-led Oct 7, 2023, attacks and to reverse laws to limit the powers of the judiciary.

Mr. Kahana gives the opposition bloc a major legislative advantage, according to Assaf Shapira with the Israel Democracy Institute, a Jerusalem think tank.

"It's important because there is not much time, because the speaker of the Knesset can make the legislative process much, much faster or much slower," Shapira said.

Mr. Kahana replaced Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally, as speaker.

Mr. Eisenkot and his allies are under pressure to swiftly advance their legislative priorities in the weeks ahead. Currently a member of Eisenkot's Yashar party, Roy Folkman, heads the temporary committee that decides much of the Knesset's work until a government is formed.

If Mr. Eisenkot fails to form a government, the Israeli President could give Netanyahu an opportunity to do so. That would likely give Netanyahu's Likud party control of the committee.

Even though Netanyahu's opponents would still hold a majority, they would "feel that their momentum has gone," Shapira said, and there would be a "real danger that some of the legislation will be delayed."

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a third cyclone in a month?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual, experts say

Andhra Pradesh is currently facing a rare weather phenomenon. Since October 28, the State has already been hit by two back-to-back cyclonic storms, and there is an imminent threat of another one battering the coastal districts in the next two days.

On October 28, the State was battered by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab , which made landfall near Narsapur in West Godavari district. On November 3, it was hit again by severe cyclonic storm Murasu , which made landfall close to Ongole in Prakasam district. Now, cyclonic storm Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and make landfall on November 20 between Narsapur and Puri.

Three tropical storms battering the coast within less than a month during the post-monsoon season is a rare scenario. The last times such a thing happened were in 1976, 1987 and 2013. Both 1976 and 1987 were El Niño years, and this year is also categorised as a super El Niño year .

When it comes to tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal, there are a number of driving factors, and El Niño is just one of them. Mostly, the formation of storms over the Bay, especially their frequency and intensity, differs slightly from the rest of the world, because the Bay of Bengal is almost a land-locked sea, said S.S.V.S. Ramakrishna, former head of the Department of Oceanography and Meteorology, Andhra University, who has spent over four decades researching the pattern of cyclones over the Bay.
“El Niño typically suppresses the southwest summer monsoon over India, but it has the opposite effect on the Northeast (winter) Monsoon and post-monsoon cyclogenesis in the Bay of Bengal,” he said.

During El Niño years, the northeast monsoon tends to be significantly more active over southern peninsular India. This creates continuous moisture convergence and frequent convective disturbances over the southern Bay, providing a steady assembly line of low-pressure areas.

And sometimes, in rare occurrences, remnants of a Pacific Ocean cyclone cross the Strait of Malacca, re-enter the Bay of Bengal, and intensify into a cyclone. “We had seen this phenomenon during the Odisha Super Cyclone in 1999,” he said.

Mr. Ramakrishna also pointed out that in October and November, the Bay of Bengal consistently retained high sea surface temperatures—over 26.5 degrees Celsius—and anything above 26 is conducive to developing a cyclonic system. This has been aided by the El Niño-modified upper-level wind patterns over the southern Bay of Bengal, which reduce vertical wind shear.

Another key factor that acted as a catalyst is the massive freshwater discharge from rivers like the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Godavari into the Bay of Bengal, which resulted in creating a low-salinity surface layer. This acts as a “barrier layer” that prevents cooler, deeper ocean water from mixing upward, so a passing cyclone (like Arnab or Murasu) does not cool the sea surface enough to stop the next storm from forming days later.

Persistent upper-tropospheric ridges (anticyclonic circulations) over the China–Myanmar region and central India have acted as steering barriers, blocking storms from recurving northeast and forcing them northwestward into the Andhra coast, he said.

articles.title: Kaziranga: 21 elephants died in 22 months, RTI reveals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Environment activist Dilip Nath sought the information for the January 2025 to October 22, 2026 period

Information obtained under the Right to Information (RTI) Act reveals that 21 elephants died in the Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve during the almost 22-month period between January 2025 and October 22, 2026.
Sonitpur district-based environmental activist Dilip Nath sought the information from the Eastern Assam Wildlife Division, which administers four ranges of Kaziranga National Park, on September 23.

According to the response to his RTI query, 12 elephants died in 2025 and nine died in 2026 (up to October 22). The reply also notes the death of a woman in human-elephant conflict during this period.
However, the wildlife division did not disclose the age or gender of the elephants that died during the 22-month period.

“Poaching or death of rhinos, the flagship species in Kaziranga, has always been a matter of concern. The death of so many elephants in less than two years should also be equally alarming, given the shrinking of space for them,” Mr Nath told The Hindu on Wednesday.

Kaziranga recorded an estimated 1,228 elephants during a 2024 count. According to the seventh Elephant Population Estimation Report released in October 2025, the park’s three wildlife divisions had 1,288 elephants.
Mr Nath said the lack of information on wild elephant deaths on public platforms raises serious questions about transparency in the park’s management.

In addition to their wild counterparts, a few captive elephants engaged by the Forest Department in Kaziranga have died since December 2025. They include Swarnamoyee, a female safari elephant, and Krishna, a female departmental elephant.
Beyond Kaziranga, 626 elephant deaths between 2000 and 2023 were attributed to electrocution, train collisions, poisoning, poaching and retaliatory killings.
A Wildlife Institute of India report said these causes accounted for 52% of the 1,209 elephant deaths recorded over the 23-year period.

articles.title: Kulgam encounter: 25 girls, 2 teachers rescued before final assault on LeT commander Bhat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Once the civilians were moved to safety, security forces launched the final onslaught.

Anxious moments gripped Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district on Wednesday when it emerged that 25 girls and two teachers were inside a Darul Uloom (educational institute) next to the mosque where top Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat was holed up, just before troops launched the final assault to neutralise him.

Braving heavy fire from the mosque, an officer from the Army's 9 Rashtriya Rifles volunteered and, along with his comrade, entered the adjoining seminary to safely evacuate all 27 civilians, officials said.
Once the civilians were moved to safety, troops of the 9 Rashtriya Rifles and the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the Jammu and Kashmir Police launched the final onslaught.

Tear gas shells were fired into the mosque to smoke the terrorist out while a tight cordon was set up to prevent his escape, as the security forces exercised maximum restraint to ensure the religious structure suffered no damage.
Northern Army Commander Lt. Gen. Pratik Sharma, General Officer Commanding-In-Chief, met troops in South Kashmir after the successful conclusion of the operation.

Giving details of the operation, officials said a search party accompanied by local civilians entered the mosque following specific intelligence inputs and found a room on the top floor locked from the inside.
When asked to come out, the occupant opened fire, confirming the presence of Bhat, who carried a cash reward of Rs 15 lakh on his head, inside the premises.

Senior Army officers in South Kashmir had resolved to ensure that Bhat did not slip through the cordon this time, as he had done on previous occasions. He had escaped an earlier encounter in Shopian on July 8, in which another terrorist, Zakir, was killed.

Following a November 11 attack on a CRPF picket in Kulgam by Bhat and his associate Umar Nasir Dar, which left three personnel injured, security forces launched massive cordon and search operations across Kulgam and the adjoining Shopian and Anantnag districts.
Around 2,000 personnel from the Army, SOG, and CRPF, supported by a Mobile Bunker Command Post (MBCP), were deployed for the grid-based searches.

"Since November 11, cordon and search operations have been underway. In certain areas, it took us nearly three days to complete the searches due to high population density," a senior officer said, adding that while the operations may have caused some inconvenience to the general public, there were no complaints of any excesses.
A school passout and former carpenter, Bhat, who was in his early 20's, went missing on this day in November 2025 before joining LeT and its offshoot, The Resistance Front (TRF).

articles.title: Union Minister Piyush Goyal meets top Italian CEOs in Rome to boost investment, tech partnerships
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Goyal met chief executives and senior leaders of Italian companies on November 17, as India and Italy work towards a target of €20 billion in annual bilateral trade by 2029

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal held meetings with chief executive officers and senior leaders of leading Italian companies in Rome, focusing on investment, technology partnerships and joint ventures.

According to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the meetings took place on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), during the Minister’s official visit to Italy. The talks come as India and Italy take forward their Special Strategic Partnership, and work towards a target of €20 billion in annual bilateral trade by 2029.

Mr. Goyal met several corporate heads, including Walter Tosto S.p.A. Managing Director Luca Tosto, Nordimpianti System S.r.l. Chief Executive Officer Gian Piero Gagliardi and Atitech Chairman Gianni Lettieri. He also held discussions with Magaldi Green Energy Managing Director Letizia Magaldi, and Bracco Imaging S.p.A. Chief Executive Officer Fulvio Renoldi Bracco.
The talks centred on expanding Italian investments in India, facilitating technology transfer, and forming joint ventures with domestic partners.

The Italian firms expressed interest in bringing their technologies to the Indian market, and showed willingness to collaborate with Indian industry across sectors such as manufacturing, aircraft maintenance, thermal energy storage and pharmaceutical ingredients.

Mr. Goyal welcomed the interest shown by the business leaders. He encouraged the firms to partner with Indian industry, specifically pointing to opportunities in India’s infrastructure, aviation and healthcare sectors.
To move the discussions forward, both sides identified several actionable steps, including exploring suitable Indian joint-venture partners and initiating pilot projects.
The participants also noted the need to conduct cost-comparison studies, and to undertake joint studies with Indian institutions to evaluate potential collaborations.

Italy is India’s fourth-largest trading partner in the European Union. Bilateral trade between India and Italy has been growing strongly in the last three years, following the economic recovery after the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2025, bilateral trade registered at €14.25 billion.

India’s exports to Italy reached €8.55 billion, while its imports from Italy were €5.70 billion. The balance of trade remains in India’s favour at €2.84 billion, and has been in India’s favour since 1988.

articles.title: Season’s first ground frost recorded in Nilgiris
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Temperatures between 5°C and 6°C were recorded in the higher elevations of the district

The first seasonal ground frost was recorded in The Nilgiris on the intervening night of Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and Wednesday (November 18), as temperatures between 5°C and 6°C were recorded in the higher elevations of the district.

While frost usually sets in in late November or early December, the season was extremely delayed in 2025. However, the delay in the onset of ground frost led to colder weather in the early part of this year, with many places, especially Thalakundha, becoming tourist hotspots, as the area was blanketed by ground frost.
While frost usually sets in in late November or early December, the season was extremely delayed in 2025 | Photo Credit: M. Sathyamoorthy

According to officials, ground frost was seen early Wednesday morning in the low-lying parts of Ooty town surrounding Ooty lake, as well as in Thalakundha, Khandal, and a few other areas. Temperature gauges recorded lows of anywhere between 5°C and 6°C.

Over the last few years, pictures of the district’s annual ground frost have led to an increase in tourism footfall in the district, with visitors keen to witness this weather phenomenon, which occurs when ground temperatures fall below freezing, causing ice crystals to form from condensed water vapour and creating the illusion of snow carpeting open expanses, particularly grasslands.

Over the last few years, pictures of the district’s annual ground frost have led to an increase in tourism footfall in the district, with visitors keen to witness this weather phenomenon | Photo Credit: M. Sathyamoorthy

The ground-frost season also has ecological implications, with the phenomenon helping to curtail the spread of invasive species into the upper Nilgiris, as many species of invasive flora are unable to tolerate the extreme cold that native and endemic species have evolved to withstand and thrive in.

articles.title: SC notice to Lokpal on plea against HC verdict saying hearing not needed before show-cause notice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Delhi High Court, on April 15, had dismissed a petition filed by public servant Chinmoyjit Sen, who had challenged a Lokpal order dated February 25 and a subsequent show-cause notice

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) sought a response from the Lokpal of India on a plea challenging a Delhi High Court verdict which held that the anti-corruption ombudsman was not required to provide a public servant an opportunity of hearing before issuing a show-cause notice with regard to an investigation.

The Delhi High Court, on April 15, had dismissed a petition filed by public servant Chinmoyjit Sen, who had challenged a Lokpal order dated February 25 and a subsequent show-cause notice issued on February 27 in connection with a complaint.

Observing that the right to be heard arises before any final action is taken under Section 20(3) of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the high court had held that the Lokpal was not required to provide a public servant an opportunity of hearing before issuing a show-cause notice.

Section 20(3) of the Act requires a Lokpal bench of at least three members to review preliminary inquiry reports under Section 20(2), hear the public servant, decide if a prima facie case exists and choose one or more actions.
The Lokpal probes allegations of corruption under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 against specified public servants, politicians and certain institutions.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana took note of the submissions of Sen's lawyer and issued the notice to the ombudsman.
The bench, however, refused to stay the proceedings before the Lokpal against Sen and said that the matter would be taken up after a week.
The proceedings originated from a preliminary inquiry conducted by the CBI on the directions of the Lokpal.
The CBI submitted its preliminary inquiry report on January 27, following which the Lokpal examined the allegations and found certain of them against Sen to be prima facie substantiated.
The Lokpal subsequently issued a show-cause notice to the petitioner, calling upon him to respond to the two allegations and providing an opportunity of hearing under Section 20(3) of the Act.
Challenging the order and notice, Sen told the high court that the Lokpal had passed the February 25 order without giving him an opportunity of hearing.
It was further said that the Lokpal had already formed an opinion on the allegations, rendering the subsequent show-cause notice and hearing an empty formality.

articles.title: India-U.S. trade deal signing will still ‘take some time’, says Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: He added that the deal can be signed only after the U.S. finalises its new tariff framework. Recently, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the two nations had agreed that India would receive an advantage over its competitors

The actual signing of the India-U.S. trade will still “take some time”, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), adding that the negotiation part and the legal text will be completed soon.

The delay in signing, he said, was because it can be done only after the U.S. concludes its Section 301 investigations into its trade partners and finalises its tariff structure. A few days ago, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal asserted that the U.S. has acknowledged that India will receive lower tariffs as compared to its competitors.

“This is a deal that has been announced in February, the contours have already been announced as part of the joint statement,” Mr. Agrawal said while speaking at the curtain raiser of the FICCI Annual General Meeting. “The legal agreement has also been negotiated and it is now in final stages and it will be concluded soon.”
He was referring to the joint statement between India and the U.S. in February that announced the framework of an interim deal on trade.

However, Mr. Agrawal explained that the “challenge” is that this framework was announced against the background of the executive tariffs system that the U.S. President Donald Trump had put in place. At the time, the tariff on India was 50%. Later in February, the U.S. Supreme Court struck down the legal foundation of these tariffs.

“Now a new tariff architecture is being created by the U.S.,” Mr. Agrawal explained. “So until that tariff architecture comes back in place, the signing of a deal is something that I think will take some time. But concluding the negotiations and having everything ready will be something that we will strive to achieve as soon as possible.”
In particular, Mr. Agrawal spoke about the investigations undertaken by the American administration under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

One of these investigations, regarding forced labour, has been completed and a tariff of 10% has been levied on imports from India. The second investigation, looking into excess capacity, is yet to be completed and could come with further tariffs.

“There are certain 301 investigations which are already under review,” Mr. Agrawal said. “Those will also be coming to the fore in the next few weeks or months. You can’t have a deal until you have got uncertainty around multiple investigations which are already there.”

Separately, without mentioning the U.S. or any other country, Mr. Agrawal also asserted that trade deals can take a long time to conclude when parties try to maximise the benefits accruing to them rather than engaging in a spirit of compromise.

“Negotiations are always, to my mind, the art of what is possible,” the Commerce Secretary said. “You try to bring it together and keep it in a mutual win-win position because each party wants to go from the table as a victor and wants to showcase to its people that they have got something good for their business.”
As such, he explained that most agreements are not perfect, but instead involve an even trade-off where parties have simultaneously minimized their risk and also taken advantage of what they can.

articles.title: LPG tanker that sank off Bulgaria was hit by projectiles: official
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Liberian-flagged Gas Husky was carrying 3,400 metric tons of LPG from Egypt to Romania when it sent a ‌distress signal

A liquefied petroleum gas tanker that sank off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast on ​Tuesday (November 17, 2026) had been struck by projectiles, a regional governor and ‌maritime security sources said, joining a growing list ​of ships attacked in the area in recent ⁠weeks.

The Liberian-flagged Gas Husky was carrying 3,400 metric tons of LPG from Egypt to Romania when it sent a ‌distress signal on Tuesday morning before starting to sink approximately 50 miles (80 km) east of ‌Byala. All 19 crew members were rescued.
“There is ‌no ⁠doubt about the number of strikes, ⁠there were four, but we have no confirmation from the sailors about the kind of drones used,” Varna’s regional governor Mario Smarkov said.
Two ​maritime security sources said ‌the ship was hit by an unmanned system.
The vessel’s Greece-based manager did not respond to a request for comment on Wednesday.

The strike, a day after ‌a cargo ship carrying wheat sank in the ​same area, is the latest in a spate of drone attacks that have left ⁠more than 20 seafarers missing and feared dead, raising concerns about the widening conflict between Russia and Ukraine in ‌the Black Sea.
At least 17 vessels have been attacked off the coast of Bulgaria and Romania since mid-July, according to maritime security firm Diaplous.

The waters off the shores of the two NATO countries have become the primary route for shipments from Ukraine, ‌one of the world’s biggest grain exporters, the Black Sea ports ​of which have come under repeated fire from Russia since its invasion.

Romanian and Bulgarian officials ⁠have been cautious about ascribing blame for attacks near ⁠their coasts, although some have occasionally pointed fingers at Russia. Maritime security experts have also suggested ‌Russian involvement, which Moscow denies.
Moscow has also accused Ukraine of striking Russian vessels in other parts of ​the Black Sea.

LPG tanker that sank off Bulgaria was hit by projectiles: official

The Liberian-flagged Gas Husky was carrying 3,400 metric tons of LPG from Egypt to Romania when it sent a ‌distress signal

A liquefied petroleum gas tanker that sank off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast on ​Tuesday (November 17, 2026) had been struck by projectiles, a regional governor and ‌maritime security sources said, joining a growing list ​of ships attacked in the area in recent ⁠weeks.

The Liberian-flagged Gas Husky was carrying 3,400 metric tons of LPG from Egypt to Romania when it sent a ‌distress signal on Tuesday morning before starting to sink approximately 50 miles (80 km) east of ‌Byala. All 19 crew members were rescued.

“There is ‌no ⁠doubt about the number of strikes, ⁠there were four, but we have no confirmation from the sailors about the kind of drones used,” Varna’s regional governor Mario Smarkov said.

Two ​maritime security sources said ‌the ship was hit by an unmanned system.

The vessel’s Greece-based manager did not respond to a request for comment on Wednesday.

The strike, a day after ‌a cargo ship carrying wheat sank in the ​same area, is the latest in a spate of drone attacks that have left ⁠more than 20 seafarers missing and feared dead, raising concerns about the widening conflict between Russia and Ukraine in ‌the Black Sea.

At least 17 vessels have been attacked off the coast of Bulgaria and Romania since mid-July, according to maritime security firm Diaplous.

The waters off the shores of the two NATO countries have become the primary route for shipments from Ukraine, ‌one of the world’s biggest grain exporters, the Black Sea ports ​of which have come under repeated fire from Russia since its invasion.

Romanian and Bulgarian officials ⁠have been cautious about ascribing blame for attacks near ⁠their coasts, although some have occasionally pointed fingers at Russia. Maritime security experts have also suggested ‌Russian involvement, which Moscow denies.

articles.title: NASA Voyager 1 probe believed to have reached ‘light-day’ milestone
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The robotic probe, launched in 1977, was calculated by NASA to have reached a light-day from Earth, ‌the distance that light travels in 24 hours — about 26 billion km

NASA’s Voyager 1 probe is believed to have now ​hit a distance milestone accomplished by no other spacecraft from Earth, based ⁠on advance computations by the U.S. space agency, as the probe ventures through the near-emptiness of interstellar space.

The robotic probe, launched in 1977, was calculated by NASA to have reached a light-day from Earth, ‌the distance that light travels in 24 hours — about 16 billion miles (26 billion km) — on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at 5:16 a.m. ET (1016 GMT).
Infographic | Voyager I — A five-decade journey to get one light-day away

Officials at NASA’s Jet Propulsion ‌Laboratory in California will have to wait about a day to get a ‌signal ⁠from the probe, confirming it has reached this distance. They have scheduled an event ⁠for Thursday (November 19) to discuss the milestone.
“Reaching one light-day is an astounding feat, one that I never expected to see,” Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd said.

Voyager 1, the most distant human-made object, is flying at almost 38,000 ​miles per hour (61,000 kph). It crossed ‌the outer edge of the heliosphere, a protective bubble of particles and magnetic fields produced by the sun, to enter interstellar space in 2012. Its twin, Voyager 2, was also launched in 1977 and entered interstellar space in 2018.
A Jet Propulsion Laboratory representative ‌said recent power-saving measures could give the two Voyager spacecraft enough power to stay in ​communication with Earth for three to four more years.

“But the goal of the mission is to do science, and there is enough power to ⁠keep the current suite of instruments going through the 50th launch anniversary next year. Beyond that is hard to predict, and of course these are nearly 50-year-old spacecraft, and there are ‌always things the team cannot anticipate that might happen,” the JPL representative said.

Voyager 1 journeyed past Jupiter and Saturn, the solar system’s two largest planets, earlier in its mission. It continues to gather scientific data. For instance, its instruments have detected the faint monotonous hum caused by the constant vibrations of the small amounts of gas present in interstellar space.

“Voyager is sending back continuous measurements of magnetic fields, cosmic rays and of plasma waves that we ‌receive on Earth whenever the Deep Space Network points its antenna at Voyager,” Mr. Dodd said.
The Deep Space Network ​is NASA’s international array of giant radio antennas supporting interplanetary spacecraft missions.

“After the heliopause crossing, the magnetic field direction did not rotate into the interstellar direction ⁠as expected, but has maintained the direction it had when both Voyagers crossed the heliopause, a direction ⁠governed by our sun. We are watching to see when that rotation might occur,” Mr. Dodd said.

articles.title: Australia sanctions Israeli settlers, organisations over West Bank expansion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The measures prohibit Australians ​and Australian businesses from trading ‌with, or providing support to, the sanctioned individuals and organisations

Australia on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) imposed sanctions on ​three Israeli individuals and four organisations for illegal settlement expansion and settler violence in ‌the West Bank, saying those actions were extinguishing the possibility ​of a two-state solution.
Australia’s move follows Britain’s decision ⁠on Tuesday to sanction eight Israeli construction companies involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank.

“The sanctioned individuals and organisations have actively participated in the planning, ‌coordination and establishment of new settlements, including raising funds, recruitment of volunteers and providing support to violent settlers,” Australian Foreign Minister ‌Penny Wong said in a statement.

Daniella Weiss, leader of ‌the ⁠settler organisation Nachala and an advocate for the expulsion of ⁠Palestinians from Gaza, is among those sanctioned. Another sanctioned individual, Eliav Libi, has accelerated the expansion of settlements in the West Bank through his construction company.
The measures prohibit Australians ​and Australian businesses from trading ‌with, or providing support to, the sanctioned individuals and organisations.

Ms. Wong said violence at the E1 settlement project in recent weeks had undermined the prospect of a two-state solution. The E1 project would bisect ‌the Israeli-occupied West Bank and cut it off from East Jerusalem, ​fragmenting the land Palestinians hope will form the heart of a future state.
Reuters previously reported on one of ⁠the sanctioned settlers, Eliav Libi, whose company has accelerated the expansion of settlements in the West Bank by driving Palestinians from their homes.
The Israeli foreign ‌ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Israeli settlers shot dead a 72-year-old Palestinian woman this week in a part of the occupied West Bank city of Jericho, where settlers recently took over several Palestinian homes, according to witnesses and Palestinian officials.
U.N. bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal, a position Israel disputes.
Ms. Wong said ‌she had spoken to Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar about Australia’s latest round ​of sanctions.
“I outlined our position... I said we do not agree with, we oppose the settlement activities. We have ⁠had a long-standing position on this,” Ms. Wong told ABC Radio on Wednesday.

articles.title: PM Modi gifts Pichwaai painting, Banarasi Katan silk stole, Kashmiri carpet to world leaders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Prime Minister has gifted the U.S. president a golden Pichwaai painting, originating in Nathdwara, Rajasthan

A Pichwaai painting, a royal blue Banarasi Katan silk stole, and a Kashmiri silk carpet are some of the items gifted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to world leaders, including U.S. President Donald Trump, during his just-concluded visit to Manila to attend the annual India-ASEAN Summit.
The Prime Minister has gifted the U.S. president a golden Pichwaai painting, originating in Nathdwara, Rajasthan.
It is a traditional cloth-painting art known for its intricate detailing, luminous colours and elaborate compositions, officials sources said.
Created on finely prepared cloth using mineral pigments and gold detailing, it features motifs such as lotuses, cows, trees and ornamental borders, reflecting exceptional artisan craftsmanship.
The golden finish lends it a regal and luminous appeal.

Rooted in centuries-old traditions, Pichwaai preserves India's artistic heritage, supports traditional artisan communities and is valued today as both a treasured collectable and an elegant decorative artwork, the sources said.
Mr. Modi has gifted Prime Minister of Australia Anthony Albanese a blue Jaipur pottery artefact.
It is a distinctive traditional craft of Rajasthan, made from a quartz-based mixture rather than ordinary clay, giving it a smooth, delicate and translucent finish.
Known for its glossy white surface and luminous cobalt-blue designs, it features intricate hand-painted floral patterns, birds, geometric motifs and decorative borders.

The Prime Minister has gifted his Japanese counterpart, Sanae Takaichi, a royal blue Banarasi Katan silk stole presented in an elegant Sadheli box, symbolising India's enduring friendship, warmth and cultural esteem.
Woven from fine Katan silk, it showcases the centuries-old textile artistry of Banaras, with intricate motifs reflecting the precision and craftsmanship of generations of weavers.
Its royal blue colour evokes dignity, wisdom and harmony.

articles.title: Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart features drive market growth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks

Demand for air purifiers in India has witnessed explosive growth in 2026, with major brands and retail platforms reporting sales doubling or tripling year-on-year. Driven by an early surge ahead of the traditional winter pollution season , consumer behaviour is shifting toward viewing indoor air quality as a year-round health priority rather than an emergency seasonal purchase.
According to industry leaders, adoption is gaining momentum well before peak pollution months.

Smart tech brand Qubo recorded a 150 percent growth over the previous year, while Xiaomi registered approximately 3X year-on-year sales growth during the festive period. Industry executives note that growing awareness surrounding indoor pollutants, ranging from dust and pet dander to everyday cooking and cleaning emissions, is encouraging households to take a proactive approach to home wellness throughout the year.

Retail footprint and online traffic reflect this expanding market footprint across the country. Electronics retailer Croma reported that air purifier sales volumes have more than doubled in 2026. While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks.
Premium tech maker Dyson also reported that visits to its air purifier pages grew by over 100 percent in October compared to the same period last year.

Modern buyers are increasingly seeking advanced functionality and intelligent filtration tech. Croma highlighted strong consumer interest in models featuring real-time AQI displays, app controls, and multi-functional units combining purification with humidification or heating.

On e-commerce platforms, Amazon India reported that sales doubled over the past week. Shoppers are actively leveraging Rufus, Amazon’s personalised AI shopping assistant, to filter models by room size, filter type, and live sensor capabilities, prompting the e-retailer to expand selection on Amazon Now for immediate delivery.

“We have observed a notable increase in consumer demand for air purifiers on Flipkart, reflected in higher search activity, product discovery and purchases. Northern India continues to account for a significant share of demand for the category. We also witnessed a rise in purchases during the early hours following Diwali, coinciding with heightened concerns around deteriorating air quality and the steps households are taking to manage their indoor environments,” said Flipkart.

articles.title: China’s LineShine retains top spot on list of world’s most powerful supercomputers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The highest ranked Indian machine on the list is Shakti Cloud at number 35

China’s LineShine supercomputer has retained its top spot in the list of the world’s most powerful supercomputers, whose latest edition was released at the SC26 conference in Chicago on Monday (November 16, 2026). LineShine first summited this list in June this year, where it displaced the U.S. El Capitan.
Editorial | Faster, stronger: on India and its supercomputer use

The updated list is also remarkable because its top 10 machines are unchanged from June. The overall 500 admitted only 27 newcomers in this time — the lowest in history — although the reason is obvious: the amount of computing power required to enter the list increased by 7.3% in the same period. The highest-ranked newcomer was HANGANG in South Korea, at number 12.

The Shenzhen Cloud Computing Centre built and installed LineShine at the National Supercomputing Centre in the same city. It is the first Chinese supercomputer to lead the Top500 since Sunway TaihuLight did in 2017.

During one standardised test, engineers found LineShine could perform up to 2.198 quintillion calculations per second, becoming the first Top500 machine to cross the 2 quintillion mark. During the same test it consumed around 42 MW of power. Researchers built LineShine for atmospheric and ocean research.

It uses China-made processors and an operating system called Kylin. Its topping the Top500 is thus a vote of confidence for China against the backdrop of the U.S. restricting its access to advanced computing chips.
After LineShine and El Capitan, the top five include Frontier and Aurora, also in the U.S., and JUPITER Booster in Germany. The highest ranked Indian machine on the list is Shakti Cloud at number 35.

articles.title: Centre offers up to 75% relief in environmental compensation to groundwater users
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: One-time settlement scheme offers 30-75% relief on groundwater environmental compensation to regulate, regularise, and settle disputes across projects in 19 States and Union Territories

The government has introduced a one-time settlement scheme offering 30 to 75% relief in environmental compensation imposed on industries, infrastructure projects, mining units and other groundwater users for extracting the resource without mandatory permissions, delayed renewal of permits or extracting it beyond the permitted limit.

The Ground Water Charges (Dispute Resolution) Scheme, 2026, notified by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on November 12, aims to encourage project proponents to regularise groundwater extraction, bring more users into the regulatory framework and facilitate settlement of disputes and pending litigation over environmental compensation.

The scheme will remain in force for one year from the date of its publication in the official gazette and will cover projects in 19 States and Union Territories where groundwater regulation is being carried out by the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA).

According to the notification, the scheme has been conceived as a “voluntary, one-time strategic resolution and settlement mechanism” with the primary objective of achieving wider regulatory compliance.

The notification said substantial environmental compensation liabilities had discouraged several project proponents from voluntarily entering the regulatory framework, while a significant number of cases remained entangled in prolonged representations and litigation, delaying recovery of compensation.

The scheme provides relief in three categories of violations — existing projects extracting groundwater without a valid No Objection Certificate (NOC), projects applying late for renewal of NOCs and projects extracting groundwater beyond the quantity permitted under their NOCs.

The maximum relief of 75% will be available to projects that have extracted groundwater in excess of the permitted quantity, while those applying late for renewal of NOCs can get relief ranging from 40 to 70%. Projects operating without NOCs will be eligible for 30 to 60% relief.
The extent of relief will depend on the groundwater assessment category of the area and the quantity of groundwater extracted by a project.

The notification classifies assessment units into five categories — safe, semi-critical, critical, over-exploited and saline — and prescribes different rates of concessions based on groundwater consumption slabs of less than 200 kilolitres per day (KLD), 200 to less than 1,000 KLD, 1,000 to less than 5,000 KLD and 5,000 KLD or above.
For existing projects operating without NOCs, the relief will range from 60% in safe and saline assessment units to 30% in over-exploited areas for projects extracting 5,000 KLD or more.
In the case of delayed NOC renewals, the relief will range from 70% in safe and saline areas to 40% in over-exploited areas for projects extracting 5,000 KLD or more.
For projects extracting groundwater beyond the permitted quantity, the relief will range from 75% to 45%, depending on the assessment category and consumption level.

articles.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max launched with a back display
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Xiaomi 18 Pro series continues to bring Leica-tuned lenses in the flagship phones, while running on the latest chipsets from Qualcomm

Xiaomi has launched its new flagship smartphones, the Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max , in a global unveil. The Xiaomi 18 Pro series features a back display that can be used to view notification and can also act as a viewfinder.
The Xiaomi 18 Pro series continues to bring Leica-tuned lenses in the flagship phones, while running on the latest chipsets from Qualcomm.

Xiaomi 18 Pro Max has a 6.9 inch LTPO AMOLED display with a dynamic refresh rate up to 120 Hz, 4,000 nits peak brightness, supporting Dolby Vision and HDR10+. The Xiaomi 18 Pro gets a 6.4 inch display with similar refresh rate and brightness.

Xiaomi has also introduced a privacy mode like Samsung, which reduces pixels brightness if viewed from sides to avoid glancing. It can be applied to selected apps, notifications, floating windows, and split-screen views.

The back display has up to 4,000 nits peak brightness with a 1-120 Hz LTPO refresh rate, protected by Corning Gorilla Glass Victus 2. It can also be used as a real-time translation tool that displays each speaker’s language on their respective side for face-to-face communication in 29 languages.

Xiaomi 18 Pro Max runs on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, while Xiaomi 18 Pro features the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 SoC. Xiaomi 18 Pro series operates on HyperOS 4 based on Android 17 out of the box.
Xiaomi 18 Pro Max ships with a 7,050 mAh battery with 100W wired and 50W wireless HyperCharge; Xiaomi 18 Pro gets a 6,000 mAh battery with 90W wired and 50W wireless HyperCharge.
Both, Xiaomi 18 Pro Max and Xiaomi 18 Pro sport a 200 MP main camera, a 200 MP telephoto lens, a 50 MP ultrawide sensor, along with a 50 MP selfie camera.
Xiaomi 18 Pro Max starts at €1,599, while Xiaomi 18 Pro begins at €1,399. The series is available in Black, White, Cosmic Blue, and Velvet Red.

articles.title: Telangana plans to turn Hyderabad into global hub for animation, gaming and creative technology: Tourism Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana is looking to strengthen its Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) sector and position Hyderabad as a global creative hub to attract investments, generate employment and expand the State’s creative economy, said Tourism and Culture Minister Jupally Krishna Rao on Wednesday.

Addressing an AVGC Executive Council meeting with industry leaders at Hyderabad Golf Club, Mr. Rao said the AVGC-XR sector and tourism would play a crucial role in achieving the State’s economic ambitions under the Telangana Rising 2047 vision, which aims to build a $1 trillion economy by 2034 and a $3 trillion economy by 2047.

Observing that Hyderabad had established itself as a prominent centre for Telugu cinema, he said Telangana had considerable talent in animation, visual effects, gaming, design and emerging creative technologies. The government wants to build on these strengths by creating an ecosystem that would enable young people to develop original ideas, create intellectual property and access more employment opportunities within the State, he said.
The Minister said the government was preparing to host IndiaJoy 2026 at Bharat Future City from December 7 to 13, alongside the Invest Telangana Global Summit from December 7 to 9.

IndiaJoy 2026 is expected to attract more than 80,000 visitors, 8,500 business-to-business (B2B) delegates and participants from over 20 countries during the seven-day event. It will bring together animation, visual effects, gaming, comics, cinema, digital content, esports, design and emerging technologies under four themes of Educate, Exhibit, Experience and Enjoy.

The Minister invited AVGC creators, extended reality technology companies and event organisers to explore opportunities in the State’s six Special Tourism Areas covering Spiritual, Heritage, Eco-Wellness, Crafts, Water and Buddhist circuits. Technologies such as augmented reality and virtual reality could be used to showcase Telangana’s heritage and tourist destinations through immersive storytelling and interactive experiences, he added.

articles.title: EESL showcases green energy solutions at trade fair
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Energy-efficient products and sustainable technologies across sectors such as agriculture, clean cooking and renewable energy are among the key attractions at the Energy Efficiency Services Limited’s (EESL) pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi.

The pavilion also features EESL’s one-stop marketplace, EESL Mart, offering energy-efficient products and sustainable solutions. Its flagship initiatives include the Solar-Powered Micro Cold Storage (SPMCS), which provides cold storage facilities at the farm gate. The solution helps preserve perishable produce, prevent distress sales, improve market access and increase farmers’ earnings.

Secretary-Ministry of Power Pankaj Agarwal visited the EESL and EESL Mart stalls. EESL CEO Akhilesh Kumar Dixit highlighted successful energy-efficiency initiatives and best practices implemented across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Odisha.

articles.title: There is no clarity on Central Crime Branch
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State government issued orders to restructure the Bengaluru City Police on Wednesday, doesn’t offer any clarity over the fate of the Central Crime Branch (CCB) in the city.
Each of the five commissionerates has a Deputy Commissioner of Police (headquarters and crime), indicating a dedicated crime unit, mimicking the CCB in the five commissionerates.

However, the government has also created a post of Additional Commissioner (Anti-Rowdy Squad) at the pan-city level. The CCB has five wings - Organised Crime Wing, Special Inquiry Division, Women Protection Wing, Anti-Narcotics Wing and Economic Offences Wing.

It is now speculated that the Additional Commissioner (Anti-Rowdy Squad) will take over the Organised Crime Wing of the CCB and the remaining four divisions will be decentralised into five commissionerates. The OCW presently has an East and West Squad in the CCB. Mimicking that, the Anti-Rowdy Squad will have two DCPs under the Additional Commissioner. However, there is no clarity on this aspect in the order.

What has further added to the confusion is an ad-hoc arrangement where the Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms (DPAR) issuing transfer orders on Wednesday stated Hemanth M. Nimbalkar, posted as Commissioner of Police (Anti-Rowdy Squad), “will supervise Crime Control under Chief Commissioner in Bengaluru City Commissionerate.”
The arrangement has not been institutionalised and there is no clarity what this will entail.

articles.title: Laxman Kumar calls for barrier-free access to public buildings for persons with disabilities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister for Welfare of Persons with Disabilities Adluri Laxman Kumar has called for mandatory accessibility facilities, including ramps, lifts, tactile pathways and accessible toilets, in government buildings, hospitals, educational institutions, commercial complexes and public transport systems to ensure barrier-free access for persons with disabilities.
He said accessibility measures would benefit not only persons with disabilities but also senior citizens, pregnant women, children and people with temporary mobility limitations.

Participating in a two-day national-level summit organised by the Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in New Delhi on Wednesday, the Minister stressed the need for regular maintenance and monitoring of accessibility infrastructure.

Representing Telangana, Mr. Laxman Kumar presented the State’s perspective on the theme ‘Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat’ and suggested measures to address challenges in implementing accessibility standards.

He proposed appointing a nodal officer in every government department to oversee accessibility infrastructure, earmarking funds in annual budgets and preparing time-bound action plans to address deficiencies. He also sought the involvement of organisations representing persons with disabilities and technical experts in accessibility audits.

The Minister emphasised the need to make government websites, mobile applications and online services accessible to persons with visual and hearing impairments. He also recommended specialised training for architects, engineers, contractors and government personnel in inclusive design.

Mr. Laxman Kumar proposed a national digital platform to monitor accessibility facilities in government buildings and public spaces. Departments should upload details of buildings, existing facilities and improvement works, along with photographic evidence, he said.
He also suggested an online grievance redressal mechanism to enable persons with disabilities to report accessibility barriers and track the resolution of complaints within stipulated timelines.

The Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan should evolve beyond an infrastructure development initiative into a nationwide movement to protect the rights, dignity and independence of persons with disabilities, he added.

articles.title: Ecstasy marks ‘Sri Sathya Sai Rathotsavam’ in Puttaparthi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Folk dances representing various States and ‘Chekka Bhajana’ by students of Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Learning add grandeur to the silver chariot procession marking the ongoing birth centenary celebrations of Sri Sathya Sai Baba

Prasanthi Nilayam, the abode of Sri Sathya Sai Baba, witnessed a confluence of devotion, spirituality and India’s rich cultural heritage on Wednesday morning with the performance of two events — ‘Sri Sathya Sai Sathyanarayana Vratham’ and Sri Sathya Sai Rathotsavam — as a part of the ongoing birth centenary celebrations of Sri Sathya Sai Baba.
The ‘Sri Sathya Sai Sathyanarayana Vratham’ performed in the Sai Kulwant Hall amidst the chanting of sacred hymns witnessed the participation of over 1,100 couples from across the world.

Adding further splendour to the day’s celebrations was the Sri Sathya Sai Rathotsavam. The procession of the idol of Sri Sathya Sai Baba mounted in a silver chariot was introduced during the Baba’s centenary celebrations last year.

After special rituals, the aesthetically decorated chariot was taken out in a ceremonial procession from Pata Mandiram to the accompaniment of vibrant folk dance performances representing different States of the country.

R.J. Rathnakar, managing trustee of the Sri Sathya Sai Central Trust, members K. Chakravarthi and I.S.N. Prasad, and All-India president of the Sri Sathya Sai Seva Organisations Nimish Pandya were among those who participated.
Adding grandeur to the event was the ‘Chekka Bhajan’ by the students of the Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Learning.
District Collector A. Shyam Prasad and MLA Palle Sindhura Reddy were among the thousands of devotees who joined the celebrations.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh’s amended semiconductor policy fully matches Centre’s capital support
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: By aligning with the second phase of India Semiconductor Mission and offering a combined support of up to 80% of eligible cost, A.P. wants to be the place where India builds its chips, from design to fab to packaging, says IT Minister Nara Lokesh
The Government of Andhra Pradesh has amended its Semiconductor & Display Fab Policy 4.0 in alignment with the second phase of the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM Semicon 2.0).
Under the amendment, the State will match 100% of the Centre’s capital support for silicon fabs, display fabs and chip packaging projects.
The amendment was notified through G.O.Ms.No.87, dated November 16, 2026.

With the State’s top-up, a silicon fab approved under Semicon 2.0 will get a combined support of 80% of its eligible capital cost: 40% from the Government of India (GoI) and 40% from A.P. Compound semiconductor, photonics, sensor, discrete and display fabs, and advanced packaging units will get 70%, and legacy packaging units 50%.

“A.P. wants to be the place where India builds its chips, from design to fab to packaging. By matching the Centre’s support rupee for rupee, giving investors one window and building the talent they need, we are making it simpler and cheaper to build a fab here than anywhere else in the country,” said IT Minister Nara Lokesh.
He stated that the amended policy covered all 10 Semicon 2.0 categories under six pillars: design, machines and materials, fabs, packaging, research and development, and talent.

Under the deployment-linked incentive, the State adds 4.50% of net sales on top of the Centre’s 9%, taking the total to 13.5%. This will be capped at ₹45 crore per application and ₹180 crore per company.
For machines and materials, the State will add 18% of capital cost on top of the Centre’s 30%, for combined support of 48%, plus the Centre’s production-linked incentive.
Assembly, testing, marking and packaging (ATMP) and outsourced assembly and test (OSAT) units will have 100% of the Centre’s capital support matched by the State.
For R&D and talent projects, the State will give 25% of eligible project cost, with combined Central and State support capped at 75%.
The Minister said the State was planning a dedicated ‘AP Semiconductor Park’ of about 5,000 acres in Tirupati as a manufacturing and supplier cluster for the full value chain.

It will be run by a public-private park company with an investor-led board that has up to three government nominees. It will offer developed land, shared industrial cleanrooms, high-voltage power with redundancy, ultrapure water, natural gas and specialty gases, effluent treatment and water recycling, testing labs, logistics, and research and training centres on site.

articles.title: Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets Bahrain amid wider Gulf attacks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Iran said its recent attacks — including those on other U.S. facilities in Bahrain on November 15 and November 13 — were in response to U.S. drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers

Iran widened its attacks on its Gulf neighbours on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), firing on the U.S. Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait and Bahrain in what appeared to be retaliation for American strikes the day before.
After about two months without such attacks, Iran has repeatedly targeted U.S. facilities in Bahrain in recent days. The small Persian Gulf island kingdom hosts the U.S. Navy’s 5th Fleet.

The early morning attacks came after a U.S. fighter jet struck a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
