articles.title: Christian community seeks West Bengal CM’s intervention over targeted attacks ahead of Christmas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bishop of Calcutta Reverend Paritosh Canning ruled out claims of religious conversion by institutions affiliated with the Churches of North India

Ahead of the upcoming Christmas festivities, the representatives of Christian communities in West Bengal have expressed concerns about the rising attacks on churches across several districts in the State and have sought intervention from Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.

During a press conference addressed by the Bengal Christian Council (a cluster body for Protestant churches), the Bishop of Calcutta, Reverend Paritosh Canning, said that the concerns of the people of the community are not without reason.

“West Bengal has traditionally been a land of communal harmony, where people belonging to different faiths and communities have coexisted in peace, mutual respect, and brotherhood. With Christmas approaching, the apprehensions of the Christian community have become particularly serious. However, the prevailing atmosphere of insecurity has raised genuine concerns about whether Christians will be able to observe their religious services and celebrate festivals without fear or disruption,” the bishop said, speaking to media persons.

He added that such incidents have increased since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government came to power in West Bengal in May 2026. Attacks have been reported across several districts in South Bengal, on both banks of the Hooghly River, including South 24 Parganas, North 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, and Paschim Medinipur, among others.

Bishop Canning said that there are allegations of religious conversions in the churches, adding that “we can confirm that no conversion takes place at the churches operating under the Churches of North India.”
“All the minority communities used to live peacefully under the previous governments. However, it is not clear who the attackers are or why they are doing this,” he said.

In another development, representatives of Bangiya Christiya Pariseba (BCP) held a meeting in response to remarks by West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya. The State BJP president had on Sunday said that religious conversions are taking place across districts in West Bengal and issued a warning to Christian missionary schools in the State, claiming that they are targeting teachers wearing saffron sarees.

The Archbishop of Calcutta (Roman Catholic), Reverend Elius Frank, also participated in a meeting organised by BCP, though he did not speak to the media. In a letter addressed to Samik Bhattacharya, Herod Mullick, the founder-secretary of BCP, said that “if any institution or individual is found guilty of illegal or forced religious conversion through greed or deception, we strongly condemn such actions and stand firmly against them.”

“However, making broad, unsubstantiated generalisations without naming specific individuals or institutions unfairly casts a shadow of suspicion over the entire Christian community and the more than 800 educational institutions we operate across West Bengal,” the letter added.

articles.title: West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own party members, says Union Minister as feuds rise in party
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “BJP workers are being beaten up, and those beating them are also from the BJP. The police administration has turned a blind eye and is not functioning impartially,” alleged Bongaon MP Santanu Thakur

Amid reports of growing feuds within the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in West Bengal , Union Minister of State and Bongaon MP Shantanu Thakur not only publicly acknowledged factionalism within the party but also said that BJP supporters are attacked by its members.
The Minister spoke about developments in his own constituency in North 24 Parganas, but reports of factional feuds within the BJP rank and file have surfaced across the State.

“Here, BJP workers are being beaten up, and those beating them are also from the BJP. The police administration has turned a blind eye and is not functioning impartially,” Mr. Thakur, who is the Bongaon MP and also a prominent leader of the Matua community, alleged.

The Minister, who hails from Thakurbari and is the religious head of the Matua community, said that divisions are emerging within the party, resulting in major problems. Differences between Shantanu Thakur, the Bongaon North MLA, and State Food and Civil Supplies Minister Ashok Kirtania have been going around in political circles.

On Sunday, BJP’s Panihati MLA Ratna Debnath, while expressing condolences over the death of a BJP worker, said that it would have been better “had the BJP not come to power in the State.” Arup Saha, husband of Ruma Saha—the secretary of BJP’s Panihati-1 Mandal (zone)—was attacked on Saturday (November 14, 2026), by a mob that allegedly included some of the party’s supporters. Saha succumbed to his injuries on Sunday.

Reports of an intra-party feud have surfaced between long-time supporters of the ruling party in the State and former Trinamool Congress supporters who switched allegiance after the Assembly election results in May 2026. Political observers say that the majority of the BJP leadership, including Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, had joined the party about five to six years ago.

State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya has repeatedly said that the doors of the party are closed for Trinamool supporters who want to join. Mr. Bhattacharya said that an FIR should be registered against elements who are trying to associate with the party and tarnish its image. “Register FIRs. Suvendu Adhikari is the police minister. Give me the papers; I will file them,” Mr. Bhattacharya said.

articles.title: Site inspection held for key Goshree-Mamangalam traffic corridor in Keralam’s Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Developing the stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease the existing pressure on several roads

People’s representatives and officials on Monday conducted a site inspection for the proposed Goshree-Mamangalam road development project, which is expected to provide major relief from traffic woes in Kochi.

The project is critical to improving the overall traffic system in the city and enhancing connectivity between various points. The demand for the proposed road dates back more than 30 years. Developing this stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease the existing pressure on several roads.

A sum of ₹1 crore was earmarked for the development of Goshree Bridge and Goshree-Mamangalam Road in the last State Budget following interventions by Hibi Eden MP, MLAs T.J. Vinod and Uma Thomas, and Mayor V.K. Minimol. The allocation was intended for conducting a traffic study, demarcating the alignment, and completing the survey. An action plan will be formulated based on scientific studies and survey findings.

Initially, the Goshree-Mamangalam road was proposed to be developed at 22 metres. However, during the tenure of the previous Kochi Corporation council, the width was scaled down to 15 metres in the 2024 Master Plan, which was subsequently approved by the State government. Based on this, follow-up measures are now being planned.

Coordination among various departments is essential, as several roads within the Kochi Corporation limits form part of the project. Accordingly, the PWD (Roads) will be entrusted with conducting the traffic study, carrying out the survey and preparing a detailed project report. This is expected to facilitate the efficient and time-bound execution of the project through coordinated efforts by the Corporation and the PWD.

The delegation assessed the existing condition of roads proposed to be included in the project, nature of traffic movement, development potential, and the role of the departments concerned. This is expected to aid the coordination of the proposed traffic study, survey, and subsequent follow-up measures.
MLAs T.J. Vinod and Uma Thomas, Mayor V.K. Minimol, and deputy mayor V.R. Sudheer were among those who participated in the inspection.

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan to bring light rainfall to parts of coastal T.N. on November 17
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The RMC, Chennai, has forecast that mainly dry weather is likely to prevail over the rest of the State during this time

With the deep depression in the Bay of Bengal intensifying into cyclonic storm Akvan on Monday evening, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) in Chennai has issued a cyclone warning for Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts.

The cyclonic storm lay centred about 610 km east of Chennai at 5.30 p.m. on Monday (November 16, 2026). The clouds associated with the system are likely to bring light to moderate rainfall at isolated places over coastal Tamil Nadu and the Western Ghat districts, as well as Puducherry and Karaikal, on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). The RMC, Chennai, has forecast that mainly dry weather is likely to prevail over the rest of the State during the same period.
Cyclone Akvan to make landfall between Nellore and Tuni in Andhra as very severe storm on November 20
Cyclone Akvan to hit Andhra on November 20; Naidu reviews preparedness, 173 fishing boats yet to return
Cyclone Akvan may bring rains to Telangana between November 19 and 21

For Wednesday (November 18, 2026) and Thursday (November 19, 2026), the RMC has forecast that heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places over Chennai, Tiruvallur, and Chengalpattu districts. The rain could be accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning, with gusty winds reaching speeds of 40-50 km/hour at one or two places.

Heavy rain could occur at isolated places over Kancheepuram and Ranipet districts. Moderate rain is likely to occur at a few places over the rest of north coastal Tamil Nadu and the Western Ghat districts, Puducherry, and Karaikal. Light rain may occur in isolated places over the rest of Tamil Nadu, with thunderstorms and lightning at one or two places.

A fisherman mends fishing net at Palavakkam beach in Chennai on November 16, 2026, as they remain ashore following an advisory against venturing into the sea from November 16 to 21 in view of impending Cyclone Akvan | Photo Credit: V. Umesh Kumar

On Friday (November 20, 2026), moderate rain is likely in isolated places over the northern coastal districts of Tamil Nadu, the Western Ghat districts, Puducherry, and Karaikal. Light rain is likely at isolated places over the rest of Tamil Nadu, with thunderstorms and lightning at one or two places.

It is very likely to continue moving north-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening. Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm around Thursday morning.

It will continue to move northwestward, and could cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around Friday noon as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 km/hr.

articles.title: Kerala High Court refers petition challenging clean chit to Chief Minister in Punarjani case to Chief Justice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: High Court Registry directed to place the matter before the Chief Justice to decide whether the case would be considered by the court trying MP/MLA cases, Prevention of Corruption Act, or as a PIL

A Single Bench of the Kerala High Court has referred the petition challenging the closure of the preliminary inquiry against Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan in the Punarjani case for consideration before the appropriate court.

Justice C. Jayachandran observed that there was a strong prima facie indication that the petition had features of a public interest litigation (PIL). The Bench directed the High Court Registry to place the matter before the Chief Justice to decide whether the case would be considered by the court trying MP/MLA cases, Prevention of Corruption Act, or as a PIL.

The petition had been filed by lawyer K.M. Shajahan challenging a Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) report closing the preliminary inquiry and dropping corruption charges against the Chief Minister in connection with the Punarjani flood rehabilitation scheme.

The court examined two aspects while considering the petition — first, if the petitioner had the right to challenge the preliminary inquiry report, and second, if the court had the jurisdiction to hear the matter.

The petitioner argued that he had preferred the plea in his capacity as a citizen and a whistleblower, with every right to challenge the report. The State pointed out that a petition in this regard was filed by one of the complainants in the Punarjani case. This petition was later withdrawn and filed as a PIL seeking a CBI probe. However, the PIL was dismissed by a Division Bench of the court. The State contended that the petitioner did not have any right to move the petition since the complaint had already been decided by the court.
The Single Bench found that the jurisdiction to try the case would have to be decided first before examining the rights of the petitioner.

articles.title: 70% turnout in most districts as four-phase panchayat polls end in Rajasthan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The declaration of results will bring the election of representatives in all 14,403 panchayats in the State to a close

The four-phase panchayat election process in Rajasthan concluded on Monday with polling held for 3,747 sarpanch and 33,885 ward panch posts across 25 districts. Voting exceeded 70% in most of the districts that went to the polls in the final phase.

There were stray incidents of confrontation and violence at some places, though long queues of voters were seen at several polling stations since morning. Villagers in Jalore district’s Gundau and Bharatpur district’s Shakarpur staged protests and created a ruckus raising allegations of bogus voting.

Police fired in the air and used force to disperse the supporters of two rival candidates for the sarpanch post at Mahu Gulawali in Dholpur district. The two groups clashed and hurled stones at each other, while one of them set on fire two motorcycles parked outside a polling booth.

In Dholpur’s Baroli village, polling started in late afternoon amid tension over a shooting incident on Sunday that resulted in the death of one person following a clash over election-related rivalry. Police have detained the main accused and 10 others in connection with the incident.

The allegations of fraudulent voting sparked tension in Kali Pahadi village of Khairthal-Tijara district and a verbal altercation between two groups escalated into a physical confrontation. Police arrived in the village on receiving information and brought the situation under control. An elderly person, who sustained serious injuries during the clash, was referred to Alwar for treatment.

Voting for both sarpanch and ward panch posts was conducted through ballot papers. More than 1.05 crore voters were eligible to exercise their franchise at 11,905 polling stations. Counting of votes started immediately after the polling ended. Results are expected to be declared by late night. The declaration of results will bring the election of representatives in all 14,403 panchayats in the State to a close.

The sarpanch and ward panch polls are not contested on political party symbols and parties do not officially allot tickets for these posts, unlike the zila parishad and panchayat samiti polls. Polling for zila parishad and panchayat samiti members across all four phases has been completed. Votes will be counted on November 20.

articles.title: A poverty line that falls short
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Reliable poverty estimates are not just for academic purposes. India has made real progress, but without a credible benchmark, it is hard to say how much, or how much remains to be done

There is no serious doubt that poverty in India has fallen sharply over the past decade. However, researchers and policymakers cannot agree on how many are still poor. Depending on the estimate, the share ranges from about 5% to more than 26%. Take the recent World Bank report. At its international line of $3 a day (2021 PPP), 2.6% of Indians were poor in 2022-23. Raise the line to $4.20, the bank’s benchmark for lower middle-income countries, and the figure jumps to around 16.1%. Same country, same year. Only the yardstick changed. A low level of extreme poverty does not necessarily mean poverty is not still a major issue. Where you draw the line decides how much economic insecurity you see.

India’s own figures tell a similar convoluted story. For example, SBI Research (2025) takes the Tendulkar line of 2009, adjusts it for inflation, and gets poverty of 7.2% in rural India and 4.6% in urban India for 2022-23. Rangarajan and Dev (2014), using an inflation-adjusted version of the Rangarajan Committee line, arrive at 10.8%. Further, Sethu, Surya and Ruthu (2024), who rebuild the Rangarajan method from the latest consumption survey, report 26.4%. Most of that gap boils down to the lines themselves: SBI’s Tendulkar-based lines use, after adjusting for inflation, about ₹1,632 a month per person in rural areas and ₹1,944 in urban areas. In contrast, Sethu et al. use much higher thresholds of ₹2,515 and ₹3,639. And the outcomes are obvious: Higher lines, higher poverty. Method matters too. One camp takes an old line and adjusts it for inflation. The other reconstructs the line from spending patterns in the new survey. Both have limitations, and they are answering different questions.

articles.title: Kishtwar killings aftermath: Remarks by Congress’ Karra, BJP’s Parihar spark protests in J&K
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Karra said that “two SPOs were killed by the Army in a mistaken-identity case on November 11”, while senior BJP leader Sharma said, “Congress is spreading misleading information to shift blame from terrorists to security forces”

Two separate remarks made by J&K Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra and BJP legislator Shagun Parihar in the aftermath of the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar on Monday (November 16, 2026) sparked protests from different quarters.

In response to the statement by Mr. Karra that “two SPOs were killed reportedly by the Army in a mistaken identity case on November 11”, senior BJP leader and Leader of Opposition (LoP) Sunil Sharma said, “The Congress is spreading misleading information to shift the blame from terrorists to our security forces. The SPOs were on duty and travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah to relieve the jawans posted there. Calling two martyrs hunters is an insult to their sacrifice and to their grieving families.”
He demanded that Mr. Karra “immediately withdraw the remarks and apologise to the martyrs’ families, the J&K Police and the Indian Army”.

Scores of members of the BJP and BJP-affiliated organisations held street protests against Mr. Karra and the Congress in Jammu. Members of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) also burn an effigy of Mr. Karra as a mark of protest.

BJYM leader Arun Prabhat, while condemning the statement of Mr. Karra, said, “It shows the hearts of Congress beat for Pakistan. The conspirators should face action. In case of any role of mosques, such places too should face action.”

Mr. Prabhat was seconding the controversial remarks of Ms. Parihar of the BJP, who claimed “announcements were made from the mosques in Kishtwar’s Dachhan area to identify the targets” allegedly ahead of the killings of two SPOs on November 11.

However, several religious organisations, including the Anjuman Islamia Bhaderwah and Kishtwar, in the Chenab Valley condemned the statement of Ms. Parihar and denied any role of mosques in the latest attack on the policemen. Ruling National Conference (NC) legislator Tanvir Sadiq said the BJP must be “held accountable for its MLA’s deeply irresponsible and inflammatory allegations against a mosque in Jammu”.

“Making communal allegations in the aftermath of a tragic killing is utterly unacceptable. The BJP leadership cannot hide behind silence or pretend this is an isolated matter. It must unequivocally condemn these remarks and issue an unconditional public apology. Stop playing with the communal harmony of J&K,” said Mr. Sadiq.

A spokesman of the All J&K Shia Association said the organisation “strongly condemn Ms. Parihar’s attempt to drag a mosque into the tragic killing of our brave SPOs”. “Terrorists are enemies of all humanity and terrorism has no religion. Unsubstantiated claims against a place of worship only weaken our fight against terror,” said the Association.
Jammu and Kashmir / Indian National Congress / Bharatiya Janata Party

articles.title: Customers at some of the U.S.’ largest banks are reporting difficulty accessing accounts online
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Bank of America, Chase, J.P. Morgan, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com
Customers reported difficulty accessing the online accounts at some of the U.S.’ largest banks on Monday (November 16, 2026).
Bank of America, Chase, J.P. Morgan, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com.
Chase Bank’s services are experiencing a technical bug issue, not a cyber issue, a spokesperson said Monday (November 16, 2026).

“Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds,” a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. “We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible.”
The reports follow a major outage by Microsoft that began on Friday (November 13, 2026) and lasted for hours, which impacted services including Outlook, Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.
Some Chase customers received a message that said, “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”

articles.title: BJP holds key party meeting in Mathura for Assembly polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach

Senior BJP leaders from Uttar Pradesh, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, attended a key meeting at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Cow Research Institute in Parkham, Mathura, to discuss strategy for the upcoming U.P. Assembly polls.

The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach to counter the Opposition’s renewed pitch.

“One goal, one idea... BJP government again for the third time... Today, in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, I participated in a planning meeting with National General Secretary (Organisation) B.L. Santosh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and BJP Uttar Pradesh Incharge Shri Vinod Tawde,” wrote Pankaj Chaudhary, U.P. BJP president, on X.

“In the meeting, various important topics, including upcoming organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and providing benefits of public welfare schemes to every household, were discussed in detail. On this occasion, National General Secretary Irani, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya ji and Shri Brajesh Pathak, co-incharges of BJP Uttar Pradesh, Ministers of the State Government, public representatives, and state officials were present,” he added.

State Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya said the construction of a grand temple at Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura will be a major poll issue in the 2027 U.P. elections, and that a grand Krishna temple will be built—through the courts or mutual dialogue, as with Ayodhya.
“If Akhilesh Yadav wants to join us in kar seva, we will take him along too to build a grand temple of Lord Krishna,” said the Deputy CM.

The meeting in Mathura is also significant amid the BJP’s emphasis on Mathura and western Uttar Pradesh. “The BJP holds meetings regularly to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment and other issues. Reach out to various sections of society is also part of our work,” said Dinesh Dubey, a senior BJP leader based in Lucknow.

Asad Rizvi, a political analyst based in Lucknow, said, “the meeting is significant as it is organised only a few months before the Assembly elections. Amid the main Opposition parties (the Samajwadi Party-Congress) pushing backwards, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Brahmins and marginalised groups through the PDA plank, the BJP will be recalibrating their policies and making a renewed effort towards them. ”

The SP president Akhilesh Yadav in a cryptic statement urged the BJP leaders to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. “I request them to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. It will be auspicious. If they fall ill, call a good doctor,” said Mr. Yadav.

articles.title: Tribute to Kartar Singh Sarabha, Punjab free from drugs and unemployment, says CM Mann
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision

Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said on Monday (November 16, 2026) that the greatest tribute to the 19-year-old revolutionary and freedom fighter Kartar Singh Sarabha is to fulfil his dream of a Punjab free from drugs, unemployment, and injustice.

He was speaking after paying tribute to Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha on his 111th martyrdom anniversary at his native village, Sarabha, in Ludhiana district. The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision.

“Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha embraced the gallows at the tender age of just 19, proving that courage, conviction and love for the motherland know no age. At a time when youngsters today are planning their futures, this great revolutionary was planning the liberation of the country. He sacrificed his youth, dreams and ultimately his life for our freedom,” he said.

“On November 16, 1915, Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha was hanged at Lahore Central Jail along with six other revolutionaries in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case. His fearless commitment to the freedom of the country remains a shining example of patriotism and selflessness,” he added.

As the Punjab 2027 Assembly election approaches, the drug menace has once again become a central campaign issue. In the run-up to the Assembly polls, the major political parties in the fray—the Congress, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), and the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)—are making the drug menace a key plank of their campaigns.

While the ruling party has been asserting that eradicating drugs is its “biggest priority,” the Opposition parties have accused the AAP of failing to curb the drug menace and instead patronising the drug trade.

articles.title: Cyclone 'Akvan' LIVE updates: Akvan to become a severe cyclone tonight
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The clouds associated with the system are projected to bring light to moderate rainfall at some parts of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal
Cyclone Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm over Bay of Bengal by the morning of 19 November 2026.
Very slow north-northwestward movement of Cyclone Akvan over central parts of South and adjoining Westcentral BoB at 0830 IST of today.
It will become a Severe Cyclone tonight, moving northwestwards become Very Severe Cyclone on 19 evening, to cross Andhra Pradesh coast around 20th noon.

Cyclone Akvan, expected to form over the Bay of Bengal on Monday evening, is very likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni by noon on November 20 as a very severe cyclonic storm, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in its forecast on Monday (November 16, 2026). Winds at landfall may reach 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph.
Cyclone Akvan is likely to hit the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Tuni by noon on November 20 with winds of up to 145 kmph. Check its path here.

The Odisha government yesterday geared up for the possible impact of Cyclone Akvan, the third cyclonic storm formed over the Bay of Bengal in three weeks, with the deployment of 74 rescue teams and early evacuation of vulnerable people in the southern districts.
Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari held a meeting to review preparedness based on the latest IMD forecast and said the government made “full arrangements to secure lives and property”.

According to the latest bulletin issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), a deep depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal moved with a speed of 10 kmph during the past six hours till 5.30 pm, and intensified into a cyclonic storm Akvan.
It lay centred at a distance of 790 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha.

It is very likely to turn into a very severe cyclonic storm around November 19 morning and cross Andhra Pradesh between Nellore and Tuni, around noon the next day, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph, the IMD said.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Monday (November 16, 2026) reviewed preparations for the deep depression over the Bay of Bengal, which is likely to intensify into Cyclone Akvan by evening, at the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) centre in the State Secretariat.
Cyclone Akvan is set to hit the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 20. CM Naidu reviewed preparedness as 173 fishing boats were yet to return.

articles.title: Calcutta High Court issues criminal contempt proceedings against Abhishek Banerjee
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice Krishna Rao had said that by his remarks on November 7, Abhishek Banerjee had committed criminal contempt of the court” and “attempted with interference of administration of justice

The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) initiated criminal contempt proceedings against Diamond Harbour MP and Mamata All India Trinamool Congress leader Abhishek Banerjee over his remarks allegedly casting aspersions on a sitting judge.

Justice Krishna Rao said that he has gone through the transcript of Abhishek Banerjee’s speech and his facebook post on November 7, which clearly indicates that he has “committed criminal contempt of the court” and “attempted with interference of administration of justice”. He also added that remarks amounted to “scandalising the court”.
The court said the alleged contemnor has to explain within 15 days as to why appropriate action should not be taken against Mr. Banerjee.

Justice Rao, on November 13, had taken exception to Mr. Banerjee’s remarks, observing that an elected representative and an educated person could not be treated like an ordinary layperson. “You ask your client, who are the judges with the BJP and who aren’t... since he is so intelligent, let him give a list. I will see,” Justice Rao had remarked. The Court had said “Your client is writing the ACR [Annual Confidential Report] of the judges”.

On November 7, when a scuffle had erupted outside his residence, Mr. Banerjee claimed that he was attacked seven times in six months and said that he was not granted the desired protection from the judiciary.

The residence of Mr. Banerjee was attacked allegedly by BJP supporters in the early hours of November 7 and the three term MP vented his ire against the judiciary. Only a few days ago, the Trinamool MP had said that his party” lost elections not to the BJP but to the Supreme Court of India”.

Mr. Banerjee had approached the bench of Justice Rao challenging the State government’s decision to downgrade his security. On the petition of Diamond Harbour MP Justice Rao directed the West Bengal Government to review his security arrangements. The Court directed the Principal Secretary, Home and Hill Affairs Department of the West Bengal government to convene for a review committee meeting within two weeks of the order.

articles.title: Bilkis Bano says Supreme Court did not inform or hear her before granting bail to two convicts; vows to fight order
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The short order, published recently on the court website, had reasoned that the two men had already undergone more than 17 years in prison and one of them suffered a severe handicap

Bilkis Bano, who survived gangrape and the murder of her family during the 2002 Gujarat riots, has issued a statement conveying her “pain, shock and disbelief” at the Supreme Court’s decision to grant bail and suspend the life imprisonment of two men convicted of the crimes that changed her life forever.
Ms. Bano, through her counsel senior advocate Shobha Gupta, stated she was neither informed nor heard before the order was passed on October 28.

“I still cannot believe that once again, for the second time, an order has been passed by the Supreme Court without calling me up and without hearing me. I learnt of this through press reports,” her statement read.

A Bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale, on October 28, had suspended the life sentences of Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya, who were two of the 11 men convicted of gangraping the then 19-year-old Ms. Bano and murdering 14 members of her family, including her infant daughter, in 2002.
The short order, published recently on the court website, had reasoned that the two men had already undergone more than 17 years in prison and one of them suffered a severe handicap.

The apex court order for the duo’s release on bail came in an appeal filed by them against a 2017 Bombay High Court judgment upholding a CBI court decision of 2008, convicting the men and sentencing them to life terms in prison.
The two convicts had only arraigned the States of Gujarat and Maharashtra, where the trial was transferred to on a Supreme Court order, in their appeal.

“How could the Honourable Supreme Court simply suspend the sentence if the men who did this to me? How could they not even inform me? How could they not even make sure my voice was heard in their courtroom?” Ms. Bano asked.
In 2024, the apex court had quashed the order of en masse remission granted by the State of Gujarat in August 2022 to the 11 men.

The court had then empathised with Ms. Bano, noting how she had been “coerced to live the life of a nomad and an orphan… the gruesome and horrific acts of violence have left an indelible imprint on her mind which will continue to torment and cripple her”.
In her statement on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), Ms. Bano said she had “rebuilt from the rubble of my life… learned to smile”, but the October 28 order has made her scared, once again.
Ms. Bano stated she would fight the October 28 order granting bail to the two convicts.

articles.title: SIR row: Supreme Court to hear Rahul Gandhi’s application on December 9
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The affidavit asserted that the massive exercise (SIR), in which approximately 13 crore voters were excluded, was a unanimous decision of the ECI

The Supreme Court has agreed to hear an application filed by the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi , and leaders of the INDIA bloc , posing 48 interrogatories to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), Election Commissioners, and senior ECI officials regarding the conduct of the Service Information Report (SIR) and the veracity of the claims made in an October 26 affidavit filed by the poll body.
The affidavit asserted that the massive exercise (SIR), in which approximately 13 crore voters were excluded, was a unanimous decision of the ECI.
A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant posted the case for December 9.

The petitions were originally listed for Tuesday (November 17, 2026). However, while the Bench was rising for lunch break, senior advocate Harish Salve, appearing for the Election Commission of India, enquired whether there would be enough time to hear all of the petitions.
Mr. Salve said there was already a Special Bench scheduled later in the afternoon, and suggested an adjournment to a later date.

Mr. Gandhi, on Monday (November 16), told the Supreme Court that the ECI failed to produce any proof to establish its claim that the special intensive revision (SIR) was a “unanimous” decision made by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

The reported friction between Mr. Kumar and the two Election Commissioners over the SIR and the CEC’s allegedly unilateral and authoritarian conduct had triggered widespread protests across India demanding his removal from office.

The ECI’s October 26 affidavit, in response to a petition filed by INDIA bloc leaders led by Mr. Gandhi, denied any differences of opinion between the CEC and the Election Commissioners over the SIR process.

Mr. Gandhi said the court must not accept such “bare assertions” from the ECI. He questioned why the affidavit was filed by the ECI when Mr. Kumar, Mr. Sandhu and Mr. Joshi were separately made respondents.

The Opposition leader, represented by senior advocate A.M. Singhvi and advocate Prasanna S., said the ECI chose not to explain when and where exactly the decision to conduct a nationwide SIR was made.

articles.title: Export duty on diesel hiked ₹2.5/litre, ATF ₹1.5/litre, petrol remains nil
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The government late Monday (November 16, 2026) hiked the export duty on diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹2.5 per litre and ₹1.5 per litre, whilst keeping the levy on export of petrol unchanged at nil.
Duty rates on petrol and diesel meant for domestic consumption remain unchanged.
The hike in diesel levy assumes added significance as India looks to further up their exports of the vehicular fuel to Europe amid a global supply crunch.
In the upcoming fortnight, diesel exports would draw a levy of ₹14 per litre compared to ₹11.5 per litre mandated for the previous fortnight.
ATF exports would draw a levy of ₹12.5 per litre against ₹11 per litre.

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

articles.title: Head of China’s Baidu warns of AI ‘bubble’ ahead of APEC talks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Chinese President Xi Jinping is due to hold talks with U.S. counterpart Donald Trump on Thursday during APEC

Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption is not boosting profits for most companies, the head of Chinese technology giant Baidu said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), ahead of talks on the sensitive sector between the world's top two economies.

The health of the global AI investment boom is under question, as U.S. chip titan Nvidia reports quarterly results later in the day -- its first since former CEO Jensen Huang quit over a widening affair scandal .

Robin Li, chief executive of Baidu, spoke during a panel discussion with business leaders in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, which this week hosts the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting.
Asked about the current global landscape for the technology, Mr. Li called the situation "urgent".
The "penetration and expansion of AI into the application layer has arguably fallen short of expectations", he said.
"While there is intense competition at the foundational level, can we say that companies are seeing higher revenues or increased profits after adopting AI?" Mr. Li asked.
"For most, the answer is no. If we fail to address this, the concern that AI might be a bubble could well become a reality," he added.
Chinese President Xi Jinping is due to hold talks with U.S. counterpart Donald Trump on Thursday (November 19) during APEC.
They are expected to discuss the risks posed by AI as calls grow for cooperation between the two tech powerhouses despite their fierce rivalry in the field.
Baidu, sometimes called China's Google, has made an aggressive push into AI in recent years.
But its challenges have grown as a domestic consumer slump drags on cash flows generated by advertising.

On Monday (November 16), the Beijing-based search engine provider posted a sixth straight drop in quarterly revenue, as Li acknowledged "headwinds in online marketing" despite "tangible results" in the company's AI strategy.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: We may meet with Kim Jong Un also, so that'll be good, Donald Trump told reporters

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un smoked and grinned as he visited a ski resort in pictures released on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), as Donald Trump hinted at a possible meeting between the pair this week.
Before departing for China, U.S. President Trump, who met Mr. Kim three times during his first term, left open the possibility of meeting the North Korean leader.
"We may meet with Kim Jong Un also, so that'll be good," Mr. Trump told reporters, adding that whether Kim would make the trip was "up to President Xi" of China.

As Mr. Trump made the remarks, North Korean state media reported that Kim and his family, accompanied by party officials, travelled to a tourist zone near the northern border with China on Sunday (November 15) and Monday (November 16).

Photos released by the official Korean Central News Agency show Kim sitting on a leather chair, grinning, with a cigarette in his hand and sunglasses on, at what appeared to be a ski resort, with his wife Ri Sol Ju standing behind him.
Another photo shows his young daughter Ju Ae, whom Seoul's spy agency has said is being groomed to be Kim's successor, skiing downhill in a white outfit but without a helmet.
The city of Samjiyon is located near the Chinese border and is close to Mount Paektu, considered by North Koreans to be the sacred birthplace of Kim's father, Jong Il.

As he toured the resort, including ski centres and hotels, Kim "expressed great satisfaction, saying that all the structures are really impeccable as they were built in a delicate way", KCNA reported.
"The more he looked at it, the more admiration he felt at the spectacular scenery reminiscent of a town in the forest," it said.

While Mr. Kim made the visit near China, which is hosting the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in the southern city of Shenzhen, experts say it was unlikely intended to signal plans to travel to the summit.
The straight-line distance between the two cities is more than 2,500 kilometres (1,553 miles).

"The KCNA report does not contain any message aimed at the United States, and there are no signs of preparations for a meeting," Hong Min, a senior researcher at the Korea Institute for National Unification, told AFP .

articles.title: PM Modi leads foundation stone-laying ceremony for Philippines’ oldest gurudwara’s redevelopment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: PM Narendra Modi, who is on a three-day visit to the Philippines, said he felt "very blessed" to visit the over a century-old Gurudwara Khalsa Diwan in Manila
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) visited the oldest gurudwara in the Philippines and led the foundation stone-laying ceremony for its redevelopment.
Mr. Modi, who is on a three-day visit to the Philippines, said he felt "very blessed" to visit the over a century-old Gurudwara Khalsa Diwan in Manila.
Several dignitaries were present at the occasion, including Senator Francis Joseph Escudero and Mayor of Manila City Francisco Isko Moreno.

"The Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara has stood as a testament to the vibrant India-Philippines cultural and people-to-people ties for over a century," the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a social media post.
On Monday (November 16, 2026), Mr. Modi said the gurudwara is a centre of immense spiritual significance.
ALSO WATCH Watch: PM Modi in Manila for ASEAN, Quad and East Asia Summits | Above the Fold | Nov 16, 2026
"Inspired by the teachings of the Guru Sahibs, the Sikh community has made a mark globally, being at the forefront of serving others and building a better planet," he said in a post on X.
The gurudwara was originally established in 1901 and formally organised in 1903. It was registered as Khalsa Diwan in 1924, according to the MEA.

"The Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara holds a unique distinction of being the oldest Gurudwara in the Philippines. It continues to play an important role through its spiritual, cultural and philanthropic activities for the Sikh and other communities in Manila," it said.

Mr. Modi arrived in the Philippines on Monday (November 16, 2026) to attend the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit, aiming to strengthen ties with Southeast Asian and East Asian nations and to discuss regional and global challenges.

articles.title: Singapore seeks ‘trusted access’ to AI chips after new US curbs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Singapore is finding itself at the centre of the controversy as cloud computing firm Megaspeed, suspected of helping Chinese firms get around US export controls, is based there

Singapore said Tuesday (November 17, 2026) it was seeking “trusted access” to advanced AI chips after the United States imposed new curbs aimed at stopping Chinese firms from accessing the technology through overseas data centres.

The curbs came days after a spy scandal forced Jensen Huang to quit as Nvidia chief, as questions emerged over whether Singapore-based Megaspeed aided Chinese firms in accessing advanced artificial intelligence chips in violation of US rules.
“We are studying the details of this new measure carefully,” Singapore’s ministries overseeing digital development and energy, trade and industry said in a joint statement.
“We are engaging affected companies to understand the potential impact on their businesses,” the ministries added.

The city-state was also talking to the “relevant US authorities on the scope and implementation of the measure, as well as exploring how to facilitate trusted access for Singapore companies”, the ministries added.
One loophole allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centres in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.

Under the new rule, data centres anywhere in the world will need a US licence to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.
The rule also requires licences to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, which the US commerce department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion”.
Singapore is finding itself at the centre of the controversy as cloud computing firm Megaspeed, suspected of helping Chinese firms get around US export controls, is based there.

The scandal erupted on November 8 when The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang and Megaspeed executive Alice Huang -- who are not related -- were romantically linked, and that some within the US government suspected she might be a spy for China.
The city-state is battling to contain the damage to its reputation as a stable rules-based business hub and trusted destination for multinational investment.

“We take our international reputation seriously and do not condone companies using their association with Singapore to circumvent or violate the laws of other countries in their international business activities, including export controls,” Singapore said.

articles.title: U.S. federal court strikes down fixed terms for student, exchange visas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: In July, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposed a policy aimed at preventing international students from staying in the country for more than four years unless they obtained federal approval
A U.S. federal court has struck down a Trump administration proposal to cap the amount of time foreign students, scholars, and journalists can spend in the country on their respective visas.

In July, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposed a policy aimed at preventing international students from staying in the country for more than four years unless they obtained federal approval.

Boston federal Judge F. Dennis Saylor delivered a ruling on Monday (November 16, 2026) striking down the DHS proposal as "arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and otherwise not in accordance with law."

"Put bluntly, DHS is seeking to prevent or discourage the very activity — providing educational opportunities for foreign students in the United States — that Congress sought to permit and encourage," Judge Saylor said in his ruling.
"The statute simply does not grant DHS such broad and open-ended authority to undermine the F-1 visa programme," he added.
The proposed rule also sought to shorten how long foreign journalists can stay in the country from several years to 240 days – or 90 days for Chinese journalists.
The proposed rule also shortened the grace period – the window to depart after finishing studies or post-completion OPT from 60 days to 30.
For language programmes, there was an aggregate limit of 24 months for stays, including breaks and vacations.
The Foundation for India and Indian Diaspora Studies (FIIDS) welcomed the federal court order.

"Once again, the court has come to the rescue of international students — and, in doing so, has helped protect the future of American science, technology, research, and innovation," said FIIDS President and Chief of Policy and Strategy, Khanderao Kand.

Miriam Feldblum, president and CEO of the Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Education, one of the lead plaintiffs, termed the federal court ruling as a clear and important victory for international students and scholars and the colleges and universities that welcome them.

"The harmful consequences of the current administration's policy actions and efforts are already evident in the significant declines in international student enrolment and interest we are witnessing," Ms. Feldblum said in a statement.

fullParagraphs: Intermittent spells of rain, followed by hot and humid weather, have led to a spike in dengue cases in Thiruvananthapuram, even as the overall trend in dengue cases across the State has been on a slow decline since July

The Karyavattom campus of Kerala University (KU) has emerged as a hotspot of dengue in the city, where over 50 cases have been reported since November 9. Health department suspects that this is a gross underestimation, as the transmission is likely to have begun weeks before

Intermittent spells of rain, followed by hot and humid weather, have led to the spike in dengue cases in Thiruvananthapuram, even when the general dengue case trend has been on a slow decline since July across the State.
In the last 10 days, Thiruvananthapuram district has reported 200 probable cases of dengue and 97 confirmed cases.

On Monday, following a meeting called by the Health department, which was joined by the Vice Chancellor, some KU syndicate members as well as public health experts of the School of Public Health under Kerala University of Health Sciences, it was decided to shut the Karyavattom campus and the hostel buildings for three days so that intense vector control measures can be taken up and a break in disease transmission can be achieved.

“District health officials and vector control teams had visited the campus and hostel and we found that solid waste management was a huge issue in the campus. Plastic disposable containers used for food delivery which are disposed of carelessly are emerging as a major contributor to vector breeding in urban areas.. Rain water stagnation in these containers which are strewn around is a major hazard. Indoor plants in hostel rooms, broken manholes and blocked drains leading to rainwater stagnation have all led to intense mosquito breeding inside the vast campus,” a senior Health official said.

The Health department has also decided to serve notice to the KU Registrar under the Kerala Public Health Act, for allowing the campus to be a breeding ground for mosquitoes and posing a public health issue

Teams from the Pangappara health centre have been at work on the campus since November 10 but the district vector control team and the Corporation health staff will be joining them now. Fogging will be done to kill adult mosquitoes and indoor space spraying inside the hostel room, which will be accompanied by a source reduction campaign, officials said.
The district health administration has identified several pockets of dengue within the city itself, where an abundance of breeding sources and intense vector breeding has been spotted
Health officials point out that several large government properties with vast, ill-maintained grounds are also turning out to be hotspots for dengue in the city.

“The Cliff House compound and the sprawling official bungalows around it are all major breeding grounds for mosquitoes. In the Cliff House, seven police personnel there on guard duty were down with dengue, following which a district health team had visited the location. In some of the bungalows where renovation works are going on, building materials and discarded parts of equipment are all thrown about carelessly, leading to rain water stagnation and mosquito breeding,” a health official said.
Health officials said that without public participation, source reduction and mosquito control cannot be taken up successfully.
Kollam district too has reported a significant number of dengue cases over the last 10 days.

articles.title: Call for cancellation of TNMSC’s tenders for repair works at TASMAC warehouses in Tamil Nadu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Tamil Nadu Medical Officers Association (TNMOA) has urged the Chief Minister, Health Minister and Managing Director of Tamil Nadu Medical Services (TNMSC) to cancel the corporation’s recent tenders to carry out repair works at warehouses of Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (TASMAC) and to direct that the works be undertaken through the Public Works Department or another agency.

When TNMSC was earlier made to procure gold coins (for ‘Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam’ ), it drew strong criticism. Now, using TNMSC to take up repair works at TASMAC warehouses is strongly condemnable, TNMOA said in a statement.
Symbolism or substance? Tamil Nadu’s public health professionals question gold ring scheme
Gold ring scheme for newborn babies in Tamil Nadu: Doctors’ body flags high security, logistics costs
Earlier, The Hindu had reported that TNMSC has invited tenders for special repairs at TASMAC warehouses in three locations.

TNMSC was established to procure quality medical equipment and medicines at affordable cost for the Health department, it said. The association said that already, several irregularities were reported in TNMSC’s core function of procuring medicines. There were repeated instances of TNMSC issuing ‘No Objection Certificates’ instead of procuring essential medicines and asking college deans and joint directors to purchase them using funds under the Chief Minister’s Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme (CMCHIS).

The association expressed concern that instead of addressing the shortcomings and strengthening TNMSC, a model agency in the country, the State government is taking steps that undermine the institution.

articles.title: How does India address service outages?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Does Indian law require Microsoft to have reported the recent outage that affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite? What rules apply in such situations and what are their shortcomings in the present form? How are cloud companies accountable in other countries? What are Indian customers’ options?

From November 12 to 13, an as-yet unspecified problem with Microsoft infrastructure affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite Microsoft 365 worldwide, including its Outlook email service. Microsoft apologised during the outage and attributed the incident to a fault in an upgrade of its network capacity, although more precise details are still expected.
In India, among consequences in various sectors, IndiGo and Akasa Air alerted passengers of disruptions to their email support while Air India rerouted its email.

articles.title: Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart features drive market growth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks

Demand for air purifiers in India has witnessed explosive growth in 2026, with major brands and retail platforms reporting sales doubling or tripling year-on-year. Driven by an early surge ahead of the traditional winter pollution season , consumer behaviour is shifting toward viewing indoor air quality as a year-round health priority rather than an emergency seasonal purchase.
According to industry leaders, adoption is gaining momentum well before peak pollution months.

Smart tech brand Qubo recorded a 150 percent growth over the previous year, while Xiaomi registered approximately 3X year-on-year sales growth during the festive period. Industry executives note that growing awareness surrounding indoor pollutants, ranging from dust and pet dander to everyday cooking and cleaning emissions, is encouraging households to take a proactive approach to home wellness throughout the year.

Retail footprint and online traffic reflect this expanding market footprint across the country. Electronics retailer Croma reported that air purifier sales volumes have more than doubled in 2026. While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks.
Premium tech maker Dyson also reported that visits to its air purifier pages grew by over 100 percent in October compared to the same period last year.

Modern buyers are increasingly seeking advanced functionality and intelligent filtration tech. Croma highlighted strong consumer interest in models featuring real-time AQI displays, app controls, and multi-functional units combining purification with humidification or heating.

On e-commerce platforms, Amazon India reported that sales doubled over the past week. Shoppers are actively leveraging Rufus, Amazon’s personalised AI shopping assistant, to filter models by room size, filter type, and live sensor capabilities, prompting the e-retailer to expand selection on Amazon Now for immediate delivery.

articles.title: What to know about the online banking delays affecting major U.S. banks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused problems throughout the financial system on Monday (November 16, 2026), resulting in thousands of customers reporting difficulty accessing online accounts at several major U.S. banks and the money transfer service Zelle.

JPMorgan Chase, the largest U.S. bank by total assets, said a software bug was affecting its internal hardware systems and causing transaction delays. The company was working to bring banking services back online.
Some Chase customers received a message that said, "Some services aren't available. We're working on them. Please try back later."

In a sense, yes. Customers at Bank of America, Citigroup and other banks trying to transact with Chase may have seen their transactions slow, even though those banks were not having issues with their services.
"Other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," explained Joe Evangelisti, a spokesperson for Chase.
Zelle was not directly affected by the Chase glitch. But customers at other banks may have experienced transaction delays while trying to send or receive Zelle payments involving a Chase customer.

Zelle is a rapid peer-to-peer payment system used by major US banks. The platform is owned by Arizona-based Early Warning Services, which in turn is owned by financial institutions including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, US Bank and Wells Fargo.
A spokesperson for Early Warning Services said the Zelle network was fully operational.
Chase said that the technical problem was not the result of a cyberattack, stressing that it was an isolated incident and not related to anything other than a bug.
Chase said its customers still have access to their accounts and funds. The company expects the issue to be resolved by the end of day Monday.
No. While the disruptions took place just days apart, government officials and company leaders have said they were unrelated.

The major outage by Microsoft on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that lasted for hours, severely impacting services including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, was due to a technical issue that arose during an upgrade. The tech giant has said there is "no indication" that the disruptions were caused by malicious activity, such as a cyberattack or due to action by artificial intelligence agents.

fullParagraphs: Apple stood at number four position with a 10.1% share, as the sharp decline across Chinese brands lifted its position in a shrinking market, even as Apple’s own shipments fell 25% YoY after a flat Q2

India’s smartphone market dropped by 23.3% year-over-year (YoY ) during Q3 2026 to reach 36.8 million units shipments. It was the steepest quarterly contraction since Q4 2022 and also the weakest festive quarter in a decade, said IDC.
The research firm credited rising memory chip costs, pushed up by AI-driven demands , tightened component availability for the decline that led a very little room for vendors to hold prices.

Smartphone’s average selling price (ASP) was at a record high ($371), a 26% YoY growth, festive offers were a few, and due to that price-sensitive buyers held back purchases this season, and pressure is likely to carry into Q4 2026.

Samsung emerged as the top smartphone brand with a 17.7% share during Q3, followed by Vivo with a 16.8% share and Oppo having a 13.3% share. Vivo had a nearly 30% drop in shipments compared to Q3 2025, while Oppo’s fell by around 27%.

Apple stood at number four position with a 10.1% share, as the sharp decline across Chinese brands lifted its position in a shrinking market, even as Apple’s own shipments fell 25% YoY after a flat Q2.

Supply shortages on the iPhone 15, 16 and 17, along with price increases around the September launches, weighed on volumes, and less offers on older-generation iPhones cooled demand from aspirational buyers.

4G shipments declined 15.5% YoY against 24.1% for 5G, nudging 4G’s share up to 10.4% from 9.5%. The gain comes from 5G falling faster as vendors retained 4G options at entry-level price points, with no sign of renewed 4G demand.

The $200–400 band held flat (+0.1% YoY) in a shrinking market, while $400–600 surged 79.8%. articles.title: Bird flu confirmed at two farms in Keralam’s Alappuzha; 26,000 birds to be culled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Six rapid response teams of Animal Husbandry and Health departments set to carry out culling

Bird flu has been confirmed at two poultry farms in Alappuzha district of Keralam, and authorities will begin culling around 26,000 birds on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) to prevent the spread of the infection, officials said.

Around 26,000 domestic birds within a 1-km radius of the affected farms in Ambalappuzha North, Ambalappuzha South and Chennithala panchayats are likely to be culled, they said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
The infection was detected among quails and chickens at a farm in Ward 11 of Ambalappuzha North and among ducks and chickens at a farm in Ward 1 of Chennithala panchayat.
Samples collected from the farms tested positive for bird flu at the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal.
According to a preliminary estimate, 10,044 birds in Ambalappuzha North alone will have to be culled as part of the operation.
Six rapid response teams of the Animal Husbandry and Health departments will carry out the culling on Wednesday.
Each team will comprise a doctor, two livestock inspectors, two attendants and four workers.
Representatives of the local panchayats, police, revenue officials and local body employees will also assist the teams.
Two additional teams have been kept on standby, officials said.
An area within a 10-km radius of the affected farms has been declared a surveillance zone.
District Collector Shaji V Nair convened an emergency meeting to review the situation and coordinate preventive measures.

Deputy Collector (Disaster Management) S Biju, Chief Veterinary Officer Dr P Rajeev and officials from the Health, Police, Local Self-Government, Food Safety and Motor Vehicles departments attended the meeting.

articles.title: Archana Veeramani complains to Madras High Court about SIT digging up her bungalow swimming pool without notice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan directs SIT to allow her lawyer to be present, away from earshot distance, during her interrogation

Serial child sexual abuse case accused ‘Gem Granites’ R. Veeramani’ s daughter Archana Veeramani on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) complained to the Madras High Court that a Special Investigation Team (SIT) had dug up the swimming pool in her house on Saturday (November 14) in search of a body of a child victim but could not find anything.

Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, senior counsel Nitya Ramakrishnan, representing Ms. Archana, said, the police had carried out the excavation operation in the residential house at Chennai without any notice either to her client or her aged mother who has been residing over there ever since the accused got arrested on August 29 .

The counsel insisted that the SIT must be directed to issue an advance notice to Ms. Archana before carrying out any such operation in the residential premises and also allow her lawyer to be present. She questioned as to how the police could indulge in such a rampage in a residential property occupied by two women with one of them being an elderly person.

However, Additional Public Prosecutor Arun Anbumani told the court the police had not entered the building in which the two women were residing and the excavation was carried out only in the open area. He said, the operation was necessitated since a car driver had given a statement that the body of one of the child victims was buried in the bungalow.

After hearing both sides, the judge said, the court could not direct the SIT to issue advance notice while carrying out certain activities as part of the investigation. He, however, ordered that if the police wished to interrogate the two women at their residence, they should permit Ms. Archana’s lawyer to be present away from earshot distance.

The judge also extended till November 24 the time granted to the SIT to file its counter affidavit to a writ petition filed by Ms. Archana accusing the SIT of having indulged in human rights violations when she was forced to deboard from an airplane , bound to Singapore for her son’s medical treatment, on October 23, without any valid authorisation.

Ms. Archana claimed she was not an accused in that case and no court had restrained her from undertaking foreign travel. Yet, the airplane staff had forcefully deboarded her from the airplane, at the instance of the SIT officials, without assigning any reason and she was taken to the office of the SIT for inquiry without considering her health condition, she said.

Stating she was suffering from multiple sclerosis, a chronic autoimmune condition that affects the central nervous system, for about 20 years, the petitioner said she collapsed on the floor of the SIT office and lost control over her bladder. All these events were video recorded by the police despite objections and she was shifted to a hospital for treatment only on the advice of her doctor friend, the petitioner added.

articles.title: Three men arrested for illegal sand mining from Palar riverbed in Vellore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the police, the gang reportedly confessed that the sand was mined from dry riverbed to sell the consignment to retail traders.
Three persons were arrested by Tiruvalam police near Katpadi in Vellore for illegally mining sand from the dry riverbed of Palar on Monday (November 16, 2026).
Police identified the arrested persons as K. Sekar (45), R. Viswanathan (32) and G. Munusamy (37). They are residents of Sekkadu village near Katpadi.

Initial inquiry revealed that special teams were formed in the district to prevent illegal sand mining, smuggling of ganja and other banned substances and petty crime. A police team that was on routine patrol along the river near Katpadi spotted tractors and earthmover in the dry riverbed. The police also found two tractors with loads of river sand.

According to the police, the gang reportedly confessed that the sand was mined from dry riverbed to sell the consignment to retail traders. They were arrested. Two tractors and an earthmover were seized from them.

articles.title: ASEAN Summit LIVE updates: President Trump arrives in Manila to hold discussions with Quad leaders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In the first Quad Summit since 2024, PM Modi is expected to meet U.S. President Trump, Japanese PM Takaichi and Australian PM Albanese
U.S. President Donald Trump arrived in Manila today, where he is scheduled to meet regional partners, talk trade, and seek a break from a series of setbacks at home.

Upon his arrival, Mr. Trump was welcomed by Philippine Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, Ilocos Norte Representative and presidential son Sandro Marcos, Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manuel Romualdez, U.S. Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton and Pasay City Mayor Emi Calixto.

articles.title: SIR row: Supreme Court agrees to hear INDIA bloc’s ‘interrogatories’ on ‘nationwide SIR’, CEC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The affidavit asserted that the massive exercise (SIR), in which approximately 13 crore voters were excluded, was a unanimous decision of the ECI

The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) agreed to have a detailed hearing of an application filed by Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders, who have posed 48 ‘interrogatories’ to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, and senior poll officials regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The interrogatories challenge the veracity of “bare assertions” made by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in an October 26 affidavit that the decision to hold a nationwide SIR, which saw around 13 crore voters excluded from the electoral rolls, was “unanimous”.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant posted the case for December 9 after senior advocate Harish Salve, appearing for the ECI, enquired if the court would have enough time to hear the multiple petitions in the post-lunch session.

Senior advocates Kapil Sibal, A.M. Singhvi and advocate Prasanna S., for the INDIA bloc leaders, urged the Bench, which was about to rise for lunch after the morning session when Mr. Salve intervened, to issue notice on the application containing the interrogatories.

Though, initially, the court agreed to issue notice to the ECI for a response, Mr. Salve, along with senior advocate Maninder Singh, opposed the issuance of any notice before a preliminary hearing on the application.
“We will then hear the application and pass necessary orders,” the CJI said.

The application was filed as part of the Opposition leaders’ writ petition claiming the nationwide SIR exercise, the manner and extent of its conduct, was the product of a unilateral exercise of power by the CEC without the knowledge, approval or concurrence of the Election Commissioners.

Mr. Gandhi and the Opposition leaders submitted that posing the interrogatories was necessary as the controversy in their petition substantially rested upon facts that lie exclusively within the knowledge and the records of the ECI. The petitioners said they had no means of access to those facts except through the ECI and their officials.
So far, rather than disclosing those facts, the ECI has only made bare assertions.

The Opposition leaders said though the Supreme Court was not fettered by any rigid procedure, ‘interrogatories’ were recognised by the Supreme Court Rules Further, the court was empowered by the Rules to pass any orders “necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the court”.

The interrogatories covered detailed ground, including whether the October 26 affidavit claiming that SIR was a “unanimous decision”, was ever placed before Mr. Sandhu and Mr. Joshi. If so, when and how, and if they had suggested any changes in any assertions made in the document.

The Opposition leaders have asked for the number of the file clearing a nationwide SIR in which the decision of the Commission was taken, the date of the decision, whether it was taken at a meeting, upon circulation of a file or through electronic means, and the date on which each member signified approval.
