🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 17 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Microplastics, 'cocktail' of hazardous chemicals in Delhi's Yamuna, flags study

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

The researchers also identified pharmaceutical compounds such as atomoxetine, domperidone and telmisartan, along with agrochemical-related substances, including diuron and thiamethoxam

Microplastics in the Yamuna in Delhi are accompanied by a complex mixture of organic chemicals, including pharmaceutical residues, pesticides and industrial effluents, with many of these substances classified as human-health and environmental hazards, according to a new study by University of Delhi researchers.

The study, published in the 'Journal of Hazardous Materials Advances ' in September 2026, examines microplastic pollution and associated chemical profiles at eight locations along a 48.8-km stretch of the river in Delhi -- from its entry at Palla to its exit at Asgarpur Jagir -- highlighting how pollution patterns vary across agricultural, residential, industrial, recreational and forested areas.

Researchers recovered 2,289 microplastic particles from the samples, with an average abundance of 3.18 particles per litre. The analysis identified 321 distinct chemical compounds across the samples, of which 50 were detected in extracts of recovered microplastic fractions at four or more locations.

Of these 50 compounds, 36 corresponded to structures with Global Harmonized System (GHS) hazard classifications, covering categories such as carcinogenicity, reproductive toxicity, acute toxicity and aquatic hazards.

Seven compounds were detected across all eight sampling locations, including 2-naphthylamine, lidocaine and monobutyl phthalate, the study found.

The researchers also identified pharmaceutical compounds such as atomoxetine, domperidone and telmisartan, along with agrochemical-related substances, including diuron and thiamethoxam.

Radhey Shyam Sharma, head of the Department of Environmental Studies at University of Delhi and one of the co-authors of the study, said the findings highlight the need to look beyond microplastic particles and examine the complex chemical mixtures present in river ecosystems.

"The microplastics problem, along with this cocktail of organic and inorganic substances, needs to be looked at through the lens of mixture toxicity. The land-use pattern has also been explored in the study," Sharma said.

He stressed the importance of nature-based solutions, including strengthening vegetation along riverbanks and protecting natural river ecosystems, to minimise pollution-related risks.

"Vegetation ecosystems can help prevent pollution from entering the river. Natural ecosystems and riverbanks need to be strengthened to minimise these risks. The focus should be on nature-based solutions," he said.

The study found significant variations in microplastic abundance across the eight locations. The highest concentration was recorded at the recreational-hydraulic site near the barrage, followed by a floodplain area where multiple drains converge.

The lowest abundance was recorded at the agricultural entry point at Palla and a forested stretch of the river.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time improves an already perfect classic
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: One of the best Zelda games, Ocarina of Time, has got a gorgeous new remake that is worth playing, if you have a Switch 2

Remakes of past games are pure genius. There are several titles that were mega hits in the 90s or early 2000s when both silicon and game engines were breaking new ground in 3D. Many of those games do not hold up today as well as the pixel game era of the NES and SNES eras do.

Capcom has shown the world that remaking most of their lineup of Resident Evils has been successful. Ubisoft did it too, with Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag Resynced . No one expected Nintendo to jump into the fray, but they did and with style, not only remaking a Zelda game, but one of the cult favorites from the Nintendo 64 era. A game so loved, that it is continuously ranked as one of the greatest games of all times, which is a risky move to remake.
Fortunately, the Ocarina of Time remake not only wears that crown proudly, but is also the only game this year to challenge the sales might of the neon clad tsunami that is Grand Theft Auto VI .

Another saga begins in the cyclic battle of good versus evil, and it revolves around the only boy in the village without a fairy. Entrusted with the fate of the world Link must stop the evil Ganondorf who is intent on grabbing the Tri-force — an artefact that grants the bearer immense power. Guided by the enigmatic fairy Navi, Link must leave the safety of his home, Kokiri Forest, and journey across the sprawling expanse of Hyrule Field, venturing through perilous dungeons, and shift between childhood and adulthood to claim the Master Sword and become the Hero of Time.

Jumping between time from Link’s adult self to his child form is so meta, it will make you feel like you too are jumping through time with him. As an adult, tethered by responsibilities of adulting, you get to jump back to your childhood — something that is more poignant than nostalgia.

In comparison to some of the more sweeping, complex narratives of today’s fantasy games, Ocarina of Time harks back to a simplistic form of storytelling, which was mostly due to cartridge size restrictions. However, it is a template that many of Zelda’s best games have been set on. First-time players are sure to find Link’s story a refreshing one that focuses on core gameplay mechanics and a beautiful reimagining of the world.

The world is gorgeous and while it is not quite open, it does feel like it has got a lot of freedom of movement. It is great to explore all the temples filled with its well-created puzzles that you may remember the solutions for and see the new renditions of iconic places such as Death Mountain, Hyrule Field, Temple of Time and other faithful to their original designs, but are now a lot more fleshed out.
Much of the world has a lot more detail. So rather than rushing through the game, take in your surroundings and scrutinise houses, because there is environmental storytelling peppered everywhere.

Much of the game has been faithfully translated, but thankfully it is free from the oddities of that N64 controller. In addition to updated control mechanics, there are a lot of quality of life improvements, and those who have played Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom , may find the controls familiar. The motions are fluid, and there are some physics-based systems at play, that make everything from the sword clashes feel solid to the sensation of things being physically there in the world as they bounce around.

Combat gains quality of life improvements, inheriting motion aiming from its predecessors making it more snappy, lively and reactive. It lets you acrobatically dodge, backflip and attack enemies, and hits do feel like they actually connect. The enemy AI and animations have been changed to make those fights all the more nail-biting. This being the Switch 2, there are also motion controls to help you use Hookshot, Longshots, bows for some more dynamic ranged combat, if you preferred using this in the newer Zelda games. The addition of jump mechanics do change the dungeons a bit, meaning instead of having the original jump in certain zones, now you actually have to platform across.

As any Anime fan will tell you, to never venture into the English dubs, because many of them feature some over-the-top voice work. The only nitpick with Ocarina of Time is the voice acting features common thick American accents that are found in those same Anime dubs, that completely feel out of place.

I wish Nintendo had chosen a more neutral accent or even gibberish blips to pass for a more Hyrulic language. The sound design on the whole is great though, especially the music, which features a orchestral rendition of Koji Kendo’s unforgettable score. The best part is is the unlimited fun gamers can have making music on the Ocarina.

articles.title: Assam elephant rescue operation turns violent, eight people arrested
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The incident occurred when Forest personnel tried to guide a female elephant, separated from a herd, back to the jungle it came from

Eight people were detained in central Assam’s Hojai district after they clashed with Forest Department personnel on Monday night (November 16, 2026) during an operation to guide a female elephant back to the jungle it came from.

The Forest officials fired “sera bullets” (pellets) from a pump-action gun to divert the elephant away from a human settlement. Five people were injured in the firing, triggering the mob violence and leaving two personnel injured.
Forest officials claimed three people sustained pellet injuries. The injured, including one of the two personnel, were admitted to a local hospital for treatment.

Divisional Forest Officer Nayan Jyoti Rajbongshi said a herd of elephants from the hills of Karbi Anglong entered the Hawaipur Reserve Forest in Hojai on Monday morning. Barring the female elephant, estimated to be 40 years old, the herd returned to Karbi Anglong a few hours later.
“We received information about the movement of the female elephant, possibly separated from the herd, along a road in a revenue area. We managed to push it into the Hawaipur Reserve Forest,” he said.
However, the elephant emerged from the forest around dusk and headed toward a village. The Forest personnel fired the pellets to drive it away, but some villagers were injured in the process.
“The police brought the situation under control and picked up eight people who clashed with our personnel. The police recorded the statement of our personnel,” Mr. Rajbongshi said.
Wildlife officials said people often obstruct rescue operations by gathering around a wild animal that strays out of a forest.
According to Assam government data tabled in the 126-member Assembly in July, as many as 1,147 people and 246 elephants were killed in human-elephant conflicts in the State since 2016.

articles.title: Rights beyond the pad: making menstrual health services work in every school
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court has recognised menstrual health as a constitutional right and laid down obligations for schools and governments. The real challenge now is making these services function reliably, every month, in every school

The Supreme Court’s January 2026 judgment in Dr. Jaya Thakur v. Government of India recognised menstrual health as part of the right to life under Article 21 and directed States and Union Territories to provide free sanitary napkins, functional gender-segregated toilets, usable water and safe menstrual waste disposal facilities in every government and private school.

The success of this judgment, however, will not be measured in courtrooms. It will be measured in whether a girl can access a sanitary napkin, use a clean toilet with running water and dispose of menstrual waste safely.

articles.title: A period of good governance, says CM; a betrayal of people says Pinarayi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: While Satheesan sought to paint a rosy picture of good governance, development, welfare, and fulfilled promises, Pinarayi Vijayan was scathingly critical of the UDF government
Keralam Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan and the Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan have expressed divergent views on six months of Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government.

Mr. Satheesan sought to paint a rosy picture of good governance, development, welfare, and fulfilled promises. He has claimed a 28 per cent increase in tax revenue. The UDF has also rolled out politically popular goodies, including free travel for women on State transport buses, priority ration cards for financially hard-pressed families, a senior citizens welfare programme and a hike in the honorarium of scheme workers, pre-primary teachers and child carers in anganwadis.

He has also claimed that the government was focused on laying the groundwork for a “New Age Keralam”. The government also touted its legislative successes in passing laws to improve the ease of doing business, slash red tape, and provide investors with a transparent, single-window clearance mechanism.

Mr. Satheesan also dwelt at length on his flagship programme, Mission Samudra, a ₹400 crore maritime development initiative. He has sought to cast the commencement of Export-Import (EXIM) operations from the Vizhinjam International Sea Port as his government’s signature achievement.

Mr. Satheesan also promised citizens two international sea ports, 18 mini airports, aviation-linked industries, and more tech parks to transform Keralam into an economic powerhouse. He promised lakhs of new jobs for Keralam’s educated youth by 2031.
Mr Satheesan also projected Operation Toofan, the law enforcement anti-drug enforcement drive, as an administrative achievement.
In stark contrast, Mr. Vijayan was scathingly critical of the UDF government, calling Mr. Satheesan’s six months of governance a betrayal of the people.

Mr. Vijayan said Mr. Satheesan had “put up Keralam for sale”, opening the door to corruption, including hasty agreements with private entities to purchase electricity at exaggerated rates, citing a “non-existent” power scarcity and dishonestly raising the spectre of economically crippling power cuts.

He accused the UDF of sacrificing the welfare of the coastal community at the altar of mercantilism. He said the UDF had opened the floodgates of environmental exploitation by allowing corporate players to exploit Keralam’s rare earths, including mineral-rich beaches, the fragile marine ecosystem, and green-flagged deep-sea mining.

A period of good governance, says CM; a betrayal of people says Pinarayi

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

While Satheesan sought to paint a rosy picture of good governance, development, welfare, and fulfilled promises, Pinarayi Vijayan was scathingly critical of the UDF government

Keralam Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan and the Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan have expressed divergent views on six months of Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government.

Mr. Satheesan sought to paint a rosy picture of good governance, development, welfare, and fulfilled promises. He has claimed a 28 per cent increase in tax revenue. The UDF has also rolled out politically popular goodies, including free travel for women on State transport buses, priority ration cards for financially hard-pressed families, a senior citizens welfare programme and a hike in the honorarium of scheme workers, pre-primary teachers and child carers in anganwadis.

He has also claimed that the government was focused on laying the groundwork for a “New Age Keralam”. The government also touted its legislative successes in passing laws to improve the ease of doing business, slash red tape, and provide investors with a transparent, single-window clearance mechanism.

Mr. Satheesan also dwelt at length on his flagship programme, Mission Samudra, a ₹400 crore maritime development initiative. He has sought to cast the commencement of Export-Import (EXIM) operations from the Vizhinjam International Sea Port as his government’s signature achievement.

Mr. Satheesan also promised citizens two international sea ports, 18 mini airports, aviation-linked industries, and more tech parks to transform Keralam into an economic powerhouse. He promised lakhs of new jobs for Keralam’s educated youth by 2031.

Mr Satheesan also projected Operation Toofan, the law enforcement anti-drug enforcement drive, as an administrative achievement.

In stark contrast, Mr. Vijayan was scathingly critical of the UDF government, calling Mr. Satheesan’s six months of governance a betrayal of the people.

Mr. Vijayan said Mr. Satheesan had “put up Keralam for sale”, opening the door to corruption, including hasty agreements with private entities to purchase electricity at exaggerated rates, citing a “non-existent” power scarcity and dishonestly raising the spectre of economically crippling power cuts.

He accused the UDF of sacrificing the welfare of the coastal community at the altar of mercantilism. He said the UDF had opened the floodgates of environmental exploitation by allowing corporate players to exploit Keralam’s rare earths, including mineral-rich beaches, the fragile marine ecosystem, and green-flagged deep-sea mining.

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan moves slowly, likely to intensify further by November 18 morning
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Probable landfall between Visakhapatnam and Nellore; isolated heavy rain likely in Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram-Manyam, Srikakulam and Vizianagaram from November 18 evening
Cyclonic storm Akvan (meaning ‘demon’ in Persian) over the central parts of the south and west-central Bay of Bengal may intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by Wednesday morning.

Initially, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast that the weather system would strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening, but the system had either remained stationary or moved slowly.

At 5.30 p.m., the weather system was centred around 590 km east of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 630 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 650 km southeast of Machilipatnam and 650 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and 780 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha.

It may continue to move slowly north-northwestwards and intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal on Wednesday morning, and further into a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday morning.

The system has changed its track slightly, and the probable landfall points may remain between Visakhapatnam and Nellore. Isolated heavy rainfall is likely in the northern districts of Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, and strong winds with speeds of 100 kmph to 110 kmph are likely along the coastal belt from Wednesday evening.

Andhra Pradesh is experiencing a very rare event, since it is not often that a State sees three tropical cyclones crossing its coast within a month, said IMD Director General of Meteorology Mrutyunjay Mohapatra.

Speaking to The Hindu over the phone, he said it is normal for the Bay of Bengal to see three or four tropical cyclones in a year. “What is not normal is that all of them are crossing the coast near Andhra Pradesh.”

A similar event last happened in 1987. And, the reason for this can be attributed to El Nino, he said. “Both 1987 and 2026 have strong similarities. 1987 was a strong El Nino year, with drought conditions. And 2026 is one too,” he said.
Mr. Mohapatra explained that El Nino influences the formation of cyclones in such a way that more of these develop over the southern latitude, which may move towards A.P.
Handling a disaster of this kind has become challenging for the State.

Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) Managing Director and Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) CEO Prakhar Jain called the situation unprecedented. “It is challenging for the government to deal with a third cyclone, Akvan, while still dealing with the aftermath of Arnab and Murasu. A lot of restoration work is underway, and another cyclone at this time adds to the challenges,” Mr. Jain said.
The water retention capacity of soil may also be compromised due to extremely heavy rainfall triggered by the previous two cyclones.

articles.title: World needs peace, stability, predictability: Modi in Manila
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Quad leaders issue joint statement opposing economic and maritime 'coercion' in Indo-Pacific; Modi proposes seafarers’ safety initiative at East Asia Summit, also attends meeting with ASEAN leaders

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) called for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world as he attended the ASEAN-India Summit, the East Asia Summit, and the Quad Leaders’ Summit in Manila, Philippines. He made a number of proposals aimed at maritime security, protecting critical minerals supply chains, and enhancing trade.

The Quad Summit, which was being held for the first time in a non-member country, was hosted by U.S. President Donald Trump and was also attended by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, apart from Mr. Modi. The leaders issued a joint statement opposing economic and maritime “coercion” in the Indo-Pacific, and Mr. Modi announced that India would host the first Quad Business Forum in Mumbai in 2027.

The three back-to-back events had started with Mr. Modi’s meeting with the leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) for the ASEAN-India Summit, where the Prime Minister said the world now needed peace, stability, and predictability more than ever.

“Together, India and ASEAN represent nearly one-fourth of the world’s population. That is why it is essential to ensure that our future is shaped not by competition, but by cooperation,” Mr. Modi told the leaders of Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, and Vietnam. Myanmar’s military junta leader, President Min Aung Laing, was not invited, and the country was represented by an official.
At the event, he also promised that India would give e-visas free of charge to ASEAN tourists.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., and ASEAN leaders pose for an official family photo at the 23rd India-ASEAN Summit, in Manila on Tuesday. Photo: Narendra Modi Photo Gallery/ANI Photo

Following this, Mr. Modi took part in the East Asia Summit, which was attended by the leaders of India, China, Russia, the U.S., Japan, South Korea, and the ASEAN countries. At this summit, he proposed a seafarers’ safety initiative. He said that “whether it is the conflict in Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every effort towards peace”.

The East Asia Summit members also issued a joint declaration on tackling cyber-crime, given the number of online fraud cases originating from Southeast Asian countries. India will host a summit on the issue at the National Forensic Sciences University in Gandhinagar and an East Asia Summit University Heads Conclave at Nalanda.

In this image received on Nov. 17, 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi poses for a group photograph with Philippines' President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., and other world leaders, during 21st East Asia Summit, part of the 49th ASEAN Summit, in Manila, Philippines. Photo: PMO via PTI Photo
The ASEAN engagements were important as Mr. Modi had skipped the summits in Malaysia last year.

Shortly before he left Manila, the Prime Minister met the leaders of the U.S., Australia, and Japan for the Quad Summit, which was last held in 2024. This was the first time that all the Quad leaders have met since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and the blockade in the Strait of Hormuz began more than nine months ago — in a war where at least 23 Indians, mainly seafarers, have been killed.

From left, Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, President Donald Trump and Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese prepare fro a group photo during the meeting of the leaders of the Quad in Manila, Philippines, on November 17, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP

articles.title: Allahabad High Court grants interim bail to Azam Khan, terms arrest by ED as ‘motivated and mala fide’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The ED had apparently not provided the petitioner with written grounds of arrest; he was also taken into custody in the case moments after he was physically released from jail in another case, the court says

The Allahabad High Court on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) granted interim bail to former Uttar Pradesh Minister and Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Mohammad Azam Khan, observing that the arrest of Mr. Khan by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) was “motivated and mala fide ”.

A Division Bench of Justices Rajiv Gupta and Devendra Singh directed Mr. Khan’s release, noting that the Central agency had prima facie failed to follow the mandatory procedure while arresting him in a money laundering case.

“....the petitioner was taken into custody in the instant case moments after he was physically released from the jail in another case (PAN Card Case) after furnishing bail bonds and sureties on 31.2.2026 at 7:10 p.m. at the jail gate itself, which clearly underlines the motivated and malafide nature of the present proceedings,” the High Court said.
The relief will remain in force until the next hearing, scheduled for December 10, 2026.

It further noted that the ED had apparently not provided Mr. Khan with written grounds of arrest before producing him before the court for remand. Also, the arrest memo and the reasons for his arrest did not appear to have been properly communicated to him.

Mr. Khan was arrested on October 31, 2026, shortly after he was released from Rampur District Jail in another case involving allegations related to dual PAN cards. He had secured bail in that case from the Allahabad High Court on October 29, and was physically released after furnishing bail bonds and sureties on October 31. However, the ED arrested him again at the gate of the jail at around 7.10 p.m.

Challenging his arrest, Mr. Khan argued that the ED had violated his fundamental rights under Article 22(1) of the Constitution and Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), which lay down safeguards that must be followed during an arrest.

His counsel, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, told the court that the written grounds of arrest were neither handed over to Mr. Khan at the time of arrest nor provided before he was produced for remand the following day. The ED had claimed that its officers tried to hand over the documents but Khan refused to accept them.

The court further observed that although the ED claimed to have videographed the arrest, it had not produced any video or photograph showing its officers offering the documents to Mr. Khan, and him refusing to accept them. The court also noted that the ED had not mentioned the alleged videography in its remand application.
The ED’s explanation required further examination and directed both sides to exchange affidavits before the next hearing, the court said.

The ED’s money-laundering investigation centres on alleged financial irregularities and illegal occupation of farmers’ agricultural land linked to the Rampur-based Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. The agency has alleged that funds and materials allocated for public projects were diverted to the university, government works were carried out on its private campus, and donations to the Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust were routed through contractors holding government contracts. A special PMLA court in Ghaziabad remanded Mr. Khan to judicial custody on November 1.
Uttar Pradesh / Samajwadi Party / Enforcement Directorate

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: RMC forecasts moderate rainfall for Chennai on Wednesday
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The RMC has forecast moderate rainfall at isolated places in Chennai, Tiruvallur and Chengalpattu districts on Wednesday

Even as Cyclone Akvan gathers strength over the Bay of Bengal, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) here has forecast moderate rainfall at isolated places in Chennai, Tiruvallur and Chengalpattu districts on Wednesday.
Light rain is also likely at isolated places over south Tamil Nadu, the rest of north coastal Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal. Dry weather is likely to prevail over the rest of the State.

For Thursday, the RMC has forecast heavy rain at isolated places in Chennai and Tiruvallur districts. Moderate rain is likely at isolated places in Chengalpattu, Kanchipuram, Villupuram and Cuddalore districts, as well as in Puducherry. Light rain is likely at isolated places over the Western Ghats districts. Dry weather is likely to prevail over the rest of the State and Karaikal.

Meanwhile, Cyclone Akvan moved northwestwards and lay centred at 8.30 a.m. on Tuesday about 610 km east of Chennai. It is very likely to move slowly north-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over the westcentral Bay of Bengal by the evening of November 17, 2026.

Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday morning. The system is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around Thursday noon, with a maximum sustained wind speed of 120–130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph.

articles.title: Rising prices reflect government’s economic mismanagement: Congress
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Monthly costs up by over 20% for 61% of families, according to a survey cited by Congress leader Jairam Ramesh; claims PM is more pre-occupied with politics than tackling the inflation crisis

The Congress on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) accused the Union government of fuelling inflation through its “economic mismanagement and anti-people policies” and alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi remained preoccupied with politics rather than addressing the economic distress faced by households and businesses.

Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh cited a survey which found that, for 61% of families across the country, monthly household expenditure had risen by more than 20% over the past year. While 74% of respondents were cutting back on non-essential spending, 50% had reduced purchases of essential goods, he said.
Citing the survey, Mr. Ramesh said prices of ghee and edible oils had risen by 75%, vegetables by 73%, cereals by 71%, milk and dairy products by 65%, and pulses by 62%.

He also claimed that 200 garment factories had shut down in Noida over the past year, citing the impact of U.S. tariffs, high input costs, and government apathy. He said the closures reflected the wider distress in the textile industry.

“People’s plates are shrinking, and factories are being locked down. Yet, the Prime Minister’s only concern remains politics,” he said on X, accusing the government of failing to acknowledge people’s hardships or offer relief.

articles.title: NATO allies to discuss U.S. troop levels with Pentagon strategy chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unveiled the six-month review in June and threatened to withhold some ‌U.S. dues to NATO if “free riding” allies fell short of defence spending commitments

NATO allies will discuss Washington’s review of U.S. troop levels in ​Europe with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), German Defence ⁠Minister Boris Pistorius said, with more clarity on the scope of any drawdown expected within weeks.
U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unveiled the six-month review in June and threatened to withhold some ‌U.S. dues to NATO if “free riding” allies fell short of defence spending commitments.

He did not explicitly say the review could lead to cuts ‌in the 80,000 U.S. troops deployed to Europe, but stressed the goal of ‌prompting ⁠the continent to do more while enabling the U.S. military to ⁠meet global commitments.
“We expect changes in troop levels, but we don’t know anything concrete yet,” Mr. Pistorius said ahead of a meeting with his EU counterparts in Brussels that Colby will join for a working ​lunch.
“But again, a shift in ‌the balance of conventional forces would have occurred under any other U.S. President, due to increased engagement in the Indo-Pacific.”
Germany hosts about 35,000 U.S. troops, the largest American military presence in Europe. The result of the review is expected ‌to be presented before Christmas.
European military sources have speculated Washington might move ​a brigade or some 5,000 troops from Germany either to Asia or closer to NATO’s eastern flank in Poland.
Mr. Pistorius said the ⁠current talks aimed for coordination with Washington to prevent dangerous gaps in NATO’s European defences caused by any U.S. drawdown.

Later Mr. Colby ‌will join a meeting of the so-called Ramstein Group of Ukraine’s military supporters at NATO headquarters to discuss how to supply more arms to Kyiv ahead of a harsh winter, while Russia steps up air strikes on civilian infrastructure.

Mr. Pistorius said Germany and Norway would sponsor another package of US weapons under the PURL programme, focusing on supplying more PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles for the Patriot air defence ‌system to Ukraine.
“This is the fifth package in which Germany is participating. This time, we are ​providing $300 million,” Mr. Pistorius said.
Germany is working to integrate its IRIS-T missile with Norwegian NASAMS air defence systems and will deliver additional radars, drone ammunition ⁠and fighter jets to Kyiv, he said.

articles.title: Nabeel Rajab, prominent Bahraini human rights activist, dies at 62
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Nabeel Rajab, a prominent democracy activist in Bahrain who helped lead the island nation's 2011 protests known across the wider region as the Arab Spring and who spent years in prison for challenging its monarchy, died on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). He was 62.

His family found him unresponsive at their home in Turkey on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) morning, activists said. The Bahrain Center for Human Rights, which Rajab once led as president, confirmed his death in a post on X.

"We extend our sincere condolences and heartfelt sympathy to his esteemed family. We pray that God may encompass him with his vast mercy and reward him abundantly for his efforts and contributions," the group wrote.

Ebrahim Sharif, an activist who was a close friend of the family, said Rajab's wife and daughter found him unresponsive early in the morning at their home in Turkey. He said he had spoken to Rajab's brother and that the family believed Rajab likely died of a heart attack.

Rajab left Bahrain early in the Iran war, as authorities cracked down on Shia-led protests throughout the Gulf island kingdom, home to the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet. Rajab accused the government of torturing an imprisoned activist and feared he would be arrested if he returned, he told The Associated Press at the time.

Rajab rose to international prominence in 2011, as the Arab Spring uprising swept the region and demonstrations erupted in Bahrain's capital, Manama. He was a pivotal figure in the protest movement, during which the country's majority Shiite population demanded the ruling Sunni monarchy offer them greater political freedoms. As president of the Bahrain Centre for Human Rights, he advocated for expanding the powers of Bahrain's parliament, ensuring freedom of expression and fighting anti-Shia discrimination.
Bahraini authorities, backed by Saudi troops, arrested scores of demonstrators and crushed the protests, while ultimately introducing limited political reforms.

He was imprisoned on multiple occasions in the years following the unrest. His longest stretch behind bars began in June 2016. He was eventually released in June of 2020 during the coronavirus pandemic, though he was ordered to spend the remaining time in home detention.

Rajab had a history of heart issues. During one of his earlier detentions, he received treatment for an irregular heartbeat. He separately received a pardon from King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa in 2015, after concerns emerged about Rajab's health.

Bahraini authorities, backed by Saudi troops, arrested scores of demonstrators and crushed the protests, while ultimately introducing limited political reforms.

articles.title: Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge with drones and missiles as aerial attacks escalate
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Kerch Bridge is a crucial link in moving military and civilian supplies from Russia to Crimea and to support troops on the front line

U krainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), calling it an "unprecedented" operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day.

Mr. Zelenskyy portrayed the operation on the Kerch Bridge as a masterstroke, as Ukrainian forces gradually wore down Russian air defenses for weeks before bombarding the prized target with a barrage of missiles and drones overnight.

Mr. Zelenskyy didn't detail the damage, but the Ukrainian General Staff said an arch and a span of the bridge's road section collapsed, severing the road link, while the railway line was still standing but its arch was damaged.

The Kerch Bridge is a crucial link in moving military and civilian supplies from Russia to Crimea and to support troops on the front line. The construction of the bridge, a potent symbol of Russia's illegal annexation of the peninsula in 2014, was inflammatory for Ukrainians.
"The symbol of the occupation has cracked," the Ukrainian General Staff said in a statement.
Moscow's forces, meanwhile, fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv, hitting two of the Ukrainian capital's main bridges and killing at least two people.

A recent escalation in aerial attacks came as Russia and Ukraine await a date for the next round of U.S.-mediated talks aimed at ending the war that began with Moscow's full-scale invasion of its neighbour on February 24, 2022.

U.S. President Donald Trump says he plans to talk about the war in Ukraine during his highly anticipated meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China this week.
The Kerch Bridge attack was the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, Mr. Zelenskyy said on social media.
Ukrainian forces knocked out defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment and other designated targets before launching Monday night's final attack, he said.

Domestically developed long-range drones struck the bridge's road section during the night while Ukraine's Neptune missiles and other drones aimed at the rail section, he said. Flamingo precision-guided missiles delivered the final blow, he said.
Russia's Investigative Committee said the bridge was attacked by drones and sustained damage. It didn't elaborate.

articles.title: Iran targets Bahrain, slams 'fabricated' dirty-bomb report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Mediator Qatar urged "all parties" to show restraint following an uptick in hostilities, with Bahrain targeted three times in five days after a lull in Iranian attacks on Gulf countries since September

Iran launched a fresh drone attack against Bahrain on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and dismissed a report alleging a dirty-bomb plot against the United States, which President Donald Trump said he took "very seriously".

Mediator Qatar urged "all parties" to show restraint following an uptick in hostilities, with Bahrain targeted three times in five days after a lull in Iranian attacks on Gulf countries since September.

Mr. Trump was speaking after CNN cited seven anonymous U.S. officials as saying Iran was plotting to target senior administration figures with a "dirty" bomb, laced with chemical or radioactive materials.
"If there is [such a threat], they will pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before," Trump said after arriving for a summit in the Philippines.
"I hope it's not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy."
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei dismissed the report as "fabricated".

"Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations" including "the fabricated media narrative surrounding an alleged 'dirty bomb' propagated by CNN", he posted on X.
Mr. Baqaei also criticised a New York Times report questioning whether Iranian dams and water projects had military uses.
Earlier on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), explosions boomed across Bahrain's capital as a mobile-phone alert warned residents to seek safety.

Bahrain's armed forces said they "confronted, intercepted and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today... before they could achieve their objectives", while Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a U.S.-operated radar system.

"Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain," the Guards' Sepah news website said.

The attack was in response to the "repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones", it added. The Guards also said they had intercepted and captured a US drone south of Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Bangladesh connects first nuclear power plant to national grid
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The development comes as the South Asian nation of 170 million people grapples with a fuel crisis triggered by the conflict in West Asia

Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant at Rooppur in the country's northwest Pabna district began supplying electricity to the national grid on a trial basis on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), according to officials.
The 2,400 MW Russian-assisted facility is expected to meet more than 10% of Bangladesh's electricity demand once fully operational, helping the country diversify its energy sources.
“We have become the 33rd country in the world to produce and generate nuclear power,” Science and Technology Minister Fakir Mahbub Anam told reporters at the plant site.
The development comes as the South Asian nation of 170 million people grapples with a fuel crisis triggered by the conflict in West Asia.
The plant comprises two units, each with a generation capacity of 1,200 MW, officials said, adding that the first unit has begun supplying 350 MW of electricity to the national grid.

According to the Science and Technology Ministry, the initial connection would last between eight and 10 hours, during which engineers would conduct tests on the plant's turbine, generator and grid stability.
The unit would subsequently be disconnected for further technical tests and could be reconnected after about 28 hours for another four to six hours to complete additional operational checks.
Under an agreement with the Russian contractor, the first unit will undergo a 10-month trial operation before beginning commercial electricity generation at full capacity, the ministry said.
Construction on the facility began in 2017 during the administration of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, following a 2015 agreement with Moscow.

articles.title: ASEAN, Quad Summit updates on November 17, 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Quad is a ‘trusted partnership’ delivering solutions, says PM Modi

Amid the geopolitical tension, what the world needs today is peace, stability and predictability, Prime Minister Narendra Modi underlined at the ASEAN-India Summit, the East Asia Summit and the Quad Summit in Philippines, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri said.

Mr. Misri, in a briefing, said the Prime Minister has just completed a short but very intense visit to Manila, where he participated in the 23rd India-ASEAN Summit, the 21st East Asia Summit and the 7th Quad Leaders Summit.

At each of the three meetings, the Prime Minister underlined that in a world that has seen a great deal of geopolitical tension, flux and stresses and strains, what the world really needs today is peace, stability and predictability, Mr. Misri said.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi departed for New Delhi after concluding his two-day visit to the Philippines, during which he attended the ASEAN-India Summit, the East Asia Summit and a meeting of the Quad leaders.
Mr. Modi also met Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., and the two leaders discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in defence, security, trade and investment.
The Prime Minister also discussed regional and global issues of mutual interest with his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand on the sidelines of the visit.

Leaders of ‌the four-nation Quad grouping ⁠strongly oppose any destabilising or ‌unilateral actions that seek ‌to ‌change ⁠the status ⁠quo, including by force or coercion, which ‌escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and ‌stability, a joint statement said.
The leaders also ‌expressed grave concerns about economic coercion, including through arbitrary ‌export restrictions, the statement added after their ⁠meeting in Manila.

The Quad grouping, following its meeting in Manila, announced the ‘Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration’ which is “ a new initiative to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness”
“In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer,” the statement added.
In a joint press release following the Quad meeting in Manila, the group said that it “affirms the importance of the AI Accelerator, announced by our Foreign Ministers in Atlanta.”
“The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific,” it added.

articles.title: ‘Record horticultural production’ shows increase of 4.36% from 2024-25: Agriculture Ministry
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Significant increase in horticultural production reflects the hard work of India’s farmers and the impact of the Centre’s farmer-friendly policies, Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan says

India’s total horticultural production is expected to reach 3,869.15 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, an increase of 161.77 lakh tonnes (4.36%) over the production recorded in 2024-25, according to the third advanced estimates of area and production of horticultural crops released by Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan in New Delhi on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). In the previous crop season, horticulture production stood at 3,707.38 lakh tonnes.

Mr. Chouhan expressed satisfaction over the projected growth and said the significant increase in horticultural production reflected the hard work of India’s farmers and the impact of the Union government’s farmer-friendly policies. “This record production would not only strengthen the country’s nutritional security but also directly contribute to higher incomes for horticulture farmers,” the Minister said, congratulating farmers across the country for their efforts.

Farmers were increasingly moving beyond traditional crops towards the cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, and plantation crops, including cashew, coconut and cocoa, as well as aromatic and medicinal plants, he said.

“This growing interest in commercial and high-value crops is opening up new avenues of income for farmers while creating fresh opportunities for self-reliance and growth in the agricultural sector,” Mr. Chouhan said, adding that one of the most significant aspects of the latest estimates was increase in production despite a reduction in the area under horticultural cultivation.

“The total area under horticultural crops in 2025-26 is estimated at approximately 297.21 lakh hectares, compared with 301.36 lakh hectares in 2024-25. Despite the decline in cultivated area, production is projected to increase across fruits, vegetables, flowers, plantation crops, and aromatic and medicinal plants,” Mr. Chouhan said.

Fruit production is estimated to rise from 1,176.49 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 1,230.66 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, an increase of 54.18 lakh tonnes or 4.60%. “The improved output is primarily attributed to better production of banana, mango, papaya, apple, pomegranate and jackfruit,” the Union Agriculture Ministry said in a release.

The area under vegetables is estimated to increase from 117.91 lakh hectares to 119.31 lakh hectares. “Vegetable production is projected to rise by 4.35%, from 2,177.97 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 2,272.68 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. Significant increase in horticultural production reflects the hard work of India’s farmers and the impact of the Centre’s farmer-friendly policies, Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan says

India’s total horticultural production is expected to reach 3,869.15 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, an increase of 161.77 lakh tonnes (4.36%) over the production recorded in 2024-25, according to the third advanced estimates of area and production of horticultural crops released by Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan in New Delhi on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). In the previous crop season, horticulture production stood at 3,707.38 lakh tonnes.

Mr. Chouhan expressed satisfaction over the projected growth and said the significant increase in horticultural production reflected the hard work of India’s farmers and the impact of the Union government’s farmer-friendly policies. “This record production would not only strengthen the country’s nutritional security but also directly contribute to higher incomes for horticulture farmers,” the Minister said, congratulating farmers across the country for their efforts.

Farmers were increasingly moving beyond traditional crops towards the cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, and plantation crops, including cashew, coconut and cocoa, as well as aromatic and medicinal plants, he said.

“This growing interest in commercial and high-value crops is opening up new avenues of income for farmers while creating fresh opportunities for self-reliance and growth in the agricultural sector,” Mr. Chouhan said, adding that one of the most significant aspects of the latest estimates was increase in production despite a reduction in the area under horticultural cultivation.

“The total area under horticultural crops in 2025-26 is estimated at approximately 297.21 lakh hectares, compared with 301.36 lakh hectares in 2024-25. Despite the decline in cultivated area, production is projected to increase across fruits, vegetables, flowers, plantation crops, and aromatic and medicinal plants,” Mr. Chouhan said.

Fruit production is estimated to rise from 1,176.49 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 1,230.66 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, an increase of 54.18 lakh tonnes or 4.60%. “The improved output is primarily attributed to better production of banana, mango, papaya, apple, pomegranate and jackfruit,” the Union Agriculture Ministry said in a release.

articles.title: Hospital in Chennai performs complex aortic surgery on 10-year-old boy with rare vascular disease
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The child recovered and was discharged on the ninth day after surgery

A 10-year-old with a rare inflammatory blood vessel disease underwent surgery at SIMS Hospital, Chennai, to repair a large aneurysm of the aortic arch, the hospital said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The patient was diagnosed with aortoarteritis, also known as Takayasu arteritis, a condition that causes inflammation and narrowing or enlargement of blood vessels. The aneurysm had enlarged significantly, causing breathing difficulty, palpitations, and difficulty lying down. The risk of rupture made urgent surgery necessary. The patient weighed about 18 kg, adding to the technical challenges of the operation. As the aneurysm was located close to the breastbone, opening the chest through the usual approach carried a risk of injuring the enlarged aorta. The surgical team first connected the patient to a heart-lung machine through blood vessels in the groin.

The patient’s body was cooled to 16°C using a technique known as deep hypothermic circulatory arrest. Blood circulation was then temporarily stopped for about 40 minutes, enabling surgeons to remove the affected section of the aorta and replace it with a Dacron graft. Lowering the body temperature reduces metabolic activity and the organs’ oxygen requirements, helping protect them during the period when blood flow is interrupted.

The patient was subsequently rewarmed, restoring his blood circulation. Post-operative assessments showed no damage to the brain, kidneys, intestines, or spinal cord, the hospital said. The patient has resumed normal activities without breathing difficulty but will require continued medication and monitoring to control the underlying inflammation and prevent further aneurysms.

The surgery was performed by a team led by Bashi V. Velayudhan, director and senior consultant, cardiothoracic surgery, along with Mohammed Idhrees, senior consultant, cardiothoracic surgery, and a team of anaesthesiologists and other specialists.

articles.title: Chinese scientist fired after child death in gene-editing trial: state media
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The child who died had a rare neurodevelopmental condition called Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome, according to the report
A Chinese scientist who concealed the death of a six-year-old girl in a gene-editing trial has been sacked following a government probe, according to state media.
The girl died last year after receiving experimental gene therapy to correct a non-life-threatening condition -- which was not disclosed in published research, an investigation found in July.

Neuroscientist Zilong Qiu, the trial's lead researcher, had made no mention of the girl in a paper published in the prestigious journal Nature , according to the joint investigation by Science and Retraction Watch .

Qiu was dismissed as deputy director of the Songjiang Research Institute affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University, state broadcaster CCTV said Friday, citing a statement from Shanghai authorities.
The reported statement included only Qiu's surname, but referenced the Nature study published on February 18.
Qiu was given a five-year suspension from participating in scientific projects and recorded in a database for "serious breaches of research integrity", the report said.
Another researcher on Qiu's team was sacked and handed a five-year suspension, while several others with ties to the hospital where the trial took place were also punished.
The child who died had a rare neurodevelopmental condition called Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome, according to the report.
The hospital's ethics committee had approved a gene-editing trial to treat the disorder in January 2025, the report said.
The committee terminated the study after the girl died in March due to complications from gene therapy.
Shanghai authorities found that Qiu's team failed to properly inform the hospital of possible safety issues from earlier tests on primates, according to the report.
The July investigation by Science and Retraction Watch found that the girl's parents, who paid more than $800,000 to fund the experiment, were not adequately informed about the risks.

articles.title: All-too fallible: On India’s vote against moratorium on death penalty
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Death penalty requires a near-infallible criminal justice system

India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.

Only a small group of countries worldwide are executing more people. In India, per Project 39A, the Supreme Court released 38 persons from death row in 2016-2025 after they had spent eight years there on average. Some have endured more than two decades. The punishment requires a measure of infallibility that the criminal justice system cannot supply. The safeguards neither deter convictions in cases with flawed evidence, false testimony, and so on nor remedy unequal access to competent legal representation among those facing the penalty. India should formally suspend executions and commission a review of penalty statutes and the treatment of prisoners on death row. Second, it should spare offences that do not involve intentional killing from the penalty. Research suggests meting out excessively harsh punishments for non-fatal crimes could incentivise offenders to escalate their violence, including to kill potential witnesses. The greater goal should be to abolish the practice in law while improving investigative and prosecutorial practices and access to legal aid.

articles.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledges ‘mistakes,’ signals interest in return if company chooses
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The statement comes after an online petition to reinstate Huang gathered more than 1,90,000 signatures, including from tech industry figures like SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has signalled his interest in returning to lead the AI computer chip company in his first public statement since he abruptly left the company last week following revelations of an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy .

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he said in a social media post.
He acknowledged making “serious mistakes” in his personal life but said that he’s received an “outpouring” of support from employees, investors, business partners and customers for his return.

articles.title: U.K. sanctions Israeli companies building West Bank settlements
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The long-discussed E1 project would effectively cut off eastern Jerusalem from Palestinian population centres in the occupied West Bank, harming the prospects for a viable independent Palestinian state, Britain says

The UK has sanctioned Israeli construction and property development companies it says are involved in building West Bank settlements, the first concrete step in Britain's previously announced effort to slow the expansion of settlements and preserve the possibility of a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

The sanctions are the first announced since Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Sept. 8 that Britain would toughen its stance toward its longtime ally. His announcement followed Israel's decision to seek bids to build 1,200 homes in the E1 area east of Jerusalem and an increase in settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank.

The long-discussed E1 project would effectively cut off eastern Jerusalem from Palestinian population centres in the occupied West Bank, harming the prospects for a viable independent Palestinian state, Britain says.

“Illegal settlement expansion in the West Bank is destroying the prospects of a two-state solution, so today we are sanctioning companies involved in this activity and disrupting their access to the finance that enables it,” Miliband said in a video posted on X. “And our warning to companies thinking about being part of settlement expansion, including the unconscionable E1 project, is clear: We will clamp down on you.”
Britain has long been one of Israel's staunchest allies. Miliband recently described himself as a “proud British Jew” whose grandmother survived the Holocaust.

But the U.K. government has grown increasingly critical of Israel's government as the war in Gaza has drawn tens of thousands of protesters onto the streets of London and other cities. Earlier this year, Britain joined five other Western countries in imposing additional sanctions on settlers and settlements.

The latest measures target eight property development and construction firms, as well as Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement that has blocked humanitarian aid convoys from entering Gaza, the government said.

The companies are Har Hevron Development Co., Hemdat Shomron, S.A.G. (Velvel) Construction and Development, Lev HaHar Yazamut, Harey Zahav, Ariel Residential Judea & Samaria, Ami Gvirtzman Architects 2021 and Z.F. Building Co.
All eight companies and Tzav 9 are now subject to UK asset freezes, and people associated with them will be barred from serving as directors of UK-based companies.

Announcing Britain's plans Sept. 8, Miliband said Israel had crossed a “long-standing red line” by advancing the E1 project. First proposed in the 1990s, it has been repeatedly delayed by international opposition. Israel's outgoing government, dominated by settler leaders, has begun seeking bids to build several thousand homes.

Miliband said Britain would target companies that facilitate settlement building, block the import of goods produced in the settlements and ban advertising for settlement land. Britain also plans to extend its international human rights regime to “enable swifter action to deter settlement expansion” and place restrictions on some arms exports to Israel, he said.
He said the full legislative package would be in place within six to nine months.

On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Death penalty requires a near-infallible criminal justice system

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.
